attorneys.name: Robert Abrams
attorneys.practice_type: Administrative Law Lawyers in Denver, CO
attorneys.bio:
Robert Abrams is an attorney and trial lawyer practicing Contract Law. His emphasis is Construction, Construction Defect, Breach of Contract, Lease Issues, Real Estate and Land Development Matters.

Mr. Abrams' focus in law is construction disputes, partnership disputes (LLC, general and limited partnerships), construction defect, contractor/subcontractor issues, contractor/homeowner disputes, product warranty, general breach of contract, UCC contract sales, CCPA and other contract related matters involving terms or breach.

What sets Mr. Abrams apart from other lawyers practices in contract and construction matters is his 25 years of business experience in construction, contracting and land development.

Mr. Abrams guides, advises, drafts and prepares his clients by offering competent legal representation in contractual matters.

As a fifteen year durable surfaces subcontractor, contractor and real estate developer, Mr. Abrams has an intimate working knowledge of contract, general construction, construction defect and general construction matters. He has negotiated scores of contracts and sub-contracts with general contractors, tradesmen and other service and product vendors. Moreover, he has developed a profound understanding of the construction industry in general and construction contracts in particular. His knowledge and experience provides enormous benefit to his law clients.

As a land developer building single and multi-family homes, Mr. Abrams brings extensive real estate development experience to his clients. This includes land acquisition, design, architecture, engineering, soils, surveys, financing, marketing, development and sales. During each phase, extensive contract and construction terms are negotiated.

As a twenty year veteran Denver businessman, Mr. Abrams has developed broad expertise in the rights and obligations of the contracting parties; and, the required performance and duties contained therein. He professes the foundation of contract lies with the obligations of the contracting parties and the responsibilities to each other prior to the agreement's formation. This legal foundation provides the meaningful framework for drafting contractual terms and documents. Proper advance legal advice protects the interests of each party, which makes the contract terms more enforceable.

Expert preventative preparation provides the greatest protection in the event of a dispute. It foresees the obligations of the parties and the consequences to each in the event of breach. Proper legal assistance in contract preparation makes the issues more clear should litigation ensue.

As a trial lawyer, Mr. Abrams limits his practice to all types of contract and construction related matters. In the event of litigation, Mr. Abrams combines his years of contract experience and his substantive knowledge of contract law, on his clients' behalf. He successfully negotiates his clients' position to avert litigation.

Mr. Abrams is a rare combination of attorney, litigator, negotiator, businessman and developer. With his experience and background in construction, construction defect, contracting, contractor relations, building and contract law, he provides clients with unparalleled representation.

Wins and Settlements:

• Over $1 million in settlements in 2014.

• Nearly 1,000 Clients Served by the Firm

• 2019, $1 MILLION TRIAL VERDICT IN BUSINESS LAW DISPUTE

• Over 200 Trials and Evidentiary Hearing Court Appearances

• 2016, 26TH LARGEST JURY VERDICT OF ALL LAWSUITS FILED BY ALL LAW FIRMS IN COLORADO

• $3.4 MILLION IN JUDGMENTS, JURY AWARDS AND SETTLEMENTS IN ONE YEAR. CONGRATULATIONS TO THE LAWYERS AT Abrams & Associates, LLC

• OVER $11 MILLION OBTAINED BY JURY VERDICT, JUDGMENT AND SETTLEMENT IN THE LAST 5 YEARS

• OVER 90 PERCENT OF ALL CASES SETTLED

• EXCEPTIONAL CLIENT SATISFACTION

attorneys.name: Alyssa Akre
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Denver, CO
attorneys.bio:
Robinson & Henry Attorney Alyssa Akre is a member of the firm’s Criminal Defense Team. As a former prosecutor, Alyssa has handled hundreds of criminal cases and litigated 45 jury trials, including vehicular homicide, sexual assaults, and other felonies in Arapahoe and Jefferson Counties. Now she uses that experience and insight to defend clients facing felony and misdemeanor crimes.

Alyssa assists clients facing complex criminal charges in various courts, including juvenile, county, and district courts. She is passionate about helping people thrust into an unfamiliar criminal justice system.

Representative matters

Prevented permanent protection order - Vacated temporary protection order and stopped PPO from being issued

Defended against harassment charges - Obtained unsupervised deferred dismissal of harassment charges

Preserved driving privileges - Resolved two traffic infractions to retain teen's driver's license

attorneys.name: Dave Albrechta
attorneys.practice_type: Employment Law Lawyers in Durango, CO
attorneys.bio:
In his first nine years as an attorney, Dave assisted people in the areas of general civil litigation, employment law, and business planning and consulting. Representing hundreds of people in private negotiations and multiple courts and agencies, Dave noticed a pattern. Because our traditional adversarial system focuses only on monetary compensation, clients often leave this process feeling that they did not receive "justice" or that the underlying wrongs are still raw and not healed.

In 2023, Dave began exploring other ways of being a lawyer - of bringing kindness, collaboration, and cooperation to the law. He crafted a blueprint for how he could help clients heal from the traumas they've experienced, instead of fighting for years for a resolution that addresses only financial wholeness. This ultimately led to Dave and Eleni's discovery of the integrative law movement. In 2024, they renamed their firm Aspen Grove Integrative Law.

Dave's goal is to help clients find meaningful resolutions through peaceful means and to avoid the adversarial legal system. He combines legal wisdom with love and compassion to provide balanced assistance through complicated situations.

attorneys.name: Eleni Kennebeck Albrechta
attorneys.practice_type: Probate and estate planning Lawyers in Durango, CO
attorneys.bio:
Eleni works primarily within the areas of probate and estate planning, employment law, and family law. Eleni enjoys assisting clients with organization and preparation of their estate plans. Eleni earned her Juris Doctor with a certificate of concentration in labor and employment law from the University of Toledo College of Law in August 2014 and is a licensed Colorado attorney.

Before moving to Ohio for law school, Eleni was Political and Finance Director of a campaign for Colorado Secretary of State. Prior to that she worked as a teller at Citywide Banks in Denver and interned for a gubernatorial campaign. Eleni earned a Bachelor of Arts degree in 2008 from the University of Colorado at Boulder. She spent a semester studying foreign policy at American University in Washington, D.C. in 2007, and had the opportunity to study international labor law, criminal law, and business in emerging markets in Prague, Czech Republic and Vienna, Austria in 2013.

Eleni is from Denver, Colorado but loves living life with her husband and dog (Cosmo) in Durango, Colorado. Eleni has a passion for wilderness and travel, and she enjoys planting trees, as well as hiking, camping, rafting, snowshoeing, and backpacking. Eleni has served as Treasurer and Trustee of the Christy Farm Nature Preserve.

Eleni is looking forward to helping you with your legal needs in Durango, Colorado.

attorneys.name: Jody Harper Alderman
attorneys.practice_type: Eminent Domain Lawyers in Denver, CO
attorneys.bio:
Highly respected in her field by her peers, Jody Harper Alderman has practiced eminent domain law and real estate law for over three decades. Among her colleagues, Jody is known for her willingness to go above and beyond for a client, oftentimes “giving 150 percent,” her law firm partner, Carrie Bernstein, says. “She truly cares about people, which is why she has represented some clients practically her entire career.”

During law school at the University of Colorado School of Law, it was the takings clause of the U. S. Constitution — from where the power of eminent domain stems — that immediately piqued Jody’s interest. Her University of Colorado Law Review article focused on the Fifth Amendment’s takings clause. Upon graduating from law school, she calls it fortuitous that she found a job at a Denver law firm where she could focus on the area of law that so interested her. Jody worked at Grimshaw & Harring until 2009, when she and Carrie left to start Alderman Bernstein. As a married mother of three, Jody wanted to nurture her professional ambitions while being fully present for her family.

At Alderman Bernstein, Jody’s practice focuses primarily on eminent domain law, and she also does both transactional and litigation work related to real estate. Jody handles contract disputes; quiet title actions and Rule 105 proceedings; Rule 106 appeals of land use decisions; drafting and negotiation of a variety of real estate contracts, leases, easements and other conveyance instruments; and due diligence and closings.

Jody is highly recognized within the legal field. She has been selected to Super Lawyers every year since 2014; she has been designated as one of the Best Lawyers in America for Eminent Domain and Condemnation Law each year since 2007; and she is an AV Preeminent Rated Lawyer by Martindale-Hubbell. In 2022, Jody was named Best Lawyers Lawyer of the Year in Eminent Domain and Condemnation Law in Denver. Jody has co-chaired the CLE International Annual Eminent Domain Conference since 2015, putting together a continuing education program for eminent domain professionals, including lawyers, appraisers and right-of-way professionals.

Jody has litigated numerous eminent domain, inverse condemnation, and takings cases. She represents clients in every stage of a condemnation case, including negotiating for the acquisition of property and commencing condemnation proceedings, immediate possession hearings, valuation trials, and appeals. She represents private landowners, special districts, school districts, counties, municipal governments, and other public entities in her eminent domain practice. Representative clients include property owners involved in acquisitions by the City of Thornton for its waterline project, power companies acquiring utility easements for electric transmission lines and substations in several counties throughout Colorado, numerous special districts in acquiring various rights of way and utility easements for multiple projects. Jody has argued numerous cases to the Colorado Court of Appeals and the Colorado Supreme Court.

Along with her myriad professional accomplishments, Jody is passionate about giving back to her community. She’s on the Board of Advisors for Holy Family High School in Broomfield, Colorado, where she also coaches the Mock Trial Team and teaches a Mock Trial elective class. Since 1999, she’s volunteered with the Tennyson Center for Children, one of the Rocky Mountain region's leading treatment centers and K-12 schools for emotionally and crisis-affected children and youth. Tennyson serves children and families impacted by abuse, neglect and trauma. Jody was on the Board of Directors of Tennyson Center from 2007 to 2014, during which time she served as Chair of the Board for two years, and she returned to the Board from 2016 to 2022, serving as Chair of Board from 2018-2021. “It’s a really wonderful place and they’re doing tremendously important work,” Jody says. Jody is also currently a member of the Development Committee at Women’s Bean Project in Denver.

attorneys.name: Leigh A. Alpert
attorneys.practice_type: Immigration and Nationality Law Lawyers in Boulder, CO
attorneys.bio:
Leigh has practiced immigration law since 2012. She has been selected to the Colorado Rising Stars List from 2018 - 2024, a peer designation awarded to no more than 2.5 percent of attorneys in Colorado. In 2023 and 2024, Leigh was selected by 5280 Magazine as a top lawyer in the field of immigration law in the Denver-metro area. Leigh has experience in a wide range of cases, both family-based and employment-based, immigrant and nonimmigrant matters. Her specialty is in working with persons of extraordinary ability, investors, and religious workers. Leigh also has extensive expertise in H-2B petitions for seasonal companies in the landscaping and concrete industries.

Leigh is a Michigan native and a December 2011 graduate of the University of Michigan Law School. Leigh interned with the Omaha Immigration Court, the Michigan Immigrant Rights Center, the University of Michigan Law School's Human Trafficking Clinic, and the Neighborhood Defender Service of Harlem. She received her Bachelor of Arts degree with high distinction from the University of Michigan where she majored in Political Science and was awarded Phi Beta Kappa.

Leigh has served as a member of the AILA Colorado USCIS Liaison and Legislative Advocacy Committee since 2017. She was the recipient of the AILA Chapter Pro Bono Champion Award in 2016. A successful community organizer, she has managed and facilitated over 15 citizenship workshops on behalf of AILA Colorado. Leigh regularly volunteers at the Colorado Lawyers Committee's Legal Nights. She previously served as the Immigration Committee Chair of the Arapahoe County Bar Association.

Leigh is a member of the American Immigration Lawyers Association (AILA). She is admitted to practice law in Colorado, New York, and the U.S. District Court for the District of Colorado.

Highly proficient in Spanish, she has lived in Guanajuato, Mexico, and taught English at a bilingual high school in Granada, Spain.

attorneys.name: Laura L. Ammarell
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Greenwood Village, CO
attorneys.bio:
When I decided I wanted to pursue a career in law more than 25 years ago, I had no idea how much I would truly enjoy the practice as much as I do. I grew up in Colorado, not far from where our law firm is located just south of Denver in Greenwood Village. I have been a domestic practitioner in Colorado for more than two decades, helping hundreds of individuals seek change and resolution in their personal lives. I am a proud graduate of Colorado State University (Go Rammies!) and a Cum Laude graduate of Gonzaga University School of Law (Go Bulldogs!). I practice family law exclusively, representing clients statewide in their dissolution of marriage cases, allocation of parental responsibilities, support matters, paternity and adoption. I am a child of divorced parents, and I understand the trauma and confusion that comes with being exposed to conflict and uncertainty when you are young. I use my personal and professional perspective built over decades to help my clients navigate what is typically the most difficult journey of their lives. I’ve been there, I understand.

In addition to my private practice, I lecture groups of students, lawyers, paralegals and other professionals on a wide variety of topics from adoptions to effective advocacy in the family law courtroom through the Colorado Bar Association, National Business Institute and the University of Denver’s Sturm College of Law.

I also participate on the Executive Council of the Family Law Section of the Colorado Bar Association (since 2012) as Chair of the Section and Chair of the 2019 and 2020 Annual CBA Family Law Institute. I am a member of the Arapahoe, Denver, Douglas-Elbert and Colorado Bar Associations, and a Fellow of the Colorado Bar Foundation. I am a Past-President of the Douglas-Elbert Bar Association and in 2009 I was presented with the Douglas-Elbert Bar Association Professionalism Award.

Outside of my practice, I enjoy anything outdoors in our beautiful state! That includes camping, boating, hiking, skiing (both snow and water) and taking our pugs for a walk! I enjoy cooking and getting together with my wonderful friends and laughing at what life brings us. I have four beautiful children who motivate me every day to do what I do the very best way I can.

I handle all kinds of domestic matters from child support modification to dissolution of marriage. I also serve as a Court-Appointed Guardian ad Litem in probate matters in Colorado, and I am trained as a Child and Family Investigator and mediator. Along with my partner of over 13 years, we provide private legal representation, mediation, arbitration and other consulting services both together as a team and separately.

attorneys.name: Erica Anderson
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Denver, CO
attorneys.bio:
I am a Colorado Native and was raised in Boulder County. I am a dedicated criminal defense attorney with six years of experience. Upon graduation from law school, I served as a Judicial Law Clerk for two District Court Judges with a criminal docket. The knowledge I gained from this clerkship has assisted me in understanding how Judges receive and evaluate arguments presented in high-level, complex criminal cases.

After my clerkship, I became an attorney at Sawyer Legal Group and assisted hundreds of clients across the state of Colorado with various matters including, but not limited to, pre-charge representation, pre-trial negotiations and litigation, jury trials, bench trials, sentencing hearings, civil protection order hearings, punitive contempt proceedings, deregistration hearings, and sealing hearings.

I took a brief hiatus from Sawyer Legal Group to provide defense services at the Colorado Public Defender's Office. At the Public Defender's Office, I handled a very high volume of criminal cases with charges ranging from low-level petty offenses and traffic infractions to serious felonies.

These experiences have provided me with a well-rounded understanding of courtroom procedure, judicial decision-making, as well as effective defense strategies and advocacy both inside and outside of the courtroom.

In addition to this experience, it is important to me to bring a certain level of compassion to each of my clients. Each client is experiencing one of the most stressful and overwhelming moments in their life and I approach each case with a certain level of respect, empathy, and honesty. I work hard to ensure that each client is heard, informed, and vigorously represented.

Family law appealed to Rachel D. Anderson because she wanted to help people through likely one of the most difficult times in their lives.

"Divorce is hard, especially when children are involved," Ms. Anderson said. "Everyone deserves to have an attorney that understands them and skillfully fights for their rights."

By having compassion and empathy, Ms. Anderson is able to uniquely identify with the state of mind and emotions of her clients.

"That allows me to really see the case from their point of view, which in turn helps me enthusiastically advocate for their interests," Ms. Anderson said.

attorneys.name: Richard M. Arnold
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce Lawyers in Littleton, CO
attorneys.bio:
PERSONAL STATEMENT: Rich has been practicing law in Colorado since 1983. Rich practices primarily in the areas of family law and divorce, construction disputes, estate planning and general civil litigation. Rich is a founding member of Arnold & Arnold, Attorneys at Law, LLP, having merged his practice with the practice of his wife, Jean Arnold, in 1994.

Rich has been in the private practice of law virtually his entire career, with a three and one-half year stint as in-house counsel for a large electrical construction company from 1987 to 1990. Rich began a solo practice in 1990 in Littleton, Colorado. That practice continues today as part of Arnold & Arnold, LLP.

Rich’s approach to the practice of law is to strive to provide responsive personal service to all clients, while balancing the often competing goals of financial success, highly competent legal services, and appropriate community service. Rich particularly enjoys the role of counselor to his clients, giving guidance and advice, as well as the personal satisfaction of successful courtroom advocacy.

Rich’s personal interests include golfing, skiing, hiking, biking, volleyball reading and music. Rich is involved in a variety of community service organizations including Denver Urban Ministries, where he has provided pro bono legal services since 1991, twice earning the volunteer of the year award. Rich also is active in the Africa Partnership of the Rocky Mountain Conference of the United Methodist Church, many local church committees and choirs, and served as a board member for a variety of community and foundation organizations over the last twenty years.

Rich and Jean Arnold have two children. Some of his greatest joys have been sharing the experiences of his children, including marching band, and the camping and high adventure experiences while serving seven years as a Boy Scout Assistant Scoutmaster.

attorneys.name: Gerald D. Arrington
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Colorado Springs, CO
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Gerald D. Arrington, practicing Criminal Defense in Colorado, came to our office after leaving his home state of Virginia, where he served three terms as the elected Commonwealth’s Attorney (D.A.). Gerald is an experienced trial lawyer who has practiced criminal law since 2004.

Gerald is now putting that invaluable experience to work for you as a zealous hard-hitting advocate for your rights. Having won hundreds of cases before judges and juries, Gerald knows what it takes to win— extensive trial experience, tireless dedication, thorough preparation, and open client communication lines.

No matter how serious the crime, Gerald likely has experience handling it, often as both a prosecutor and a criminal defense attorney. He has tried numerous cases involving Murder, Vehicular homicide, Sexual Assault, Drug Distribution, and Firearm Crimes.

Gerald also understands that for many clients, more minor cases such as D.U.I., Domestic Violence, or Simple Drug Possession can have huge impacts on one’s life.

While Gerald loves to try cases in front of judges and juries, he understands the importance of obtaining a favorable result as quickly as possible. Using his extensive negotiating skills, it is his goal to obtain a dismissal or deferred disposition if possible without having to put his clients through the stress of trial.

In 2008, Arrington founded and operated a successful private practice focusing on criminal defense. As a criminal defense attorney, he successfully litigated hundreds of cases in the district, circuit, and appellate courts of Virginia. He held a superb trial record and obtained numerous acquittals, including a sexual assault jury trial.

In 2012, Gerald Arrington was elected as Commonwealth’s Attorney for Buchanan County, Virginia and closed his practice. After serving 3 terms, Gerald began preparations to move his family to Colorado, a state that they have always loved, to join his oldest son who proudly served in the USAF before going to work for the government.

attorneys.firm_name: John Astuno Jr. Attorney at Law
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Denver, CO
attorneys.bio:
Attorney John Astuno Jr. represents individuals in Denver, Colorado, who have suffered personal injury due to the negligence of another. From products liability to medical malpractice, he defends his clients’ right to receive compensation for their medical bills, lost wages, and the pain and suffering they have endured. He also represents the families of victims of wrongful death.

Mr. Astuno received his law degree from the University of Colorado Law School at Boulder and was admitted to the Colorado bar in 1976. He is also licensed to practice before the United States District Court, District of Denver and the United States Court of Appeals for the 10th Circuit.

As an active member of the legal community, Mr. Astuno has served in a number of organizations. He is a member of the Denver Bar Association and American Bar Associations. He also served on the board of governors of the Colorado Bar Association from 1988 to 1990, and is still an active member. He is also a member of the Association of Trial Lawyers in America (also known as the American Association for Justice) as well as the Colorado Trial Lawyers Association.

attorneys.firm_name: Daniel Barron Attorney And Mediation Services, Inc.
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Edwards, CO
attorneys.bio:
Andrew represents clients across Western Colorado through family law challenges, applying his experience as an attorney, empathy, and inclination toward action to achieve results for his clients.

Andrew grew up in Aspen and attended the U.S. Military Academy, commissioning in 2000 in the U.S. Army and serving as a tank platoon leader in the 11th Armored Cavalry Regiment. He later attended the University of Washington School of Law through the Army's Funded Legal Education Program. He finished his twenty-one year military career as a Deputy Legal Counsel to the Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff. His duties included security cooperation, domestic operations, and internal investigations.

After his military service, Andrew was the Senior Counsel for Appropriations, Fiscal, and Audit for AmeriCorps. Andrew advised agency leaders and collaborated with the White House Domestic Policy Council and the Office of Management and Budget to develop and execute AmeriCorps' $1B annual budget, programmatic initiatives, and legislative program.

Andrew is an avid skier, mountain biker, and hiker, and serves his community through several nonprofit, educational, and public service pursuits.

attorneys.name: Franklin D. Azar
attorneys.firm_name: Frank Azar Car & Truck Accident Lawyers - Aurora, Colorado
attorneys.practice_type: Injured Clients Lawyers in Aurora, CO
attorneys.bio:
Franklin D. Azar was born in Pueblo, Colorado. While Frank's father was a district attorney in Trinidad, Colorado, much of Frank Azar's family worked as ranchers on the family's ranch.. So as a young man he learned the value of hard work along-side his family and a dedication to the law from his Father. Frank attended the University of Colorado and went on to study law at the University of Denver. Frank Azar graduated Cum Laude from the University of Colorado in 1979 where he earned his B.A. degree. He was also a member of the Phi Beta Kappa fraternity. Frank Azar then went on to receive his Juris Doctor from the University of Denver in 1982.

Formerly, Frank Azar was an Assistant District Attorney for the Third Judicial District. In 1984 he started his own firm, Franklin D. Azar & Associates, P.C. where has represented thousands of clients. Franklin D. Azar & Associates currently offers representation to injured clients, whether from car accidents, motorcycle accidents, or even slip and fall injuries. The guiding principle for Franklin D. Azar & Associates is that if you have been injured by the negligence or carelessness of another, Frank Azar will help you get full and fair compensation for those injuries, regardless of their origin.

Frank Azar has devoted a significant portion of the practice at Franklin D. Azar & Associates to class action and mass tort lawsuits. These cases cover a wide range of subject matter. Some claims are intended to provide assistance to those whose claims are best served by representing an entire class or people whose injury is relatively minor, but deserves to be resolved, such as unfair compensation or wage discrimination claims. Other cases may involve claims against pharmaceutical or medical device manufacturers whose negligence has caused thousands of injuries throughout the United States.

While the main office of Franklin D. Azar and Associates is located in Aurora Franklin D. Azar & Associates has offices in Colorado Springs, Pueblo, and Trinidad, Colorado, as well as in Albuquerque, New Mexico. Frank Azar has stayed close to Trinidad and sponsors an annual golf tournament to raise money for scholarships at Trinidad State Junior College. Frank Azar is also active in supporting a number of charitable organizations, such as Operation Walk Denver, The Bridge Project, and Bear Creek Junior Sports.

Mr. Azar is admitted to practice before the bars of Colorado, Texas and the United States District Court for the Southern District of Texas. He is also a member of the Colorado, Texas, Minnesota and American Trial Lawyers Associations as well as the Colorado Bar Association.

attorneys.name: Kat F. Baiardi
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Denver, CO
attorneys.bio:
Kat is an Associate Attorney at GEM Family Law, practicing in all areas of family law. Kat has specialized in family law and domestic violence for the entirety of her career, practicing in Arizona before relocating to Colorado. Kat is passionate about assisting families and advocating for her clients and their children.

Kat received her Juris Doctor from the University of Arizona James E. Rogers College of Law, where she also received a certificate in Family and Juvenile Law. Kat was a Graduate Assistant for the B.A. and Master’s in Law Program throughout law school, assisting the master’s level and undergraduate students to grasp legal concepts in civil and criminal procedure and Constitutional law, and grading student assignments and exams in these courses.

During law school, Kat also interned at Southern Arizona Legal Aid, Inc. in their Domestic Relations Unit, gaining practical family law experience in domestic violence and other family law matters. Kat additionally practiced law as a student attorney in the University of Arizona James E. Rogers College of Law’s Domestic Violence Law Clinic. Kat has a keen understanding of domestic violence issues and has worked on systemic change projects to make the legal system more accessible for survivors. As a researcher, Kat has reviewed dozens of orders of protection and used this information for her paper that was published in the Wisconsin Journal of Law Gender and Society (2023). Kat additionally presented at the 2022 VAWA Institute at Colorado’s Annual Judicial Conference in 2022 on domestic violence and credibility discounting. Kat has presented additional seminars on family law issues, domestic violence, domestic violence and its impact on custody, and trauma informed practices.

Kat has served as a Staff Attorney at Southern Arizona Legal Aid, Inc., representing survivors of domestic violence in divorce, custody, and protection order matters. At Legal Aid, she developed a Domestic Violence Law Clinic Pilot Program, creating and teaching seminars on domestic violence and supervising law student attorneys.

Kat received her undergraduate degree from The University of Colorado, Boulder, where she double majored in Psychology and Sociology, with a minor in Women and Gender Studies. During college, Kat interned at a safe shelter for survivors of domestic violence, where she did outreach and violence prevention work.

Kat is licensed to practice law in both Colorado and Arizona.

attorneys.name: Leslee K. Balten
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Litigation Lawyers in Breckenridge, CO
attorneys.bio:
Ms. Balten’s professional background is a diverse combination of civil litigation, family law litigation, and business and real estate transactional matters. Her family law practice focuses primarily on dissolution of marriage actions, post-decree modifications of parental responsibility and child support, and relocation matters. Ms. Balten is also a certified Child and Family Investigator and Parenting Coordinator/Decision Maker. Ms. Balten’s varied background provides her a unique ability to mediate with clients going through divorces with complex business issues and assets, and challenging parenting time matters. Ms. Balten strives to empower clients to find creative and amicable solutions that work for their unique situations and families.

Raised in Michigan, Ms. Balten first moved to Breckenridge, Colorado in 2000 and enjoyed several snow seasons before she headed east to attend Vermont Law School. After completing her J.D., Ms. Balten returned to Colorado to clerk for the Honorable Catherine A. Lemon of the Denver District Court. Ms. Balten then worked in private practice in the Denver metro area until returning to Breckenridge in 2016 where she now manages Ciancio Ciancio Brown, PC’s Breckenridge office. Leslee is a graduate of the 2015 Colorado Bar Association Leadership Training (COBALT), was Region 7 Vice President of the Colorado Bar Association 2019-2020, recognized as a Colorado Super Lawyers Rising Star from 2015 to 2018 and named on the Best Lawyers in America list 2022. During her free time, you can find Leslee enjoying all things outdoors including skiing, river running, biking, and backpacking.

attorneys.name: Aaron W. Barrick
attorneys.practice_type: Complex Civil Litigation Lawyers in Castle Rock, CO
attorneys.bio:
Aaron Barrick has extensive trial experience as lead counsel in over 35 fully litigated jury trials and over 100 administrative hearings. He specializes in complex civil litigation with a focus on commercial litigation, real estate law, land use, and construction law. He also acts as advocate and counselor in insurance, probate, guardianship and conservatorship matters. Prior to joining Folkestad Fazekas Barrick & Patoile, P.C., Mr. Barrick served as a Judge Advocate and Special Assistant U.S. Attorney in the United States Air Force where he gained a unique perspective serving as both defense counsel to high-profile clients before courts-martial in the Pacific Rim and Southeast Asia, and later as managing trial attorney and chief prosecutor of the Air Force's busiest criminal justice office. Mr. Barrick was also selected to defend the Air Force against land-use reclamations, toxic tort claims, wrongful death claims, and employment disputes. He remains associated with the Air Force as senior counsel and adviser to the Colorado Air National Guard. Mr. Barrick was employed as a trial attorney for an insurance defense firm in Denver after leaving active duty and before joining Folkestad Fazekas. He is licensed in Colorado, Nebraska and Iowa.

attorneys.name: Daniel Eben Barron
attorneys.firm_name: Daniel Barron Attorney And Mediation Services, Inc.
attorneys.practice_type: Mediation Lawyers in Edwards, CO
attorneys.bio:
Why practice in the area of domestic relations? I used to ask myself that question often when I first started practicing law because of the high emotional toll that this area of law has on my clients, their families, and myself. However, I began to appreciate the ability to change a very negative experience into a means of helping people move forward with their lives with the least amount of damage, both emotionally and financially. This is my commitment and has become my personal goal in every matter I handle. Simply put, there is no other area of law I would rather practice. Domestic relations law is all encompassing. It gives me the opportunity to work in the areas of family dynamics, financial planning, and many other areas of the law.

Whether acting as an attorney or a mediator, my mission is the timely, cost effective, and fair resolution of issues in order to minimize emotional hardship, legal expenses, the risks involved with a formal court proceeding, and the negative effect that these types of disputes inevitably have on individuals and their families' personal lives.

Through the identification of interests, it is possible to not only reach equitable agreements, but also to create a path that will allow individuals and families the techniques to reach amicable resolution of future issues they face, whether personal or financial. This is especially important when it comes to co-parenting.

Why do I have the confidence to make these bold statements? I have been practicing family law for approximately 32 years. During this time, I have corresponded with professionals in all fields including financial planners, mental health care professionals, business valuators, accountants, and other attorneys. I have completed and participated in numerous courses involving effective negotiation with various levels of conflict over the last 17 years including over 260 hours of seminars and workshops. Furthermore, I have participated in and conducted hundreds of mediations throughout the state of Colorado. These experiences have allowed me to observe the various techniques and their effectiveness in resolving disputes.

My experience as an acting mediator has given me the knowledge and confidence to enable all parties to participate in good faith, even those not believing in the process, and thereby, keeping an open mind toward resolving the various issues they are facing, no matter the complexity and adversarial nature of the disputes. This is especially important in high conflict cases. I am able to act as a facilitator, evaluator, and employ interest based negotiation as necessary and appropriate for the various issues facing the individual.

I have read numerous articles and books on domestic relations issues including parenting plans for children of various ages and needs, cases involving domestic violence, relocation of a parent, grandparent visitation, child support, complex financial matters, estate document interpretation and drafting, and other areas including high conflict divorce. Additionally, I have had the opportunity to thoroughly research, negotiate and litigate other areas of law involved with my own cases and cases in which I have acted as the mediator.

attorneys.name: Lisa E. Battan
attorneys.practice_type: Immigration Lawyers in Boulder, CO
attorneys.bio:
I am a third generation Colorado native. Although I have not strayed far from home, I have a lifelong interest in learning about people from other places and other cultures.

Licensed to practice law in 1994, I work exclusively in the area of immigration law. I am active in the American Immigration Lawyers Association (AILA) and served as Chair of the Colorado Chapter of AILA. I also served on the Board of Governors of AILA, and as a member of the family immigration committee. I am also a Past President of the Colorado Bar Association's Immigration Section.

I feel greatly rewarded by my work in immigration law. I have a tremendous opportunity to meet extraordinary people from all over the world. It is truly rewarding to help people overcome the hurdles of our immigration laws in order to live their lives and fulfill their goals and dreams in the United States. Personal contact with my clients and responding to their individual needs has become the hallmark of my practice.

In addition to my work in immigration law, I have also taught and danced Argentine Tango. I have been fortunate to join my passion for tango with my work. I secure visas for most of the world’s best tango dancers and musicians who come to work in the U.S.

I also practice yoga and meditation, ride and compete my horses in the sport of dressage, listen to music from other countries, walk my dog and try to enjoy special moments with my beautiful daughter and family.

attorneys.name: Danielle C. Beem
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Litigation Lawyers in Denver, CO
attorneys.bio:
Danielle graduated from University of Colorado School of Law in 2012. Since then she has worked with Beem & Isley to advocate and help their clients in some of the worst moments of their lives.

Danielle has volunteered as a CASA (Court Appointed Special Advocate) since 2010 working with children who have been abused or neglected. After the terrible flooding impacted Colorado families in 2013 and 2014 she volunteered with the CBA's Colorado Flood Relief Program to help victims of the flooding in Colorado navigate their legal issues and options and specifically dealing with their insurance companies.

Having been injured in a car accident when she was only 17, Danielle brings a personal perspective to her cases and truly understands the pain, loss, and intangible or often overlooked impact theses injuries have on her client's lives. She takes the time to talk with each client, get to know them, and spend time with them to understand their lives and how they are coping with their injuries, so that she can fully stress the impact to both the insurance adjuster and juries.

When she is not busy advocating for her clients, Danielle enjoys spending time with her family, traveling, making jewelry, and is enjoying being a new mom.

attorneys.name: Matthew E. Bennett
attorneys.firm_name: Frank Azar Car & Truck Accident Lawyers - Aurora, Colorado
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Aurora, CO
attorneys.bio:
"I know firsthand how an auto collision can turn someone's world upside down. I wake up every day honored to fight for real people and to lend my voice to those who need it most."

Matthew E. Bennett joined Franklin D. Azar & Associates, P.C., in September of 2018. A native of Atlanta, Georgia, he moved to Colorado during his high school years and has remained a proud Coloradan ever since. Since joining the Azar team, Mr. Bennett has negotiated several six-figure settlements.

An alumnus of the University of Colorado in Boulder, Mr. Bennett obtained his B.A. in English Literature and Economics in 2010. Following graduation, Matthew worked for multiple Colorado-based healthcare organizations, most notably as an analyst and ambulatory physician trainer for Centura Health. These roles provided Matthew the opportunities to directly interact with fellow Coloradans who had been hurt, many through no fault of their own. These experiences equipped him with the determination to lend a helping hand to those who need it most.

Pursuing a lifelong dream to practice law, Mr. Bennett attended the University of Denver's Sturm College of Law. During law school, Matthew was elected by his peers to serve as a managing editor for the Denver Law Review, the law school's flagship journal. Matthew also had the opportunity to work as a summer law clerk for the Colorado Attorney General's Office. It was during this time that he developed a passion for trial work and civil procedure. He attained his J.D. in May of 2018, having earned multiple merit-based scholarships and numerous Scholastic Excellence Awards for highest achievement along the way, including an award for achieving the highest overall grade in Health Law.

Matthew is admitted to practice in Colorado and is an active member of the Colorado Bar Association and the Colorado Trial Lawyers Association. In his free time, Matt cherishes spending time with his wife and dog, reading historical fiction, exercising, playing sports (particularly basketball), and cheering on the Colorado Buffaloes and Florida Gators.

attorneys.name: Carrie S. Bernstein
attorneys.practice_type: Eminent Domain Lawyers in Denver, CO
attorneys.bio:
For over twenty years, Carrie Bernstein has used her experience and expertise in the areas of eminent domain law and real estate litigation to advocate for her clients. Without excess drama, Carrie has a no-nonsense approach to helping her clients that people appreciate. At Alderman Bernstein, Carrie represents private landowners, quasi-municipal corporations, and public entities in eminent domain in both litigation and appeals. She has been designated as one of the Best Lawyers in America for Eminent Domain and Condemnation Law each year since 2016 and named a Super Lawyers Rising Star in 2013. Carrie has been a presenter at many continuing education programs regarding eminent domain topics. She has litigated numerous eminent domain, inverse condemnation, and takings cases. She represents clients in every stage of a condemnation case, including negotiating for the acquisition of property and commencing condemnation proceedings, immediate possession hearings, valuation trials, and appeals. Carrie has argued several cases to the Colorado Court of Appeals and Colorado Supreme Court.

Her recent representative eminent domain experience includes: representing landowners in CDOT’s widening of I-25 and I-70; representing a special district in many proceedings up to the U.S. Supreme Court regarding the issue of public use; representing landowners in threats of condemnation by RTD for its light rail and commuter rail expansion; representing landowners regarding the City of Arvada’s widening of Ralston Road; representing multiple landowners regarding Northern Water’s easement acquisitions for a water pipeline in Larimer County; representing a special district to acquire utility easements for a new development in the City of Brighton; representing a municipality to acquire easements for a sewer line project and a flood mitigation project; representing a ditch and reservoir company in a threatened condemnation of a reservoir and associated ditches; representing multiple landowners regarding the City of Thornton's water pipeline project in Weld and Larimer counties; representing a landowner in southwestern Colorado in an inverse condemnation case; representing landowners against Xcel in various Xcel infrastructure projects; representing mountain communities in their eminent domain efforts; and representing a landowner in Castle Rock’s new interstate interchange project.

Carrie also has considerable experience in other aspects of real estate and land use disputes, including those concerning title issues, lease and purchase agreements, Rule 106 appeals of land use decisions, quiet title cases, adverse possession, boundary line disputes, and easement disputes. Her recent representative real estate litigation experience includes: representing a large industrial private landowner in Eagle County in an easement ownership dispute with its neighbors in a quiet title case; representing private landowners in access easement disputes in Jefferson County; representing a group of neighbors in Eagle County regarding a Rule 106 appeal of a land use decision; representing a landowner in a Rule 106 case challenging a Town of Vail land use decision; and representing an industrial landowner in a trespass case.

Carrie also has been hired as an expert witness to opine on disputes involving eminent domain and title issues. Recently, her expert opinion about the condemnation process assisted in the settlement of a contract dispute involving the interpretation of the contract’s condemnation clause.

Carrie’s background is varied. After getting her bachelor’s degree in East Asian Studies and International Studies from Northwestern University, Carrie taught English in China for a year before returning to Denver to work in the foreign language translation industry. After five years she craved more intellectual challenge and subsequently enrolled in law school at the University of Denver Sturm College of Law. During her time there, she served on the law review for two years, including on the board of editors. Upon graduation she clerked for Judge Arthur P. Roy at the Colorado Court of Appeals for a year, which gave her invaluable insight into the inner workings of the judicial system and appellate process. She started at the Denver law firm Grimshaw & Harring (now called Spencer Fane) in 2004, where she worked in eminent domain law; civil, commercial and real estate litigation; and water law.

Carrie worked at Grimshaw & Harring until 2009, when she and Jody Alderman left to start Alderman Bernstein. As a married mother of two girls, Carrie wanted to nurture her professional ambitions while being available and fully engaged with her family.

Carrie is a native of Vail, Colorado, and was raised in both Denver and Vail. Her knowledge and familiarity with Colorado’s resort communities has drawn clients from smaller communities around the state to the firm.

Outside of her practice of law, Carrie is involved in her daughters’ schools and activities. During the winter, Carrie coaches her daughter’s recreational ski racing team. When she isn’t working hard for her clients, she enjoys traveling as well as spending time with her family and sharing her love of the mountains with her children.

attorneys.name: Gregory Biggers
attorneys.practice_type: Business & Commercial Lawyers in Fort Collins, CO
attorneys.bio:
Greg’s family hails from the Ozarks of southern Missouri. During his senior year in high school in 1992, Greg enlisted in the United States Army Infantry under the Delayed Entry Program. He was assigned to the 3rd Battalion, 14th Infantry Regiment of the 10th Mountain Division, serving in New York, Panama, and Somalia.

Immediately upon completing his military service, Greg married his high school crush Kathy. They have been happily married since 1995 and have three children – Michael, Maddie, and Danny.

In 1998, Greg graduated summa cum laude from Ball State University in Muncie, Indiana. That same year, Greg began service as a trooper with the Indiana State Police. He has worked and assisted in investigating nearly every type of traffic and criminal case. From this experience, Greg gained invaluable insights into personally serving persons in stressful, sad, and emotionally wrought situations.

While serving with the Indiana State Police, Greg worked his way through Valparaiso University School of Law. He graduated summa cum laude from Valparaiso in 2004. Upon graduation, Greg spent a year at the law firm of Mulliken Weiner Karsh Berg & Jolivet in Colorado Springs, Colorado with a focus on civil litigation.

During the next sixteen years, Greg served the communities of Albany County, Wyoming and Larimer County, Colorado as a deputy district attorney. During that time, Greg had the opportunity to represent the States of Colorado and Wyoming in a myriad of criminal cases ranging from minor traffic offenses and misdemeanor offenses to First Degree Murder.

Greg’s primary passion as a prosecutor was seeking justice for victims of violent crime and their families. He was privileged to serve under District Attorney Clifford Riedel (ret.) as the County Court Division Trial Chief. In this role, Greg had the opportunity to train, mentor, and lead the County Court Trial Division which prosecuted nearly 16,000 traffic and misdemeanor cases each year.

In 2020, Greg accepted an appointment by Sheriff Justin Smith (ret.) to the Larimer County Sheriff’s Office. In that role, Greg served as a legal advisor and trainer to members of the Larimer County Sheriff’s Office and the Larimer County Park Service Rangers.

Greg strongly believes, as written in the United State’s Declaration of Independence, that by the Laws of Nature and of God that all are created equal with certain unalienable rights. As a trooper, district attorney, and deputy legal advisor, he firmly believed that it was his responsibility, acting on behalf of the government, to respect, uphold, and defend the rights of every person as set forth in the Constitutions of the United States, Colorado, and Wyoming.

In 2023, Greg joined his longtime colleagues and friends at Reilly, Vandenberg & Biggers. Greg’s goal is to provide personalized legal services to good people in northern Colorado and southern Wyoming with a commitment to hard work, integrity, tenacity, and common sense. Greg believes that every client that he works with has intrinsic value and unique skills. His mission is to serve his clients and their families by partnering one-on-one with his clients to provide exceptional legal services so that they can spend their time focusing on their daily commitments that are important, valuable, and enjoyable to them.

During his off time, Greg enjoys spending time with his family and friends. You might find him wandering the Poudre and Big Thompson canyons in search of a trout to fool.

14th Infantry Regiment of the 10th Mountain Division

attorneys.name: Ted Bills Esq.
attorneys.firm_name: The Law Firm of Ted Bills
attorneys.practice_type: Car Accident Lawyers in Colorado Springs, CO
attorneys.bio:
For over 20 years, Ted has handled complex civil litigation and traumatic bodily injury accident claims which have consistently resulted in multimillion dollar settlements and judgments for his clients. Ted is an aggressive negotiator and advocate who persists relentlessly until he obtains the settlement or outcome that aligns with what the client wants and with what the case deserves. After this, everything else is okay.

Guided by family values and community ties, Ted began his path to representing injury victims in Chandler, Mesa, and Gilbert in 2018, when his family started spending winters in Arizona and quickly grew attached to the East Valley. He intended to open his Arizona practice at that time, but the pandemic temporarily delayed those plans. With his son now attending college nearby and strong connections throughout the area, Ted is proud to call Arizona home and to serve clients across Chandler, Mesa, and Gilbert with a unique blend of legal skill and medical understanding.

Many attorneys shy away from saying they are trial lawyers because they have fallen into the trap of tort reform and the marketing efforts implored by the insurance industry.

These efforts are made by the insurance industry in order to make trial lawyers look bad and be viewed as the cause of society's problems, such as the rise of insurance rates and frivolous lawsuits. But Attorney Bills proudly represents injured victims and gives them a fighting chance at obtaining compensation.

Ted strongly believes that his job is to be an advocate for injured people. He is fully capable of negotiating excellent and fair settlements out of court, but he is not afraid to fight relentlessly for a just verdict when the case and client require it.

FIRSTHAND MEDICAL EXPERIENCE & KNOWLEDGE OF BODILY INJURIES

Prior to law school, Ted worked at the local city-owned Memorial Hospital, which is now run by the University of Colorado Health. There, he worked in the ER and trauma center assisting doctors and nurses with direct patient care services. He also worked in orthopedics, where he assisted orthopedic surgeons with surgical procedures for broken bones, spinal cord injuries, fractures, total knees surgeries, hip surgeries, and more.

Ted also performed casting, splinting, and traction and worked in physical therapy where he helped people learn to walk again. Basically, whatever the surgeon needed help doing, Ted did.

Because Ted had to transcribe, read, and interpret physician orders, he can read and understand doctor notes and records. This, as you can imagine, is important when representing a personal injury client who has a multitude of bodily injuries. Mr. Bills knows medical terminology, human anatomy, and human physiology, which is a huge advantage when handling personal injury cases in which adequate medical coverage is being withheld or denied.

EDUCATIONAL BACKGROUND

Ted Bills received his undergraduate degree in business from the University of Colorado at Colorado Springs. When he took business law, Ted knew right then that if he got a law degree, he could use his medical background to help injured people in a different way than most other lawyers. In law school, he emphasized his studies in the area of torts and received a special national award for his outstanding performance in the area of tort law. He received his law degree from Washburn University School of Law in Topeka, Kansas, graduating in 2003.

Upon admission to the Colorado Bar, Attorney Bills was hired by a preeminent insurance defense firm that handled mostly trucking litigation defense for insurers of truck drivers in the states of Utah, Colorado, Arizona, and Wyoming. Here, Ted learned all the tricks of the trade regarding what insurance companies do to prevent exposure and lower the amount of money they have to pay an injured person. Because Ted wanted to represent injured parties instead of insurance companies, he opened his own personal injury law firm.

attorneys.name: Sidney Billings
attorneys.practice_type: Landlord Lawyers in Colorado Springs, CO
attorneys.bio:
Robinson & Henry Associate Sidney Billings is a dedicated real estate law attorney specializing in landlord-tenant law and Homeowners Association matters.

Sidney ensures landlords' leases reflect current laws, and she represents them during eviction proceedings or other disputes with tenants. Additionally, Sidney helps clients reach favorable outcomes in HOA and property conflicts. Sidney prides herself in excelling where some lawyers fall short: accessibility and communication. She aims to demystify tangled legal processes so her clients are always on the same page.

Before joining R&H, Sidney honed her courtroom skills as a public defender in El Paso County.

Representative matters

Obtained judgment for landlord - Secured $43,267 judgment plus fees against tenants for methamphetamine contamination of rental property

Protected homeowner's property rights - Homeowner won possession judgment, defeating ex-boyfriend's common law marriage claim

Defended against bankruptcy filing - Secured a judgment of possession despite tenant's numerous frivolous bankruptcy filings

attorneys.name: Clifton Black
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Colorado Springs, CO
attorneys.bio:
Managing Attorney Clifton Black has been practicing law since 2000 and is a founding partner of Black, Blink, & Associates LLC. He is a lifelong resident of Colorado Springs and earned degrees from Pikes Peak Community College (now Pikes Peak State College) and the University of Colorado, Colorado Springs. He received his Juris Doctorate (law degree) from the University of Missouri, Kansas City.

Cliff practices in both Criminal Defense and Business law.

Criminal Defense: Cliff has been practicing criminal defense since the beginning of his career, 2000. Throughout that time, he has handled thousands of criminal defense cases, ranging from misdemeanors to serious felonies, including, but not limited to:

DUI’s,

domestic violence cases,

assault,

theft,

harassment,

burglary,

robbery,

trespassing,

identity theft,

fraud,

sex assault, and

drugs.

Cliff prides himself on working zealously for his clients. By using his years of experience, knowledge of the law, legal research, negotiation skills, and thoroughly knowing the facts of his case, he is able to obtain favorable results for his clients.

Cliff has built one of the top criminal defense firms in Colorado Springs. He focuses on hiring long-term, top notch, criminal law experienced attorneys and staff. The law firm is retained by clients from around the State of Colorado, and the attorneys appear in jurisdictions throughout the state.

Business Law:

Cliff began representing clients with business needs in 2009. He built his reputation advising clients with business needs in highly regulated industries. He quickly became known as a foremost authority in Colorado Springs in different industries.

Cliff represents clients with the following needs:

Business formation advice and counseling,

Preparing and filing Articles of Incorporation for Corporations and Limited Liability Companies,

By-laws and Operating Agreements,

Partnership Agreements and Shareholder Agreements,

Leases,

Licensing

Asset Purchase Agreements,

Company Purchase Agreements,

Promissory Notes

Security Agreements

Deeds of Trust,

Purchase Agreements,

Letters of Intent

Periodic Reports

Being a Registered Agent

Cliff has been appointed to task forces of the City of Colorado Springs by the City Council. He has prepared proposed ordinances and worked with the City Attorney’s Office in drafting ordinances, rules and regulations. These task forces discuss potential additional regulations for regulated industries. Cliff’s opinion has been sought out by the local news channels and has sat on numerous panels discussing emerging industries.

Cliff has represented many clients in buying and selling businesses, or all the business assets. He has assisted clients with companies that are worth less than a hundred thousand dollars to companies that are multimillion dollar companies. When issues arise in these transactions, Cliff is known to come up with creative solutions to get the deals done.

Many attorneys throughout the state contact Cliff for his opinion and seek answers for highly regulated industries.

attorneys.name: Peter Blink
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Colorado Springs, CO
attorneys.bio:
Managing Attorney Peter Blink is an Iowa native and Colorado enthusiast. As a zealous litigator, Peter has over 12 years practicing as an attorney with the District Attorney’s Office in Colorado, and County Attorney Offices in Iowa. Peter’s unique insight as a former prosecutor means he knows how to negotiate favorable plea deals and achieve success at trial. Peter has litigated criminal matters ranging from protection orders violations, domestic violence charges, sex assaults, DUI/DWAI, theft, trespassing, revocation of probation cases, narcotics, firearms offenses, to murder.

As an experienced negotiator, Peter prides himself on his ability to negotiate with District Attorneys to gain the best possible outcomes for his clients. Through zealous negotiations, motions hearings, and pretrial conferences, he supports his clients in obtaining the best possible position while resolving their cases. However, sometimes negotiations fail and as a veteran trial attorney, Peter isn’t afraid of defending his client’s rights in court.

Peter and his family fell in love with Colorado and moved here in 2022. When not spending time with his family, Peter enjoys spending time being outdoors, woodworking, and rooting for the Green Bay Packers.

attorneys.name: Richard H Bloch
attorneys.firm_name: The Law Firm of Richard Bloch, P.C.
attorneys.practice_type: Felony Lawyers in Denver, CO
attorneys.bio:
Hello. My name is Richard Bloch. Thank you for taking the time to view my firm's web page. Let me start by telling you about my pre-law life. I grew up in New York City. I graduated from a Waldorf High School and then received my BA from Cornell University. Before law school I was a New York cab driver, a restaurant manager and for a period of time I worked as a butcher in my father's butcher stores. I graduated from the University of Denver Law School in 1986 and immediately went to work for the Arapahoe County District Attorneys Office. I remained with that office until opening my own practice in 2004.

As a District Attorney I spent six years working on nothing but Habitual Criminal Cases. I became a Chief Deputy in 1999 and from then until I left the office worked on nothing but murder cases. In my years as a District Attorney I trained many of the current District Attorneys, judges and police officers in Constitutional Law, Habitual Criminal Law and Trial Practice.

My law practice consists of mainly private clients but I also accept a limited number of Court Appointments. I do this because I believe that everyone deserves to receive the best legal representation available, even if they are in custody and indigent. Since many of these case involve the most serious types of crimes such as Murder, Aggravated Robbery, Aggravated Assault, Sexual Assault, Kidnapping, Child Abuse, Sex Assault on a Child, Felony Menacing, Methamphetamine Manufacturing and Escape, my Court appointments keep me involved in complex criminal law litigation and they also give me the opportunity to try many more jury trials then most other private attorney's have the chance to do.

While I have predominantly a felony defense practice, I also represent many people charged with DUI, misdemeanor and traffic cases. My experience working major felony cases ensures that my clients facing less serious charges get the same type of legal representation that a person facing life in prison would receive.

Many lawyers advertise themselves as aggressive. Many lawyers will inflate the extent of their experience and their successes. Many lawyers want you to believe that being aggressive, confrontational, angry, and over confident are positive traits. THEY ARE NOT. These behaviors will hurt you and often hide a lack of experience. There are three stages of every case. The plea bargaining stage: the trial stage; and, if necessary, the sentencing stage. I have the respect of most of the states district attorneys and judges. I have the experience to know when you are being treated fairly and when you are not being treated fairly.

Having worked on thousands of cases I can give you sound advice as to whether to risk going to trial or whether to accept a plea bargain. I can often achieve very positive results without the risk of trial. I am also an extremely experienced trial lawyer. I have had hundreds of jury trials. If a jury trial is the right thing to do, you will see a different side of my personality: passionate, aggressive, intelligent and persuasive. But I am not driven by the need to feed my ego. I am driven by my need to make sure that my clients are treated fairly. Some of my clients are innocent. Literally all of my clients are good people who made bad choices at some point in their lives. I CARE ABOUT YOU AND I WILL FIGHT FOR YOUR RIGHT TO BE TREATED FAIRLY.

My law practice consists of mainly private clients but I also accept a limited number of Court Appointments. I do this because I believe that everyone deserves to receive the best legal representation available, even if they are in custody and indigent. Since many of these case involve the most serious types of crimes such as Murder, Aggravated Robbery, Aggravated Assault, Sexual Assault, Kidnapping, Child Abuse, Sex Assault on a Child, Felony Menacing, Methamphetamine Manufacturing and Escape, my Court appointments keep me involved in complex criminal law litigation and they also give me the opportunity to try many more jury trials then most other private attorney's have the chance to do.

While I have predominantly a felony defense practice, I also represent many people charged with DUI, misdemeanor and traffic cases. My experience working major felony cases ensures that my clients facing less serious charges get the same type of legal representation that a person facing life in prison would receive.

Many lawyers advertise themselves as aggressive. Many lawyers will inflate the extent of their experience and their successes. Many lawyers want you to believe that being aggressive, confrontational, angry, and over confident are positive traits. THEY ARE NOT. These behaviors will hurt you and often hide a lack of experience. There are three stages of every case. The plea bargaining stage: the trial stage; and, if necessary, the sentencing stage. I have the respect of most of the states district attorneys and judges. I have the experience to know when you are being treated fairly and when you are not being treated fairly.

Having worked on thousands of cases I can give you sound advice as to whether to risk going to trial or whether to accept a plea bargain. I can often achieve very positive results without the risk of trial. I am also an extremely experienced trial lawyer. I have had hundreds of jury trials. If a jury trial is the right thing to do, you will see a different side of my personality: passionate, aggressive, intelligent and persuasive. But I am not driven by the need to feed my ego. I am driven by my need to make sure that my clients are treated fairly. Some of my clients are innocent. Literally all of my clients are good people who made bad choices at some point in their lives. I CARE ABOUT YOU AND I WILL FIGHT FOR YOUR RIGHT TO BE TREATED FAIRLY.

attorneys.name: Elizabeth Bonanno
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Denver, CO
attorneys.bio:
Elizabeth Bonanno is a Partner at GEM Family Law, and is named one of ten Best Divorce Lawyers in Denver by Forbes for both 2024 and 2025. Elizabeth practices exclusively in family law, having served hundreds of clients during her tenure with their divorces, parenting, and child support cases. Elizabeth's family law practice has focused on asset and business valuation, income valuation, complex divorce, parental responsibilities, child relocation, and child support matters, among others. Elizabeth speaks both Spanish and Italian and uses these skills to assist non-native speakers in navigating through domestic matters.

Elizabeth's outstanding legal work and professionalism has been recognized by her selection as a 2017-2025 Colorado Super Lawyers® "Rising Star", her inclusion in The Best Lawyers In America© 2021-2025 for both Family Law and Family Law Arbitration, by the judicial officers of Arapahoe County, who invited her to serve on their Best Practices Committee, and by Law Week Colorado, who named her as one of only seven "Up and Coming Lawyers" for 2015. She was also a finalist for the Gary McPherson outstanding young lawyer of the year award from the Colorado Bar Association in 2016.

Elizabeth graduated from the University of Colorado Law School with Honors in Juvenile and Family Law. Elizabeth practiced family law for seven years at Griffiths Law PC, and was a partner at the firm from January, 2017 through July, 2019, joining the GEM family on August 1, 2019. She received additional family law experience as a law clerk to Judge Norman D. Haglund on the domestic docket in Denver District Court.

Elizabeth trained in trial advocacy under Colorado Supreme Court Justice Nancy Rice (Ret.) and displays confidence and poise in the courtroom, having run many hearings and trials - Elizabeth is one of the foremost family law litigators. However, she is also a firm believer in mediation and alternative dispute resolution, assisting clients in settling matters before they reach the courthouse. Elizabeth is trained in Collaborative Law, whereby parties commit to resolving their dissolution of marriage cooperatively and without the court's involvement.

Along with her law practice, Elizabeth has authored articles for publications and has presented at seminars on family law topics. She is a member of several professional organizations, including Past President of the Metro Denver Interdisciplinary Committee, an organization committed to the improvement of family law via the intersection of the mental health and legal fields, the Denver Bar Association, the Colorado Bar Association, the Colorado Judicial Institute and the James E. Doyle American Inn of Court, and is a member of the Arapahoe County Best Practices Committee, an invite-only group of judicial officers, clerks and attorneys focused on improving family law in Arapahoe County.

Jonathan Booker is a Shareholder, and Director of Criminal Law at Hernandez & Associates P.C., where he focuses his practice exclusively in the field of criminal defense. Jonathan is an accomplished trial attorney, winning a substantial number of not guilty verdicts while assisting hundreds of individuals as they navigate our complex judicial system. Jonathan represents his clients with the highest degree of professionalism, guided by obtaining the most favorable individual results possible.

Jonathan's education, personal, and professional experiences continue to motivate him as a trial attorney. Jonathan represents individuals facing charges of driving under the influence, violent crimes, drug offenses, sexual assault, and murder throughout the state of Colorado. attorneys.name: Amanda A. Bradley
attorneys.practice_type: Eminent Domain Lawyers in Denver, CO
attorneys.bio:
Amanda Bradley is a real estate litigation and transactional attorney with more than 20 years of experience advising clients in real property transactions, negotiating and preparing real estate contracts and related documents, and representing clients in all phases of real estate litigation.

She has represented clients in eminent domain actions involving various municipal and county governments, special districts and urban renewal authorities throughout Colorado, including negotiation of possession, appraisal review, possession hearings, valuation litigation, and appeals. Amanda also has considerable experience in other aspects of real estate dealings and land use disputes, including those concerning title issues, boundary disputes, lease and purchase agreements, and other complex contractual disputes.

Her representative experience includes: representing electric associations in acquiring property for transmission lines and related facilities; representing private property owners in opposition of attempted condemnation and regulatory takings; representing counties and municipalities in connection with numerous roadway improvement projects; representing metropolitan and other special districts in connection with acquisitions for infrastructure improvements representing a landowner in trial court and appellate proceedings to oppose an attempted private condemnation to serve future development; providing legal counsel for various matters pertaining to the relocation of a medical campus in Denver, including the condemnation of reversionary interests and the negotiation of agreements to facilitate the property's sale and ultimate redevelopment; and representing a developer in a multi-million dollar refinancing transaction and acquisition of real property for construction of a mental health facility, including negotiating and drafting construction documents, counsel regarding necessary governmental approvals, and clearing title to the subject property.

Outside of practicing law, Amanda is actively involved in her children’s school, is a dedicated volunteer for Project 1.27, a non-profit focused on providing support and training for foster and adoptive parents, and enjoys fly fishing whenever she can.

attorneys.name: Tracy L. Brooks
attorneys.practice_type: Elder Law Lawyers in Denver, CO
attorneys.bio:
Tracy joined Chayet & Danzo in 2021 as a law clerk. Ms. Brooks was admitted to the Colorado Bar in October 2022. She works in the areas of estate planning and elder law. Her interest in elder law began when she took Marco D. Chayet and Tamara E. Trujillo's class in elder law during her second year of law school. The same year, Tracy served as a student attorney at the University of Colorado's Juvenile and Family Law Clinic. As a student attorney, she served as Guardian ad Litem (GAL) in Dependency and Neglect cases and represented clients in a variety of other family law matters.

During law school, Tracy participated in several public interest programs. She served as Co-President, then President of Colorado Law's If/When/How Chapter, and participated on the board of CU Law's Juvenile and Family Law Club. Additionally, she interned with an immigration non-profit to help refugee and asylee clients navigate the United States' complex visa system.

Tracy is passionate about family-related legal matters, particularly those that impact some of the most vulnerable populations, including minors, individuals with disabilities, and the elderly. Recognizing the importance of family-however you choose to define it-Tracy's affection for elder law grew from her understanding that each case represents a unique set of personalities, legal issues, challenges, and goals.

When she's not working, Tracy enjoys snowboarding, traveling, spending time with her weird dog,and connecting with friends and family.

attorneys.name: Natalie Brown
attorneys.firm_name: Frank Azar Car & Truck Accident Lawyers - Aurora, Colorado
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Aurora, CO
attorneys.bio:
"First, Last and Always, A Proud Mom"

Top-Rated Personal Injury Attorney in Denver, CO

Natalie Brown, born and raised in Butte, Montana, is a Personal Injury attorney. Natalie graduated with honors from the University of Montana in 1982 and obtained her J.D. in 1986 from the University of Denver. In 1986 she was admitted to practice in Colorado federal and state courts.

Natalie joined the Colorado Trial Lawyers Association in 1986. As a member of CTLA, her peers elected her to leadership positions including the Board of Directors (1999-2005), Treasurer (2005-2006), Secretary (2006-2007;) Vice President (2007-2008); President-Elect (2008-2009) and President (2009-2010).

In 2004, The American Board of Trial Advocates elected her to membership. Membership in ABOTA is by invitation only and membership is granted to those lawyers who display skill, civility, and integrity in the practice of law.

In 2007, the American College of Trial Lawyers inducted Natalie as a Fellow of the College. . The American College of Trial Lawyers is an invitation only fellowship of exceptional trial lawyers from the United States and Canada. The College thoroughly investigates each nominee for admission and selects only those who have demonstrated the very highest standards of trial advocacy, ethical conduct, integrity, professionalism, and collegiality. The American College of Trial Lawyers inducts less than 1% of lawyers nation-wide.

Many organizations and publications recognize Natalie's trial skills and her dedication to her clients. In 2010, Law Week Colorado honored Natalie as Editor's Choice for Best Trial Lawyer in Colorado. In 2012, Best Lawyers in America named her Plaintiff's medical malpractice Lawyer of the Year for Colorado. Best Lawyers in America recognizes her skills every year and has done so since 2005. Colorado Super Lawyers named her Super Lawyer from 2006 to the present. Her Super Lawyer honors include Top 100 lawyers in Colorado and Top 50 Women Lawyers. In 2001 the Colorado Trial Lawyers Association presented her with its Case of the Year award for Preston v. Dupont, 35 P.2d 433 (Colo.2001).

Natalie volunteers as a faculty member at the National Institute for Trial Advocacy and speaks at CTLA and CBA Seminars and Conventions. When away from the office, Natalie is a volunteer coach for high school mock trial teams. She enjoys gardening and spending time with her husband and two dogs.
