Joe has resolved a significant number of complicated and high conflict marital dissolution and child custody cases since joining the firm with thorough preparation, knowledge of substantive and procedural law, and strong negotiation and trial skills. His strategic and tailored approach to each individual case results in successful outcomes for clients often dealing with difficult circumstances. Joe also has background in finance and this experience assists clients with navigating, valuing, and equitably dividing complex and significant marital estates to include direct involvement with the engagement and effective use of expert witnesses. Prior to joining Ammarell Deasy, LLP, Joe worked at two prominent law firms in Colorado and Vermont, and as a solo practitioner in Colorado for several years with significant experience in all aspects of Family Law, Business and Commercial Law, and selected Personal Injury and Criminal Defense matters. Joe is creative and skilled with the factual development of cases, investigation, discovery, legal procedure, legal research, legal writing, trial, and appellate advocacy. Joe's present dynamic Family Law practice involves cases from client intake through the trial of contested issues, including the preparation and Filing of Petition for Dissolution, Service of Petition, Responsive Pleadings, Motion Practice, 16.2 Financial Disclosures, Temporary Orders, Allocation of Parental Responsibilities, Child Support, Spousal Maintenance, Business Valuation, Discovery, Depositions, Preparation and Examination of Lay and Expert Witnesses, Child and Family Investigation, Parental Responsibilities Evaluation, Enforcement of Orders, Punitive Contempt, Remedial Contempt, Mediation, Arbitration, Evidence, Permanent Orders, Trial Practice, and Appellate Practice. Joe earned his Bachelor of Science degree from the Leeds School of Business at the University of Colorado, Boulder in 1993 with areas of emphasis in Finance and International Business. In 2000, he earned his Juris Doctorate, Cum Laude, from Suffolk University Law School in Boston. He is licensed to practice law in Colorado State and Federal Courts, Massachusetts, New York, and Vermont. He is a member of the Colorado Bar Association, CBA Family Law Section, CBA Litigation Section, and the Arapahoe County Bar Association. Joe has good things to say about the firm: "I enjoy our multi-disciplined approach to complex Family Law litigation and the team-first environment employed at Ammarell Deasy, LLP on behalf of clients seeking clarity and direction in the most difficult of legal circumstances. My practical life and family experiences over many years are helpful in advising and advocating for clients in difficult and high conflict situations." Joe believes in the phrase "best interests of the children" and does not just present it as legal doctrine. He has a desire to help individual clients with challenging circumstances, and his intellectual curiosity is piqued by the highly variable legal and evidentiary issues presented in Family Law cases. He has a knack for creating a clear picture of each case for the Court one detail at a time. Joe presently resides in the South Metro Denver area with his wife, daughter, son, dog, and cat. In addition to balancing his family and work obligations, Joe tries to remain active in and around the Rocky Mountain West. Outside of the practice of law, he enjoys running, hiking, swimming, sports, weather, leisure reading, travel, alpine and Nordic recreation, the CU Buffs, listening to and playing music on guitar, and spending time with his family in Colorado, California, and New England. He is an aging distance runner and endurance athlete, having competed in several marathons and triathlons through the years. Joe and his wife presently focus much of their free time guiding and supporting their own two children in their individual journeys toward adulthood. Joe was born and raised in Rhode Island and maintains a very strong connection to his roots in Southern New England. Prior to moving to Colorado from New England several years ago, he served as an Assistant District Attorney in Massachusetts, where he successfully prosecuted both simple and complex criminal cases at the grand jury, trial, and appellate levels. He also assisted and advised law enforcement agencies with complex, time-sensitive search warrant applications and the execution of police searches to ensure the preservation of evidence necessary for important criminal investigations and prosecutions. While there, he also briefed and argued an issue of first impression in Fourth Amendment Search and Seizure, Commonwealth v. Dora, 57 Mass. App. Ct. 141 (2003), which became a published opinion of the Massachusetts Appeals Court. Prior to becoming an attorney, he worked for several years as an accountant and financial professional at a property and casualty insurance company in Boston. Joe now brings his significant prior experience and know-how to Family Law cases involving high conflict and complex financial evidence.

attorneys.name: Reid DeChant
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Denver, CO
attorneys.bio:
Reid is a dedicated legal professional with a unique journey in the realm of criminal justice. Born and raised in the city of Scottsdale, Arizona, he kick-started his academic journey by earning a Bachelor’s degree in Criminal Justice from Arizona State University.

Venturing further into the world of law, Reid relocated to Denver, Colorado, where he pursued his passion for legal expertise at the University of Denver. It was during his time in law school that he began to refine his trial advocacy skills, a journey that led him to become a distinguished member of the National Trial Team.

Mr. DeChant’s commitment to client-focused representation and trial advocacy continued to grow during his tenure at the Colorado Public Defender’s Office, where he passionately defended the rights of the accused. He firmly believes in taking any case to trial when a favorable resolution seems unattainable, and his dedication extends to regularly attending trial advocacy trainings across the nation to ensure he possesses the most effective tools for his clients.

Recognizing that clients often approach him during some of the most challenging moments in their lives, Mr. DeChant prioritizes transparency and honesty. He refrains from making promises he cannot keep and instead offers unvarnished truths. When you consult with Mr. DeChant, expect an honest assessment of your situation, empowering you to make informed decisions about your case.

His overarching mission is to explore every conceivable avenue to secure the best possible outcome for each client, regardless of the circumstances. Mr. DeChant’s track record speaks for itself, with successful negotiations that span the legal spectrum. When you entrust your case to Mr. DeChant, you are gaining an unwavering advocate dedicated to safeguarding your rights and achieving the best possible resolution.

attorneys.name: MariaJose Delgado
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Denver, CO
attorneys.bio:
MariaJose Delgado received her bachelor’s degree from the University of Virginia in religious studies. She later engaged in post-baccalaureate study in Rome, Italy, with a focus on interreligious dialogue.

MariaJose discovered her passion for family law in 2008 and has made conflict resolution among families the focus of her legal career ever since. She was a Beasley Scholar at Temple University Beasley School of Law in Philadelphia, PA, and her participation in the school’s family law legal clinics and other volunteer work earned her the Rubin Public Interest Award.

She is an active member of the Family Law Section of the Colorado Bar Association. She has served on Colorado’s Child Support Commission which reviews child support laws and makes recommendations to Colorado’s legislature. She has been recognized by National Advocates Top 40 Under 40 and by Super Lawyers as a Rising Star.

As a mediator, MariaJose brings to the table a solution-oriented mindset and significant experience as an attorney practicing all aspects of family law. She always has ideas.

attorneys.name: Tahli Delgado
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Colorado Springs, CO
attorneys.bio:
Tahli attended the University of Colorado, earning degrees in both Finance and International Business. She earned her law degree from the University of Denver, Sturm College of Law, with an emphasis in Human Rights Law. While at DU Law, she participated as a mediator on the mediation team, as a litigation advocate in mock trials, as well as an editor for the Denver Journal of International Law and Policy.

Tahli began her career as an intern for the Honorable Judge Laurie Clark at the Lindsey Flanigan Juvenile Court, where she assisted with paternity and adoption cases, in addition to truancy and dependency and neglect concerns. She has continued advocacy efforts on behalf of children through her work with unaccompanied minor refugees, as well as legislative endeavors directed towards juvenile criminal justice reforms. Children's issues remain near and dear to Tahli's heart, and she practices with the Child's Best Interests in mind at all times.

Understanding that life doesn't always proceed how we might wish or plan, and that family defines each of us in many ways, Tahli found her place in family law. She has navigated divorce and custody issues of her own, and therefore has a unique perspective of clients' needs and wishes during these difficult times. She can empathize with her clients' fears and worries, and this awareness is reflected in her thoughtful representation, providing integrity, compassion, and formidable advocacy.

Notably, Tahli recognizes that while attorneys may be busy with many cases, her clients each have only one case, and yet that one case is the most important one of all. Therefore, she realizes that clients are much more than case numbers, but that there is a meaningful story behind each name, and Tahli provides the attention and respect that every single client deserves, as if each were her only client.

Tahli has two beautiful daughters, whose kindness and happiness lights up her life. She enjoys cooking, crafting, and hiking with her dog Bam Bam.

Tahli is a member of the Colorado Bar Association and the El Paso County Bar Association. She has volunteered at Metro Volunteer Lawyers' Family Law Court Program, provided pro bono services in asylum cases, as well as offered legal advice at El Paso County's Family Law Days.

attorneys.name: Ezekiel Denison JD
attorneys.practice_type: Aviation Lawyers in Northglenn, CO
attorneys.bio:
Hello! My name is Ezekiel Denison, and I am an aviation attorney at Ramos Law. I consider an attorney's role in society to be one of ethical stewardship. Whether it be an airman in need of assistance with medical certification, or an individual generally looking for support, my goal is to help alleviate the suffering. I joined Ramos Law in January 2023 because I believe in the firm's values and approach. The entire organization deeply cares about helping others.

I grew up in Laramie, Wyoming and attended the University of Wyoming. There I earned undergraduate degrees with honors in Psychology and Economics. I later graduated magna cum laude from Gonzaga University's School of Law in Spokane, Washington. After law school, I practiced at a general law firm in my hometown where I gained experience in both criminal and civil law. Regardless of the subject, I learned that truly equitable results require sincerely listening to the client, diligent research, coherent explanations (both verbal and written), and ethical decision-making. This diverse educational and legal background helps me meet each pilot where they are and provide them with the quality service they deserve. Flying is not just a passion, it is an identity, and I pride myself on helping pilots get back to doing what they love.

When I'm not working, I enjoy playing basketball, hiking, traveling, listening to music, and checking out new restaurants. My wife and I have two dogs and love going on new adventures. I'm also working on obtaining my private pilot's license. I am passionate about experiencing the present moment, spending time with my family, and continuing to learn.

Ramos Law is always here to help. If there is anything you need, please do not hesitate to reach out.

attorneys.firm_name: The Law Offices of Susan Deschler
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Denver, CO
attorneys.bio:
My name is Susan Deschler. My main practice areas are Criminal and Traffic Law.

I graduated from the University of WI-Parkside in 1994 and The John Marshall Law School in Chicago, IL, in 2001. I graduated in the top 25% of my law school class and was selected to be an Editor on The John Marshall Law School Journal of Computer and Information Law. The Comment I drafted was chosen for publication.

After law school, I was a member of Adjunct Faculty at UW-Parkside, teaching Legal Research & Writing to undergraduate students. I was also elected to serve as a Kenosha County Board Supervisor.

The majority of my practice in WI was as a solo practitioner, in the area of criminal and family law. I also was appointed to serve as a Court Commissioner in the 6th and 7th Judicial Districts.

I moved to Colorado the Spring of 2015. Prior to returning to private practice, I served as the Deputy District Attorney for County Court in Clear Creek County. I have been a licensed attorney for over 22 years and look forward to assisting each client with their legal situation. I am respectful and dedicated to being the best advocate for every client.

I have 4 adult children--Derek, Ashley, Collin, and Kyle.

attorneys.name: Adam Detsky JD
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Northglenn, CO
attorneys.bio:
Adam is an experienced trial attorney admitted to practice law in Colorado and New York. He has practiced in state and federal courts across the country. His civil litigation practice includes handling of a wide range of personal injury claims including motor vehicle accidents, premises liability, product liability, FELA, bad faith claims, and coverage disputes. He has handled all aspects of personal injury litigation from inception of the claim through appeal representing both plaintiffs and defendants.

Before joining Ramos Law, Adam spent over four years representing injured victims. Prior to that, Adam defended a national railroad against toxic torts claims stemming from long-term workplace exposure to various carcinogens.

In addition to his legal practice, Adam dedicates significant energy towards volunteer activities. Adam serves as a member of the board of directors for the American Mock Trial Association ("AMTA") - an academic non-profit that organizes undergraduate mock trial for over 350 colleges and universities each year. Adam also serves as a member of the board of directors for the Mockingbird Foundation - a non-profit that writes competitive grants to youth music education services programs across the country. Adam also has a passion for teaching, having spent a decade as an adjunct professor of trial advocacy at a university in New York.

Adam received his bachelor's degree in criminal justice from the University of Maryland, College Park. He obtained his Juris Doctor from Syracuse University College of Law. After obtaining his law degree, Adam practiced at an Am Law 200 firm for over a decade in New York before moving to be closer with his family here in Colorado. In his spare time, Adam enjoys live music and spending time with his wife and son.

attorneys.name: Sean Dingle
attorneys.firm_name: The Law Office of Sean R. Dingle, LLC
attorneys.practice_type: Medical License Defense Lawyers in Denver, CO
attorneys.bio:
After graduating from California Western Law School, Sean served as a Deputy District Attorney in the DA's Office for Colorado's 10th Judicial District. During his ten years as a Deputy District Attorney, he tried over 150 jury trials and prosecuted a wide variety of criminal offenses. He specialized in prosecuting major crimes, including complex gang and domestic violence-related homicides. He also developed one of Colorado's first dedicated welfare fraud prosecution programs. As a result, the Colorado Welfare Fraud Council honored him - in 1996 - with their Prosecutor of the Year Award.

In 2001, Sean became an Assistant Attorney General with the Colorado State Attorney General's Office. As counsel for the Colorado State Board of Medical Examiners, he prosecuted complex medical professional disciplinary matters before Colorado's Office of Administrative Courts. He was also instrumental in administrative rule-making and policy implementation procedures for the Board of Medical Examiners.

In 2003, Sean entered private practice by joining the law firm of Cooper & Clough, P.C., where he specialized in defending physicians and lawyers in legal malpractice actions. On a number of occasions, he tried - with great success - several complex multi-million dollar birth-injury and wrongful-death cases. He also defended - again, with great success - doctors and lawyers in medical and legal professional disciplinary and licensure matters before both the Colorado State Board of Medical Examiners and the Colorado Supreme Court's Office of Attorney Regulation Counsel.

In 2006, Sean moved to the law firm of Dickinson, Prud'Homme, Adams & Ingram, LLP, where he specialized in defending medical, nursing, and hospital malpractice actions. His clients included Longmont United Hospital and all seven of the HCA-Health-One Medical and Surgical Centers in the Denver Metro Are, including Rose Medical Center, Presbyterian/St. Lukes Medical Center, Swedish Medical Center and Sky Ridge Medical Center. He continued his success - both inside and outside of the courtroom - by defending a number of high-profile, multi-million dollar medical and nursing negligence cases. He also defended, successfully, medical and nursing professionals in disciplinary and licensure matters before the Colorado State Board of Medical Examiners and the Colorado State Board of Nursing.

Sean has extensive trial experience and a proven record of success both inside and outside of the courtroom. By combining a strategic and effective approach to litigation with personalized and detailed attention, he not only provides his clients with practical solutions to their immediate legal issues, but he also helps them prevent future challenges and litigation.

Awards and Honors

Honors

Prosecutor of the Year Award, Colorado Welfare Fraud Council, 1996 - 2016

attorneys.name: Joseph Ditlow
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce Lawyers in Colorado Springs, CO
attorneys.bio:
A native Coloradan, Joseph (Jad) was born and raised in Boulder where he attended Fairview High School. In 2001, he graduated from the United States Air Force Academy with a Bachelor of Science degree in History. Jad started his Air Force career at Vance Air Force Base in Enid, Oklahoma. While there, he attended flight school and found himself working in the Judge Advocate Office as a Legal Assistance Clerk. He immediately fell in love with the law.

In 2003, Jad moved to the Boston, Massachusetts to work for the Air Force as a Systems Program Manager. He also started law school at the New England School of Law (NESL). During his second year at NESL, Jad was transferred to Milwaukee, Wisconsin to work as an Operations Commander for Air Force Recruiting. He also transferred to Marquette School of Law where he interned for the Wisconsin Supreme Court and was inducted into Alpha Sigma Nu (Jesuit Honor Society). In May 2009, Jad was admitted to practice law in Wisconsin. In November 2009, Joseph was admitted to the Colorado bar.

In February 2010, Jad transferred to the Air Force Reserves and simultaneously became a Deputy District Attorney for the 9th Judicial District Attorney’s Office in Glenwood Springs, Colorado. Jad went into private practice in 2012 where he engaged in family law, criminal defense, dependency and neglect defense, and municipal prosecution. He has practiced, primarily, family lawyer in Colorado Springs, CO since 2012 and has developed a passion for the practice.

Jad is active in El Paso County’s legal community. He is on the Community Justice Center’s board of directors, a mentor attorney for Teen Court, and regularly assists clients at local clinics. Jad loves the outdoors; and, in his free time, is frequently found with his family on the many hiking and ski trails Colorado has to offer.

As a Lieutenant Colonel in the Air Force Reserves, Jad is keenly aware of the interplay between family law and the military. Jad further understands the effects that divorce and parenting time issues have on service members and their families, both while serving and after.

As a child of divorce, Jad believes that his personal and professional experiences aid him in relating to clients. Joseph is very aware that the effects of divorce are prevalent long after the formal ending of a marriage. He will make it a point to keep his clients focused on their children and how their actions today will impact their future.

attorneys.name: Gary L. Doehling
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Grand Junction, CO
attorneys.bio:
After defending insurance companies in personal injury litigation for 25 years, attorney Gary Doehling formed the Gary Doehling Personal Injury Law Firm, P.C. to help injury victims prosecute claims against insurance companies. Gary Doehling grew up in Los Alamos, New Mexico. He graduated Magna Cum Laude from Arizona State University College of Business in 1979, and received his Juris Doctor from Arizona State University College of Law in 1982. He moved to Grand Junction, Colorado after graduating from law school and he has been a trial attorney in Western Colorado and Eastern Utah ever since.

Over the last 25 years, Mr. Doehling has represented numerous insurance carriers including Allstate Insurance, American International Insurance Group, American Family Insurance, American States Insurance, Colorado Farm Bureau Mutual Insurance Company, Commercial Union Insurance Company, Farmers Insurance Group, Hartford Insurance Group, National Farmers Union Insurance Company, Trinity Universal Insurance Company, USAA, and USF&G. Mr. Doehling is now putting this experience to work for the residents of Western Colorado and Eastern Utah.

Victims of accidents need professional and competent assistance. Lives have been turned upside down. Gary and his team have the knowledge to help you through this stressful and challenging time. At Doehling Law, our client's interests come first. We thoroughly explore all available insurance and avenues of recovery in order to maximize recovery for accident victims. If you are confronted by an unreasonable adversary, we will provide you with effective representation to seek justice in the courtroom. Mr. Doehling is not a stranger to the courtroom. He is an experienced and successful trial attorney who can effectively represent you through trial and appeal. He has successfully represented clients in court and jury trials in Alamosa, Aspen, Craig, Delta, Denver, Durango, Eagle, Grand Junction, Glenwood Springs, Gunnison, Grand Junction, Moab, Montrose, Pagosa Springs, Price, Salt Lake City, Steamboat Springs and Telluride. You can rest assured of not being outgunned by the insurance companies you oppose.

attorneys.name: Marco Donatelli
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Northglenn, CO
attorneys.bio:
Hi, my name is Marco Donatelli, I am an attorney at Ramos Law. Simply put - I help people through difficult situations. That's what I've always done, and now I help people to navigate our legal system. I was taught to care deeply and fight for what's right - and that's what we do every day here at Ramos Law. I am proud to be a part of such a passionate and dedicated team.

I was born and raised in Long Island, New York. I grew up hiking in the Adirondack Mountains, sailing around Long Island Sound, and helping my father in his own small law firm. My wonderful parents were pillars of our community. They instilled in me the importance of community involvement and a strong work ethic.

After receiving my undergraduate degree in political sciences and economics from the University of Geneseo, I worked as a paralegal for a boutique firm in New York City. This solidified my interest in the law, but I wanted to dive deeper. I went to Brooklyn Law School where I graduated cum laude and specialized in areas such as constitutional law and international law. There I also served as an editor for the Brooklyn Journal of International Law and on the executive board of several honors societies.

During law school, I worked as a Judicial Extern at the New York Appellate Division, 1st Department, where I researched and drafted court opinions and memoranda of law. This gave me a unique "behind the bench" view into the inner workings of judicial chambers which informs my practice every day. I also worked at several litigation firms around Manhattan, learning the craft of Real Estate Development, Insurance Litigation, Personal Injury, Mass Tort Litigation, and more. I then worked for the King's County (Brooklyn) District Attorney's Office, where I prosecuted misdemeanor cases and offenses. Through these experiences, I have gained a broad base of knowledge, but my goal has remained the same - serving my community.

When I'm not in the office, I enjoy playing blues guitar, home winemaking, exercising, and anything outdoors.

I am always here to help. If there is anything that my team can do, we will. Please do not hesitate to reach out.

attorneys.name: Nathan Dowell
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Denver, CO
attorneys.bio:
Nathan Dowell is a family law attorney with more than 25 years of legal experience. Throughout his career, Nathan has focused his practice on family law, representing clients in a wide range of matters in courts throughout the Denver metropolitan area.

Nathan has extensive experience handling complex and highly contested family law cases, including parenting disputes involving issues such as substance abuse, domestic violence, and child abuse. He also represents clients in cases involving complex financial estates, including businesses, trusts, mineral interests, and high-income households. At the same time, Nathan takes pride in guiding clients through less contentious matters, helping families navigate the legal process with clarity and confidence.

Nathan understands that family law cases often come at deeply emotional and uncertain times in a person’s life. Drawing on decades of experience, he works closely with clients to understand their goals, develop thoughtful legal strategies, and guide them through the legal process while protecting both their financial interests and their family relationships.

Clients value Nathan’s ability to connect with them during difficult circumstances and his calm, steady approach to resolving complex legal challenges. His combination of legal knowledge, practical experience, and problem-solving skills allows him to effectively advocate for clients while helping them move forward into the next chapter of their lives.

Nathan has represented clients not only at the trial court level but also in the Colorado Court of Appeals and the Colorado Supreme Court. In addition to his legal practice, he has authored and contributed to publications on family law topics and has presented at continuing legal education seminars, including presentations on the intersection of family law and immigration law.

attorneys.name: John Loren Eckelberry
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce Lawyers in Denver, CO
attorneys.bio:
John Eckelberry is the founding member of Eckelberry Law Firm, established in 2006 in Denver, Colorado. He is in charge of the firm's family law practice as well as bankruptcy matters, including a focus in bankruptcy litigation when divorce issues exist.

During his almost 20 years of practice, Mr. Eckelberry has provided dedicated representation to clients throughout the Denver metropolitan area, helping them to make personal and financial fresh starts. Mr. Eckelberry is a strong supporter of alternative representation models and thus provides both limited scope representation and a sliding scale hourly rate to provide options for clients who don't want traditional representation.

Frequently called upon to speak at legal seminars and conferences, Mr. Eckelberry has contributed his insight and background to numerous publications as well, and served as editor of the 2006, 2011, 2014, and 2016 editions of the Domestic Relations Bench Book published by the Colorado Bar Association. In recognition of his successful record and ethical standards, Martindale-Hubbell has awarded him its AV-Preeminent* rating.

An active participant in numerous professional and community organizations, Mr. Eckelberry is a member of the Colorado Bar Association, where he is a Former Chair for the executive counsel of its Family Law Section, and is also a member of the Arapahoe, Jefferson and Denver County bar associations. He is a former board member for Metro Volunteer Lawyers, an organization that provides pro bono legal services to low-income residents in the Denver area.

*AV-Preeminent and BV-Distinguished are certification marks of Reed Elsevier Properties Inc., used in accordance with the Martindale-Hubbell certification procedures, standards and policies. Martindale-Hubbell is the facilitator of a peer review rating process. Ratings reflect the confidential opinions of members of the Bar and the judiciary. Martindale-Hubbell ratings fall into two categories – legal ability and general ethical standards.

Eckelberry Law Firm, is a debt relief agency. The firm helps people file for bankruptcy relief under the U.S. Bankruptcy Code.

attorneys.name: Max L. Eckstein
attorneys.practice_type: Business Law Lawyers in Denver, CO
attorneys.bio:
Max L. Eckstein is the Chief Operating Officer with Ciancio Ciancio Brown, P.C. (CCB). Responsible for handling the overall day-to-day operations of the firm, collaborating with the Managing Shareholder and Shareholders to further develop and realize the firm’s vision and overall strategic plan. Max continues to build upon an already great firm culture, obtaining and retaining the best clients, and other growth initiatives for the firm.

Max is also a veteran business developer with years of experience helping business owners, professionals, and clients find their own success stories and build relationships. He is skilled at helping owners drive value, develop, and execute growth strategies, and successfully close transactions with the highest value.

Prior to his position at CCB he was a Vice President and Director of Business Development at The Forbes M+A Group, a Director of Business Development at RSM (formerly McGladrey LLP), where he was responsible for understanding client needs and bringing together the right combination of resources to achieve their goals. He also honed his business and legal skills working for the law firms of Donelson Ciancio & Grant, P.C. and the Joffe Law Firm.

Max graduated with a J.D. from University of Dayton School of Law and served as a Director at the University of Denver Sturm College of Law. He has a bachelor’s degree in business management and marketing from Central College in Pella, Iowa where he also was a quarterback. Concurrently, Max studied business at the University of London and political science at the University of Havana.

He is a former board member with the Denver Advisory Board (DAB), a C-suite business group comprised of owners and community leaders. Max also served as a board member of Legal Marketing Association – Southwest Chapter where he previously acted as Board President. He has been a guest lecturer at the University of Colorado School of Law and the University of Denver Sturm College of Law.

Max firmly believes in giving back to the community. With a small group of motivated individuals, The Mile High Country Q & Brew was founded on the principle that together they could make a significant impact on the lives of children by raising awareness and money for Tennyson Center. To date they have raised over $1.5M benefiting abused and neglected kids at Tennyson Center for Children. Furthermore, he has volunteered his time working with Junior Achievement, Adams County Public Schools, and the Denver Advisory Board.

In his limited free time, you will likely find him outside… skiing in winter, mountaineering, running, or on a bike in summer. He also enjoys family time with his wife, daughter, and twin boys when not traveling with his Australian Rules Football teammates on the Denver Bulldogs.

attorneys.name: David W. Edgar
attorneys.practice_type: Complex Commercial Litigation Lawyers in Denver, CO
attorneys.bio:
David W. Edgar is one of the founding partners of Edgar Law Firm. He, along with John M. Edgar and John F. Edgar, started the firm in 2002 in order to provide the legal solutions for clients' business problems, especially when it comes to high-stakes and complex litigation. He practices in the areas of complex commercial litigation (including business torts, fraud, franchisee-franchisor disputes, trade secret litigation), environmental litigation, toxic tort litigation, antitrust litigation, class and derivative actions, securities litigation, construction litigation, labor and employment litigation, and property litigation.

David was born and raised in the Kansas City area. He honed his litigation skills early in his career in plaintiff and defense work for individuals and companies of all sizes as an attorney with Bryan Cave (currently more than 1,275 lawyers internationally). David is a graduate of Gerry Spence's Trial Lawyer's College in Dubois, Wyoming.

David and his wife, Andrea, and their three children, Shannon, David Jr. and Aisling, live in Evergreen, Colorado. Outside of his work on behalf of clients, David enjoys devoting time to family and church, reading and writing fiction, fly fishing, playing guitar and banjo, and working to preserve the environment in the Midwest and Rocky Mountain West.

Recent Representative Cases

Ethanex Energy, Inc. v. McGuireWoods, LLP. David and the Edgar team represented the bankruptcy trustee of a development-stage renewable energy company, Ethanex Energy, Inc., engaged in the development of ethanol production facilities. Defendant McGuireWoods, LLP, is a Richmond, Virginia, based major law firm with offices in the United States and Europe. Ethanex engaged McGuireWoods to accomplish an equity financing and reverse merger, known as a PIPE (private investment in public equity) transaction. Unbeknownst to Ethanex, McGuireWoods partner Louis Zehil, was utilizing his position to perpetrate a scheme to fraudulently trade in restricted securities. Zehil subsequently pled guilty to criminal charges and was sentenced to the federal penal system. The Edgar team filed suit against McGuireWoods, with causes of action including fraud, tortious interference with business expectancies, legal malpractice, negligent supervision and breach of fiduciary duty. As a result of McGuireWoods’ misconduct, Ethanex alleged that it was unable to carry out its business plan, resulting in bankruptcy, the loss of its business expectancies and the destruction of its business endeavors. Edgar Law Firm negotiated a $6,700,000 settlement for its client.

Fitzgeralds and City of Sugar Creek, Missouri v. Station Casinos. David and the Edgar team represented a gaming company and a municipality in the Kansas City area, bringing suit against the successful applicant for license to operate a riverboat casino in Jackson County. The suit alleged various theories, including tortious interference with the business expectancy, fraudulent concealment and fraud by silence. A settlement was reached, as Station Casinos reported in its public filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission, and Station Casinos paid our clients $38 million.

Jury v. Squire Sanders & Dempsey LLP. David and the Edgar team successfully represented the redevelopers of Kansas City's historic President Hotel in a six-week jury trial against a Cleveland-based law firm, Squire Sanders & Dempsey LLP. Edgar Law Firm negotiated a $43 million settlement for their client.

Gil Egle is an attorney with over thirty years experience in the practice of law. He is admitted to practice in Colorado and Wyoming. Gil earned his law degree from the University of Wyoming in 1983. After completing law school he moved to Denver, Colorado, where he began practicing law, first in the securities field, then in commercial litigation and ultimately developing a broad and varied business, commercial litigation and construction law practice. Gil is a member of the Denver and Colorado Bar Associations, and the Wyoming Bar Association.

Gil is a frequent speaker on construction topics to contractors and other construction professionals and for a number of years taught classes to contractors on many aspects of construction contracts. Currently, Gil is the co-author and editor of a Colorado continuing legal education publication entitled, “Colorado Liens and Claims Handbook.” He is also the author for the Colorado section of the internet publication, Lien Law Online, which can be found at www.lienlawonline.com.

Gil actively represents clients in a wide range of business, litigation and construction matters. His construction practice includes representation of owners, general contractors, subcontractors and suppliers in contract drafting and negotiations, mechanic's liens and verified claims, bond claims, arbitration, and litigation involving contract claims and construction issues. Gil may be reached at 303-296-4440 or gil@preeosilv.com.

attorneys.practice_type: Collections Lawyers in Littleton, CO
attorneys.bio: PERSONAL STATEMENT: A graduate of the University of Denver, Terry Ehrlich majored in Political Science and Economics and received a Bachelor of Arts degree in 1980. She continued her education at the University of Denver and received a law degree in 1983. She was admitted to the Colorado Bar on October 31, 1983. She began her practice of law with a small law firm in Wheat Ridge, which practiced a wide variety of law, from domestic to criminal law. She took a leave of absence for 7 years to raise three children and began the practice of law again in 1994 with Arnold & Arnold, LLP. She became a partner in Arnold & Arnold in 2002. She now practices in the areas of collections, civil litigation, domestic, employment law and general commercial law. Terry believes that each of her clients deserves her time, attention, and best efforts. She works to meet the goals and objectives of her clients, without compromising her personal and professional ethics. She has been active in pro bono activities, volunteering for Metro Volunteer Lawyers, Denver Urban Ministries and Peacemaker Ministries.

attorneys.name: Kenneth F. Eichner
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Denver, CO
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Kenneth F. Eichner, principal at The Eichner Law Firm, has vast criminal law experience to help reduce the impact a criminal charge has on his clients' lives. With more than 25 years of criminal law experience and over 140 jury trials, Mr. Eichner guides his clients to their best resolution, whether it is trial or a plea agreement.

Located in Denver, Colorado, The Eichner Law Firm represents clients with all of their criminal law needs. As a former prosecutor, Mr. Eichner has succeeded in acquiring dismissals, acquittals, or reduced sentences for clients facing a wide range of criminal charges, including assault, domestic violence, sexual assault, drug crimes, and white collar crimes, such as fraud and securities violations.

Mr. Eichner was listed in the Top 100 Trial Lawyers in Colorado in 2012 by the National Trial Lawyers and Avvo has given him its highest rating. He has been published by The Washington Post, The Huffington Post, and The Colorado Lawyer. He has also been featured on Denver's 9 News, and he has been a guest lecturer at Georgetown University Law School and the University of Denver School of Law.

During 2018 Ken represented a witness during Supreme Court Justice Kavanuagh’s congressional nomination hearing and subsequent FBI interview process. In 2017, he successfully blocked indictments relating to the Clinton email investigation and obtained dismissals of sexual assault charges against four individuals. These accomplishments led to Ken's nomination for the Denver Bar Association’s Award of Merit, which recognizes attorneys for outstanding contributions and services rendered in the administration of justice.

Mr. Eichner graduated from Antioch School of Law in 1984, where he was an editor of the Law Review, and is licensed to practice in Colorado, Maryland, and Washington, D.C., in both state and federal courts

attorneys.name: Timothy J. Eirich
attorneys.practice_type: Child Welfare Lawyers in Lakewood, CO
attorneys.bio:
Timothy J. Eirich is an honors graduate of the Loyola University of Chicago School of Law. At Loyola, Tim was as a Philip H. Corboy Fellow (member of the National Trial Team), a Curt N. Rodin Fellow in advocacy, and a Civitas Childlaw Fellow. Tim was also an associate editor for the Children's Legal Rights Journal. Tim received his undergraduate degree from Santa Clara University where he majored in English and was a captain of the NCAA Division 1 Crew Team.

Tim focuses his practice on adoption, family formation, child welfare, and guardianship/custody cases. Tim represents prospective adoptive parents, foster parents, relatives, birth parents and serves as general counsel for numerous licensed adoption agencies in Colorado. Tim's practice includes infant and toddler adoptions, designated adoptions, interstate adoptions, stepparent adoptions, same sex adoptions, second parent adoptions, relative adoptions, disrupted adoptions, foster-parent adoptions, international adoptions, confirmatory adoptions and adoption subsidies. Tim also represents intended parents and other individuals in all aspects of family formation.

Tim is an experienced litigator who has tried over twenty-five jury trials, litigated dozens of contested hearings, and has argued in the front of both the Colorado Supreme Court and Court of Appeals. Tim litigated the ground-breaking case, both at the trial level and before the Colorado Supreme Court, that addressed the rights of foster parents and other caregivers in dependency and neglect cases. Tim has also received a number of awards recognizing his work. In 2012, Tim received the Excellence in Practice Award for a Juvenile Law Attorney at the Colorado Summit for Childen Youth and Families. In 2014, the Colorado State Foster Parent Association honored Tim with the Champion Award for work and efforts on behalf of Colorado’s foster parents. Also, in 2014, the Congressional Coalition on Adoption Institute awarded Tim the prestigious Angels in Adoption Award for his work in adoption and positive child welfare practices. In 2023, Tim was honored by the Arapahoe County Bar Association with the Raymond Frenchmore Award for Outstanding Contribution to Juvenile Justice by the Arapahoe County Bar Association.

Tim has handled hundreds of private, public, and contested adoptions and has been recognized as a Fellow with the Academy of Adoption and Assisted Reproduction Attorneys. Tim has also testified in front of the Colorado General Assembly on issues involving child welfare, adoption, and children and family issues and has contributed to the drafting of significant legislation involving adoption and child welfare.

Tim has lectured frequently, in both Colorado and across the nation, on the rights of relatives, foster parents, and caregivers inthe child welfare system, as well as complex issues in adoption and family formation. In addition to training and presenting on substantive issues involving adoption and child welfare, Tim has taught trial skills to fellow attorneys in Colorado and across the country as an instructor for the National Institute of Trial Advocacy (NITA).

Prior to joining the Grob & Eirich, LLC, Tim was the Deputy Director of the Rocky Mountain Children's Law Center where he litigated some of the center's highest profile cases; represented foster parents, prospective adoptive parents, relative caregivers and juveniles; and supervised a multi-disciplinary staff of attorneys and social workers who served as guardians ad litem for abused and neglected children in Denver Juvenile Court. Prior to his time with the Children's Law Center, Tim was a trial attorney with the Office of the Colorado Public Defender where he represented adults and juveniles charged with felony offenses.

Honors

Angels in Adoption Award, Congressional Coalition on Adoption Institute, 2014

Champion Award, Colorado State Foster Parent Association, 2014

Raymond Frenchman Award for Outstanding Contribution to Juvenile Justice, Arapahoe County Bar Association

Unsung Hero Award, Academy of Adoption and Assisted Reproduction Attorneys

attorneys.name: Ashley G. Emerson
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Denver, CO
attorneys.bio:
Ashley advocates for outcomes that enable families to make the smoothest possible transition during an otherwise stressful time of life. She is committed to seeking peaceful resolutions while also zealously advocating for her clients. Whether clients are going through a divorce, custody dispute, financial disputes, or any other family law matter, it is Ashley's goal that her clients feel as though their issue has been resolved with dignity.

While not all cases can be resolved outside of the courtroom, Ashley is an advocate for alternative methods of resolving disputes, when possible. Ashley feels that alternatives to litigation, including mediation, arbitration, and collaborative law, provide great options for clients who desire a less adversarial and more timely resolution of their dispute.

However, when circumstances necessitate traditional litigation, Ashley is the strong and dedicated advocate that her clients need and excels in the courtroom.

Ashley's practice is focused exclusively on Family Law. Having practiced for a number of years at one of Denver's preeminent family law firms, her experience has enabled her to successfully resolve and litigate a wide variety of family law cases.

Ashley has substantial experience representing Fathers, Mothers, grandparents, stepparents, psychological parents, members of traditional families, and members of nontraditional families in divorces, child custody matters, dependency and neglect cases, post decree and modification or emergency cases.

It is Ashley's firm belief and experience that Colorado law is and should be interpreted as gender-neutral and that Colorado's laws regarding individual and family finances and parenting arrangements allow the court to consider the circumstances of each family and make decisions that reflect each person's, family's and child's unique needs and interests.

Ashley's experience with family finances ranges from cases involving complex financial matters, including business interests, defined benefit plans, premarital agreements, trusts and high net-worth estates and individuals, to less convoluted issues, such as child support, the division of modest marital estates, and modification or enforcement of financial court orders.

With respect to parenting time matters, Ashley's experience ranges from complicated cases, such as those involving non-traditional families, domestic violence, infant parenting plans, grandparent visitation and high conflict parents, to those involving families who simply need to memorialize an agreed upon parenting schedule. Due to her work with a number of child-focused non-profits, she has a deep understanding and appreciation for the impact that divorce and custody disputes can have on every member of your family.

Ashley enjoys working with a variety of clients and tailors her services to the needs of each individual.

In her free time, Ashley enjoys traveling to adventurous locations, hiking, running, skiing, and cooking. She loves to share in these experiences with her husband and two rescue dogs.

While not all cases can be resolved outside of the courtroom, Ashley is an advocate for alternative methods of resolving disputes, when possible. Ashley feels that alternatives to litigation, including mediation, arbitration, and collaborative law, provide great options for clients who desire a less adversarial and more timely resolution of their dispute.

However, when circumstances necessitate traditional litigation, Ashley is the strong and dedicated advocate that her clients need and excels in the courtroom.

Ashley's practice is focused exclusively on Family Law. Having practiced for a number of years at one of Denver's preeminent family law firms, her experience has enabled her to successfully resolve and litigate a wide variety of family law cases.

Ashley has substantial experience representing Fathers, Mothers, grandparents, stepparents, psychological parents, members of traditional families, and members of nontraditional families in divorces, child custody matters, dependency and neglect cases, post decree and modification or emergency cases.

It is Ashley's firm belief and experience that Colorado law is and should be interpreted as gender-neutral and that Colorado's laws regarding individual and family finances and parenting arrangements allow the court to consider the circumstances of each family and make decisions that reflect each person's, family's and child's unique needs and interests.

Ashley's experience with family finances ranges from cases involving complex financial matters, including business interests, defined benefit plans, premarital agreements, trusts and high net-worth estates and individuals, to less convoluted issues, such as child support, the division of modest marital estates, and modification or enforcement of financial court orders.

With respect to parenting time matters, Ashley's experience ranges from complicated cases, such as those involving non-traditional families, domestic violence, infant parenting plans, grandparent visitation and high conflict parents, to those involving families who simply need to memorialize an agreed upon parenting schedule. Due to her work with a number of child-focused non-profits, she has a deep understanding and appreciation for the impact that divorce and custody disputes can have on every member of your family.

Ashley enjoys working with a variety of clients and tailors her services to the needs of each individual.

In her free time, Ashley enjoys traveling to adventurous locations, hiking, running, skiing, and cooking. She loves to share in these experiences with her husband and two rescue dogs.

attorneys.bio:

Her civil cases included protection order cases, landlord/tenant cases, and other civil disputes. As a magistrate, Care presided over primarily traffic and misdemeanor cases but also rotated as a domestic relations magistrate. As a district attorney, Care prosecuted misdemeanor offenses, juvenile petitions and felony cases.

Care's practice includes both criminal and family law cases. She handles DUIs and misdemeanor, juvenile and felony cases. In domestic relations cases (divorce) Care handles cases from the initial filing to any post-decree matters.

Care received her J.D. degree from the University of Georgia School of Law. She received her B.A. in sociology from Miami University of Ohio.

Care has lived in Boulder for thirty years. She and her family like to run, ski, hike and cycle. Care and her daughter both volunteer for a local charity organization.

attorneys.name: Marisol L. Escalante
attorneys.practice_type: Immigration Lawyers in Parker, CO
attorneys.bio:
Marisol L. Escalante began her legal career as a bilingual intern investigator who interviewed defendants prior to their bail arraignments at the Essex County Public Defender's Office, Central Judicial Processing Court, in Newark, New Jersey. From 1994-1998, Ms. Escalante worked as a legal assistant for a reputable personal injury law firm in Hoboken, New Jersey. She assisted in cases involving the Federal Longshore and Harbor Workers' Compensation Act, New Jersey Workers' Compensation, and Social Security Disability. Ms. Escalante ultimately became a law clerk for the firm's liability department from 1998-2000.

While in law school, Ms. Escalante was accepted into the prestigious Summer Honors Intern Program for the New York City Law Department, Medical Malpractice Unit. In 2001, Ms. Escalante went on to become an Assistant Corporation Counsel (ACC) within the Law Department's Torts Division. Ms. Escalante handled matters involving city agencies including the Department of Transportation, Board of Education, and New York City Police Department. As an ACC, Ms. Escalante handled depositions on a weekly basis as well as a heavy load of pre-trial motion work. Assigned to Part 20 of the New York State Kings County Supreme Court, Ms. Escalante regularly appeared before the Honorable James W. Hutcherson for pre-trial conferences, compliance conferences, and oral arguments.

Ms. Escalante practiced plaintiff's personal injury matters in Phoenix, Arizona for the Law Office of Sara J. Powell from 2003-2004. Her focus was on complex litigation matters involving victims of crimes including women and children who were sexually abused or assaulted. From 2005-2007, Ms. Escalante served as a legal liaison for a remediation construction company who was part of a large class action settlement agreement involving damages caused by external water intrusion and mold. Her personable and amicable nature assisted in dispute resolution and the successful completion of the remediation of over 3000 homes. Ms. Escalante also worked as a research attorney for a personal injury firm in Austin, Texas from 2008-2009. In 2009, Ms. Escalante joined a New York immigration firm as Of Counsel working on family based immigration cases. Thereafter, Ms. Escalante became the founder and principal immigration attorney of the Law Office of Marisol L. Escalante, in Baltimore, Maryland from 2010-2013.

For over eight years, Ms. Escalante was a member of Silverman Thompson Slutkin and White, bringing to the firm a wealth of legal experience and expertise in federal immigration matters with a focus on family based cases. Today, Ms. Escalante is the managing attorney for Marisol L. Escalante Law Offices, LLC. She is a fully bilingual Spanish speaking attorney, providing her clients with personal attention and quality legal representation. Ms. Escalante practices before Immigration Courts and the United States Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS).

Ms. Escalante currently lives in Colorado with her husband and 2 teenage children. She especially enjoys spending time with friends and family in the mountains of Breckenridge, CO.

attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Colorado Springs, CO
attorneys.bio:
Graham.Law family law associate Jesse Feinsod is a Colorado Springs native and attended the University of Wyoming College of Law in Laramie, Wyoming. While at UW, Jesse participated in mock trials and the Defender Aid Clinic, helping write criminal appeals.

Jesse began his legal career in Casper, Wyoming where he started with personal injury defense firm. Upon returning to Colorado Springs in 2016, he began working with TESSA in pursuing permanent protection orders for domestic violence victims. In the Spring of 2018, Jesse joined another local law firm, where he continued to represent clients through TESSA, and began his pursuit of domestic relation law.

Jesse joined the Graham Law team in the fall of 2021 and brings with him a background in domestic violence. Jesse's experience with domestic violence is extremely valuable in his current role at Graham.Law, and especially in child custody cases. A domestic violence situation is scary and lonely, and very often the voices of victims are not heard. Jesse gives his victim clients a voice and helps them through the legal process of child custody or dissolution of marriage.

Inevitably, every client brings with them their own unique and personal situation for which each requires the respect and attention of a devoted advocate. Jesse realizes each of his clients has a story to tell within the process of child custody or dissolution and zealously works with his clients to make their voice heard.

Jesse loves living in Colorado Springs with his wife and step daughter, and enjoys Colorado's great outdoor opportunities. Jesse is a member of the Colorado Bar Association and the El Paso County Bar Association.

And Becca knew she had the foundational skills to become a fierce and compassionate courtroom advocate. So, she headed back to school. Becca received her J.D. from the University of Nebraska College of Law. While there, she was Articles Editor for the Nebraska Law Review and served as co-president of the Equal Justice Society. After graduation, Becca clerked for Chief Judge John M. Gerrard of the United States District Court for the District of Nebraska. In her spare time, Becca enjoys skiing, hiking, biking and playing fetch with her dog, Sadie.

attorneys.name: Andrew T. Fitzgerald
attorneys.practice_type: Child Welfare Lawyers in Lakewood, CO
attorneys.bio:
Andrew T. Fitzgerald is a partner at Grob & Eirich and has over twenty (20) years of legal experience as both a judicial officer and attorney in adoption, child welfare, family formation, and complex custody/guardianship matters.

Andrew’s practice focuses on adoption, child welfare, guardianship and custody cases, as well as mediation. Andrew represents prospective adoptive parents, foster parents, relatives, birth parents and serves as general counsel for numerous licensed adoption agencies in Colorado. Andrew's practice includes child adoptions, designated adoptions, interstate adoptions, stepparent adoptions, same sex adoptions, second parent adoptions, relative adoptions, disrupted adoptions, foster-parent adoptions, international adoptions, confirmatory adoptions and adoption subsidies. Andrew also represents intended parents and other individuals in discussing the risks and benefits of different avenues for family formation.

Andrew is a graduate of the Indiana University School of Law in Indianapolis, Indiana. In law school, Andrew volunteered for Amnesty International and headed the awareness committee. Andrew received his undergraduate Bachelor of Arts degree from Auburn University where he majored in English and was a member of the Phi Eta Sigma National Honor Society.

In 2011, Andrew was appointed as a Magistrate in the 1st Judicial District / Jefferson County, Colorado and worked as a judicial officer in Jefferson County through 2023. He was the presiding Magistrate and handled a variety of case types, including Adoptions, Juvenile Dependency and Neglect, Juvenile Delinquency, Domestic Relations, as well as County Civil and Criminal cases, including the Jefferson County problem-solving Courts.

During his time as a Magistrate, Andrew served on the court’s Management Leadership Team, the Court Best Practices committee, and specifically the dependency and neglect system reform committee (DANSR). Andrew also served on the Juvenile Services Planning Committee, as well as Juvenile Review Board and chaired the First Judicial District problem-solving court steering committee and the First Judicial District policy and procedure sub-committee.

Andrew has been long recognized as a gifted teacher and mentor to both attorneys and new judicial officers and has presented annually for the Colorado State Judicial branch at the New Judge Orientation and Advanced New Judge Orientation on the role of Magistrates, Magistrate Jurisdiction, and Protection Orders. Andrew has also presented annual legal presentation for new Court Appointed Special Advocated (“CASA") volunteers in Jefferson County. Additional lectures / presentations include: Protection Orders, Family Law Basics: Indirect Contempt Practice, as well as presentations for the 1st JD Bar Association CLE presentations “Alternative Enforcement: Enforcing Orders without Contempt” and “Domestic Practice: Motions to Restrict Parenting Time.”

Prior to joining the bench, Andrew was a senior attorney at the Rocky Mountain Children's Law Center where he frequently litigated guardianship, custody, dependency and neglect, and adoption cases throughout Colorado. Andrew represented foster children, prospective adoptive parents, relative caregivers; and supervised attorneys and social workers who served as guardians ad litem in Colorado.

During his time at the law center, Andrew also provided legal training on roles and responsibilities of Guardians ad litem to Jefferson County and Adams County human services caseworkers. Andrew also presented at the annual 1st Judicial District Magistrate training on the Colorado Children’s Code and the role of Guardians ad Litem in judicial proceedings.

Prior to his time with the Children's Law Center, Andrew was an accomplished litigator in family law, and has experience in Administrative Court matters as well, successfully appealing a denial of Developmental Disabilities Resource Center (DDRC) eligibility for foster youth.

Trevor Wade Memorial Award

Outstanding Service to Youth in the Community

attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Denver, CO
attorneys.bio:
Emma Fletcher is a partner with Harrington Brewster Mahoney Smits, P.C. Her practice consists of family law and estate planning.

In the family law arena, Emma has extensive experience both in and out of the courtroom. Emma is a collaboratively trained attorney who strives to achieve holistic settlements that allow her clients to move forward with their life in confidence. When amicable settlement is not possible, Emma is well equipped for litigation. Her tactful preparation and poise shine in the courtroom. In addition to individual representation, Emma also provides mediation, arbitration, and PC/DM services.

For estate planning, Emma works with her clients in thoughtful manner that results in a cohesive plan for her clients and their beneficiaries. Clients can work with Emma to create or update planning documents including wills, revocable trusts, powers of attorney, living wills/advance directives, and guardianship appointments. With her experience in family law, Emma is especially well positioned to help clients update their estate plan following a divorce or legal separation.

With a background in both family law and estate planning, a significant portion of Emma’s practice is dedicated to drafting marital and premarital agreements.

attorneys.name: Catherine Ford
attorneys.practice_type: Child and Spousal Abuse Lawyers in Colorado Springs, CO
attorneys.bio:
Catherine graduated Magna Cum Laude in the top fifteen percent of her law school class. She has worked in family law in some capacity her entire life. Catherine also holds a Bachelor of Arts in Philosophy, which allows her to think creatively and craft resolutions that other attorneys may not consider.

In 2025, Catherine was selected as a Super Lawyers Rising Star—an honor awarded to only 2.5% of attorneys in Colorado.

She is a Certified Child and Family Investigator (CFI) and is currently accepting new appointments. Catherine is also a qualified expert in domestic violence, child abuse, and intimate partner violence, bringing a high level of insight and credibility to complex family law matters.

Catherine is a straightforward attorney who knows when to fight for her clients and when it is better to settle. She prides herself on being honest and transparent, even when that requires difficult conversations about the realities of a case. She believes that having uncomfortable discussions is essential to providing honest advocacy and reliable advice.

She focuses her practice on child and spousal abuse cases and child alienation matters. Catherine understands that domestic violence cases involve complex dynamics and require thoughtful, informed advocacy—both to protect victims and to ensure that those wrongfully accused are treated fairly in domestic relations court.

Outside of her legal work, Catherine loves the Denver Broncos, hiking with her family and two dogs, cooking gourmet meals, and having movie nights with her children.

Tim Foster joined the Class Action Group at Franklin D. Azar & Associates in 2020 after leaving his former practice in New York City. He brings over ten years of experience in sophisticated civil and commercial litigation, including complex contract, tort, and bankruptcy litigation matters, with a particular focus on intellectual property litigation. Mr. Foster has a passion for written and oral argument and has appeared on behalf of clients in various state and federal courts all across the United States, as well as before the United States Patent Trial and Appeal Board and the United States Trademark Trial and Appeal Board.

Mr. Foster knew he wanted to be a litigation attorney from the time he was thirteen years old. He received his undergraduate degree from Weber State University in his hometown of Ogden, Utah, with a major in Political Science and a perfect 4.0 grade point average, all while working full time in retail sales and management and while simultaneously competing on the school's nationally ranked Intercollegiate Mock Trial Team. Moving on to law school, Mr. Foster decided to relocate to the East Coast to attend New York University School of Law, where he was a member of the prestigious Moot Court Board, graduating in 2008.

After completing law school, Mr. Foster joined the New York City office of Cooley LLP as a Litigation Associate, where he gained experience in high-stakes commercial litigation matters, representing clients that included global banks and famous authors. After several years of law practice, Mr. Foster took a brief stint performing international regulatory compliance work for Citibank before returning to litigation in 2013 at a commercial litigation boutique in Manhattan's Financial District. As the most experienced associate at that firm, Mr. Foster aggressively represented both plaintiffs and defendants and participated in hearings and proceedings in forums across the country. He regularly appeared in both trial and appellate courts to argue on behalf of his clients, and has conducted and defended dozens of depositions in his career. Transitioning to Class Actions work became a way to merge his love of litigation with his desire to see justice done, wrongdoers punished, and the rights of the mistreated vindicated.

Mr. Foster is admitted to practice law by the State of New York, and is working on obtaining admission in Colorado. He is also admitted to the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York, the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of New York, and the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit.

Mr. Foster loves theatre-either as a member of a cast or as a member of an audience. He loves music in all forms-from punk rock to classical and jazz, and he was a member of a three-time championship team in the New York City Karaoke League. He is a devoted fan of the Denver Broncos (a fascination that began when he was a child) and the New York Mets. Mr. Foster collects fountain pens and enjoys bowling, biking, and hiking. Despite growing up in Utah and now living in Colorado, he has never been skiing-a deficiency he hopes to correct very soon.

attorneys.name: Katie R. Fox
attorneys.practice_type: Commercial Real Estate Transactions Lawyers in Denver, CO
attorneys.bio:
Katie Fox's past experience informs her current practice to assist clients in a range of property law matters including commercial and residential real estate transactions, condemnation, leasing, title claims, and issues related to oil, gas, and other minerals.

Katie graduated from the University of Denver in 2004, cum laude, with a degree in business and received her J.D. from the Sturm College of Law at the University of Denver in 2008. She is a member of the Colorado and Denver Bar Associations, and is currently serving as an at-large council member of the CBA Real Estate Section.

At Alderman Bernstein, Katie has represented numerous buyers and sellers in commercial and residential real estate transactions from contract formation through closing, performed detailed title examinations and drafted related curative documents, represented power companies and special districts in acquiring various easements for multiple projects, and assisted in drafting condemnation pleadings.

As a Colorado native and daughter of city planners, Katie is personally connected to the real estate transactions that shape our community and has worked diligently to develop a diverse network of real estate professionals.

Katie graduated from the University of Denver in 2004, cum laude, with a degree in business and received her J.D. from the Sturm College of Law at the University of Denver in 2008. She is a member of the Colorado and Denver Bar Associations, as well as CREW - an organization dedicated to the advancement of women in commercial real estate.

Katie is also a nature enthusiast who enjoys the Colorado outdoors, and each year, she grows and adds to her cutting garden to share flowers with friends and family on their special occasions.

attorneys.name: Roger D. Fraley Jr.
attorneys.firm_name: Roger D. Fraley Jr., Attorney at Law
attorneys.practice_type: Bad Faith Insurance Lawyers in Denver, CO
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Roger D. Fraley Jr. has been serving clients and providing expert testimony regarding insurance bad faith claims since 1989.

Mr. Fraley has over two decades of experience in practicing law and two decades of experience as an advocate for people injured both on and off the job. Unlike many attorneys these days, Roger is not afraid to go to trial. He has been the lead attorney in over 125 jury trials and numerous workers compensation hearings. Roger has the skills to get you the best result possible to compensate you for your injury.

Mr. Fraley is a member of the Colorado BAR Association as well as the Denver BAR Association, and is admitted to practice before The Federal District Court for the District of Colorado, The 10th Circuit Court of Appeals, and The United States Court of Federal Claims.

Roger Fraley was born in June of 1953 in Norton Virginia. He moved to Denver in 1954.

Roger attended the Collegiate School for Boys in Richmond Virginia and graduated in 1971. He received his bachelors from Stanford University in Palo Alto California in 1975. He went on to attend the University of Virginia and received his Master degree in English in 1978. After teaching high school for one year he became a ranch hand in Wyoming before returning to Denver. He then attended the University of Denver School of Law from which he received a Jurist Doctorate in 1985.

From 1985 until 1988 Roger practiced as a Deputy District Attorney in Denver Colorado. In 1989 he started practicing as an advocate for injured people, and in 1991 expanded his practice to include injured workers. In 1994 Roger opened his own private practice in order to better serve clients.

Roger has over two decades of experience in practicing law and two decades of experience as an advocate for people injured both on and off the job. Unlike many attorneys these days, Roger is not afraid to go to trial. He has been the lead attorney in over 125 jury trials and numerous workers compensation hearings. Roger has the skills to get you the best result possible to compensate you for your injury.

attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Centennial, CO
attorneys.bio:
Leslie A. Frost has a diverse academic background, encompassing science, law, and diplomacy. After receiving her Bachelors of Arts in Environmental, Population, and Organismic Biology at the University of Colorado at Boulder, she went on to obtain her Masters of Arts in Diplomatic Studies, with distinction, from the Diplomatic Academy of London, University of Westminster, in the United Kingdom. Before returning to the United States for law school, she studied British and European Union law in London for a year.

Ms. Frost received her Doctor of Jurisprudence from Santa Clara University School of Law, where she served as the Senior Technical Editor for the Santa Clara Journal of International Law. While in law school, she completed an internship with UNICEF in Kosovo and was the law student liaison to the American Bar Association International Criminal Law Committee.

Ms. Frost is currently a member of the American Bar Association (including Family law and International law sections), Colorado Bar Association, and the Denver Bar Association. She is also on the Attorney List for the U.S. Central Authority for the Hague Abduction Convention of the U.S. Department of State Department.

In her free time, Ms. Frost enjoys playing with her puppy, Sadie, hiking, skiing and cooking.

attorneys.name: Tim Galluzzi
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Denver, CO
attorneys.bio:
Tim Galluzzi loves to represent people and thrives in the fight to protect his clients' rights. Tim fought professionally in mixed martial arts before attending law school, and his passion for challenge and competition carries over into his legal career. He enjoys the thrill of thorough trial preparation and devotes his practice to securing successful outcomes for injured clients.

Tim specializes in personal injury. He litigates cases on behalf of clients injured in car crashes, bicycle crashes, and slip-and-falls, as well as incidents involving damage to a client's home and property, insurance bad faith, or injury from the intentional acts of others.

Tim has been recognized in both of his practice areas. He was named by Super Lawyers to the 2019, 2020, and 2021 Colorado Rising Stars list for his work representing plaintiffs in personal injury cases. The Rising Stars list recognizes no more than 2.5 percent of attorneys in each state. Tim also was named to the 2018 Barrister's Best list by Law Week Colorado as the Best Criminal Defense Lawyer.

Prior to passing the bar, Tim attended law school at the University of Colorado in Boulder. He was an Associate Editor of the Law Review and was selected to CU Law's mock trial and moot court teams, competing nationally and winning numerous awards and competitions. He represented indigent clients at the trial-court level through the Criminal Defense Clinic and at the appellate level through an internship with the Colorado State Public Defender's Office. Tim also interned for Judge J. Eric Elliff on the Denver District Court, where he gained valuable experience with jury trials in Denver County even as a law student.

Tim is active in the legal community. He serves on the University of Colorado Law School Alumni Board and is a member of the Colorado Bar Association, the Colorado Trial Lawyers Association, and the Colorado Criminal Defense Bar.

Outside of the law, Tim continues to pursue his passions. attorneys.name: Keith A Gantenbein
attorneys.practice_type: Foreclosure Defense Lawyers in Denver, CO
attorneys.bio:
Keith A. Gantenbein Jr., is the Owner of Gantenbein Law Firm, specializing in Colorado Foreclosure Defense Law, Colorado HOA Issues and Colorado Real Estate Law.

Keith has worked in real estate for over 10 years, working for his father, a local real estate agent with over 40 years of experience. Keith began his legal career in HOA law, working for Hindman Sanchez, a large Colorado Homeowner's Association (HOA) law firm. Mr. Gantenbein's experience in HOA collections and HOA foreclosures gives him a valuable approach on how to represent homeowners who have issues with their HOAs, including judicial foreclosure and unreasonable HOA fees. Keith then worked for the largest foreclosure firm in Colorado, Castle Stawiarski, in Denver. Keith used his experience to start his own debtor-rights firm, Gantenbein Law Firm, focusing on foreclosure defense, HOA Defense and Real Estate Law.

Working for these two law firms has given Keith a comprehensive and unique perspective on the challenges in the foreclosure, real estate, HOA and mortgage industry facing Coloradoans today.

Passionate in his mission to provide foreclosure help to Colorado homeowners, he knows all-too-well how one-sided the court system can be in favoring the lender. He has dedicated a considerable amount of time in his legal career to changing the system to provide more protection for borrowers and has prevented many foreclosures, keeping families safe at home.

Keith has published more than 150 informative articles on his blogs, and has been highlighted in The Denver Post news stories, Westword and the ABA Journal for his support and foreclosure help of Colorado homeowners and amending foreclosure laws. Also seen on Fox News, Denver Channel 7 news and AOL nationwide, he was again, speaking up for homeowners to improve and revise foreclosure laws. He has volunteered many hours working with the Colorado House and Senate on foreclosure reform, in the drafting of multiple legislative bills designed to provide oversight and protection to homeowners. Keith also taught at multiple seminars and Continuing Legal Education classes for attorneys, including nationwide attorney education conferences.

Most recently, Keith was instrumental in the drafting of House Bills 14-1130 and 14-1295, sponsored by Representive Beth McCann and Senator Jesse Ulibarri. These Bills were recently signed into law and go into effect January 1, 2015.

Keith is admitted to practice law in the State of Colorado and the U.S District Court of Colorado.

At Gantenbein Law Firm, Mr. Gantenbein is focused on Colorado Foreclosure Defense- including foreclosure help in Colorado, Colorado Real Estate Law, Colorado HOA Law, Colorado Landlord/Tenant Law, Credit Dispute and Credit Repair, and Civil Litigation.
