attorneys.name: Melinda S. Moses
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Denver, CO
attorneys.bio:
Melinda, or Mindy as she is better known, is a member of Ciancio Ciancio Brown, P.C. family law team. Mindy comes to CCB from a boutique firm that specialized in family law and probate. Before that, Mindy worked as a staff attorney at the Colorado Court of Appeals for almost 20 years. She specialized in cases involving all aspects of family law, dependency and neglect, and workers’ compensation. The issues she addressed ran the gamut from adoption and paternity to complex financial matters. Her cases often required resolution of constitutional issues and issues of first impression.

In addition to her work at the court and in private practice, Mindy has presented or co-presented at several seminars, including the Colorado Family Law Institute, where she spoke on “Appellate Practice 101,” a CLE seminar held at the Denver Juvenile Court on “Tips and Themes for Dependency and Neglect Appeals,” and at the Colorado Elder Law Retreat on “Grey Divorce.” Mindy also serves as a member of the Board of Law Examiner’s Law Committee, which oversees administration of the Colorado Bar Exam.

Mindy completed her undergraduate degree with distinction at the University of Colorado in English Literature, where she was inducted as a member of Phi Beta Kappa, was on the Dean’s List all four years, and received the Dean’s Scholarship. She earned her law degree from the University of Colorado School of Law, where she received the Moses Lasky Scholarship and the American Jurisprudence Award for Torts and Legal Seminar. After law school, Mindy was a Judicial Law Clerk to the Honorable Dale P. Tursi, and the Honorable John A. Criswell, both of whom served on the Colorado Court of Appeals.

Mindy is a fourth-generation Denver native. She and her husband, an architect, have raised two daughters in their historic Denver square home. Mindy enjoys time with family and friends, travel, museums, hiking, fiction, and films. At CCB, she strives to serve her clients with compassion, patience, and the skill necessary to guide them through the dissolution and post-decree process as painlessly and efficiently as possible.

attorneys.name: Judge Edward C. Moss
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Denver, CO
attorneys.bio:
After 24 years as a civil litigator and 16 years as a Colorado District Court judge, Ed Moss retired in August 2020. Before being appointed to the bench, he had a varied career as a U.S. Army officer, United States Supreme Court intern, United States District Court law clerk, commercial trial lawyer emphasizing real estate, oil and gas, and general commercial law, a member of the Westminster, Colorado City Council, and Mayor of Westminster, Colorado.

Since his appointment to the Colorado District Court in 2004, Judge Moss presided over hundreds of criminal, civil, mental health, family law, juvenile delinquency, and child dependency and neglect trials. He is a frequent lecturer on attorney and judicial ethics and was the 2016 – 2017 Chair of the Colorado Bar Association Ethics Committee. In 2010, the U.S. Department of Justice invited Judge Moss to discuss judicial performance criteria at an international symposium in Ankara, Turkey.

attorneys.name: Joseph Moulton
attorneys.firm_name: Frank Azar Car & Truck Accident Lawyers - Aurora, Colorado
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Aurora, CO
attorneys.bio:
Joe Moulton was born in Castle Rock, CO. His family later moved to the St. Louis area where he attended high school. Joe earned the award of Eagle Scout at the age of 14. Joe was also heavily involved in sports playing football and golf. After high school, Joe attended Millikin University in Decatur, Illinois where he earned a B.S. in Sports Management with a minor in Digital Media Marketing. He was a student-athlete at Millikin University as a member of the men's golf team. He also received academic honors by joining the Alpha Lamda Beta and Alpha Lamda Delta Scholar Fraternities.

After graduation, Joe began his career in sales and logistics for national companies working in Denver and St. Louis. Wanting to help people and be more dedicated to his community, he decided to attend law school.

Joe received his Juris Doctorate from Saint Louis University School of Law. During his time at law school, Joe worked for several law firms representing individuals, insurance companies, and corporations. During this time Joe devoted himself to learning the ins and outs of the pre-litigation and litigation process so that he could aggressively advocate for his future clients.

After law school, Joe began his career representing injured individuals in negligent and reckless driving, product liability, and wrongful death matters in the St. Louis Area. He is happy to be back home in the Denver metropolitan area representing people against negligent and reckless drivers and insurance companies.

Joe is admitted to practice in State and Federal Courts in Colorado. Joe is also licensed to practice law in Missouri. His practice focuses on personal injury and insurance bad faith litigation.

Joe enjoys spending time with his friends and family, golfing, and is a passionate Denver sports fan.

attorneys.name: Shawn Moussou
attorneys.practice_type: Child Support Lawyers in Greenwood Village, CO
attorneys.bio:
Shawn is an associate attorney at Ammarell Deasy, LLP, where he practices family law. Shawn represents clients both at trial and on appeal in matters involving divorce, allocation of parental responsibilities, child support, spousal maintenance, and dependency and neglect matters. Shawn also has experience bringing and defending against protection orders, emergency motions, and contempt allegations. During his legal career, Shawn has both settled and litigated cases in jurisdictions throughout Colorado. Shawn obtained his law degree from the University of Texas School of Law, and received his bachelor's degree in Political Science, summa cum laude with Major Honors and Distinction from the University of Texas at Dallas. He was admitted to practice law in Colorado in November of 2018. During law school, Shawn clerked at the Texas Attorney General's Office working in the General Civil Litigation Division where he assisted attorneys with litigation related issues in Federal and State Court regarding issues arising under the 14th Amendment to the United States Constitution and as well as both Federal and State Employment Law related issues. Shawn also interned at the Texas Court of Criminal Appeals - the Court of last resort for criminal matters in Texas - for the Honorable Michael Keasler. After law school, but before bar results were released, Shawn clerked for a solo law firm in Littleton, CO and was introduced to family law - where he found his niche. Shawn prides himself on his ability to connect with clients as they navigate their difficult circumstances, helping them to achieve their short and long-term goals. Shawn's approach to family law cases is to gather and synthesize all the relevant information to advise his clients so they can make informed decisions. Shawn balances both the legal and practical implications of decisions because in family law, it is vital to consider both. Shawn enjoys working at Ammarell Deasy because of the comradery and support his fellow colleagues provide both inside and outside of the office. Shawn was born and raised in Stuart, Florida on the Treasure Coast. After traveling across the country living in numerous states, Shawn landed in Colorado. He enjoys hiking the Flatirons with his family during the Summer and Fall and hitting the slopes in Colorado, Wyoming, and New Mexico during the Winter and Spring.

attorneys.name: Josh Murphy
attorneys.practice_type: Elder Law Lawyers in Denver, CO
attorneys.bio:
Josh joined Glatstein & O’Brien in September 2025, after many years of practice in public service, most recently as staff attorney for the Colorado Office of Public Guardianship. Josh began his law career as a Legal Aid attorney where he represented many individuals and families seeking guardianship and conservatorship for their loved ones, as well as individuals wrongfully denied Medicaid and other government benefits. Before relocating to Colorado, he served as legal counsel for the Jackson County (Missouri) Public Administrator, practicing primarily in the areas of probate administration and litigation, as well as guardianship and conservatorship proceedings.

Josh currently practices in the areas of elder law, guardianship and conservatorship proceedings, probate administration and litigation, estate and trust planning, and fiduciary representation. He also advises clients on planning for incapacity and the use of special needs and discretionary trusts to preserve public benefits for incapacitated and disabled individuals. He is an active member of the Colorado Bar Association, particularly in the Elder Law section.

attorneys.name: Kirsten Z. Myers
attorneys.practice_type: Family law and divorce Lawyers in Lakewood, CO
attorneys.bio:
Ms. Myers joined Pearson & Paris, P.C. on January 8, 2018. She is a skilled civil attorney and handles a wide range of civil matters. In the landlord-tenant arena, Ms. Myers has successfully handled a broad range of eviction cases, ensuring landlords protect their rights while complying with evolving local and state laws. Ms. Myers is known for efficiently resolving disputes to minimize disruption and financial exposure for property owners and managers.

Ms. Myers has guided clients from pre-litigation strategy through trial in cases involving breach of contract, personal injury claims, insurance disputes, real estate disputes, and construction claims. She prides herself on her ability to communicate, both orally and in writing, superior work ethic, and analytical reasoning skills. These skills and Ms. Myers’s attention to detail directly translate to her practice areas, enabling Ms. Myers to provide competent and strategic legal representation.

Ms. Myers received her Juris Doctorate from Valparaiso University Law School. During her law school tenure, Ms. Myers served as Editor-in-Chief of the Valparaiso University Law Review and was one of the founding members and treasurer of the Asian American Pacific Islander Law Student Association. Ms. Myers also participated in the Juvenile and Family Law clinic where she served as Guardian Ad Litem in family-related matters to help resolve disputes of parenting time and decision-making responsibility. Ms. Myers also appeared in the Porter County Juvenile Court as a public defender for individuals facing contempt charges for failure to pay child support. Ms. Myers was a recipient of the Hoeppner, Wagner & Evans Scholarship for outstanding commitment to the law school and was awarded the Scribes Award for demonstrating the highest levels of legal professionalism and excellence in legal writing. In May 2017, Ms. Myers was inducted into the National Order of Scribes. Since 2022 Ms. Myers has been an annual recipient of the Super Lawyers Rising Star distinction.

Outside of work, Ms. Myers enjoys cooking and experimenting with new recipes, travelling, and spending time with friends, family, and her dog, Roger.

attorneys.name: Richard C. Nehls
attorneys.practice_type: Real Estate Lawyers in Boulder, CO
attorneys.bio:
Richard C. Nehls has practiced law in Boulder, Colorado since 1976. Rich concentrates his practice on real estate and other business transactions. His real estate practice includes the purchase, development, financing, construction, leasing and sale of office, retail, residential, and industrial buildings. His business transaction practice includes entity formation and the acquisition and sale of ongoing businesses via asset or stock acquisition--for example, the purchase or sale of cable companies, rafting companies, fast food franchises, and restaurants. Rich graduated from the University of Chicago Law School where he was an editor of the law review. He served as the president of the Boulder County Bar Association in 1994 and 1995 and received its Award of Merit in 2000 for outstanding achievement, dedication to the legal profession, and service to the community. Prior to becoming a partner at Packard Dierking, Rich was the managing partner of Lirtzman, Nehls & Hepner. When he is not practicing law, Rich enjoys skiing, mountain biking, concerts, movies, college football, and college basketball.

Awards and Honors

Honors

Award of Merit, "Outstanding Achievement, Dedication to the Legal Profession, and Service to the Community", 2000

attorneys.name: Zachary Newland Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Federal Criminal Defense Lawyers in Evergreen, CO
attorneys.bio:
Federal criminal defense lawyer first and foremost.

Zachary Newland is a dedicated and experienced attorney with over a decade of experience representing clients in civil and criminal litigation matters impacting federal court. He has experience in handling all aspects of the litigation process including client consultation, legal research, motion practice, managing discovery, trial advocacy, and appellate representation.

Zachary represents clients across the country when the stakes are highest and clients cannot afford to lose. Zachary is proud to provide nationwide legal services from the Evergreen Attorneys office in Evergreen, Colorado.

Zachary Newland has worked on numerous high-profile federal criminal cases as part of national defense teams including defending Bernard Madoff, Joseph Maldonado-Passage (a/k/a Tiger King), and Ross Ulbricht (alleged founder of the Silk Road), among many others.

This Evergreen, Colorado lawyer is able to look at legal issues from multiple angles, devise effective strategies, and achieve favorable results.

Zachary Newland handles all types of federal criminal cases. This Denver federal defense attorney is proud to bring the fight to the government to protect your rights.

No matter the case, Zachary brings a client-first approach. Solving problems instead of making them is always the goal at Evergreen Attorneys.

That means different things in every case. In a Colorado federal criminal case it might mean preparing a client for a jury trial from day one knowing everything is on the line. But the right lawyers know that each case is different. Sometimes, a client facing Colorado federal grand jury investigations needs to carefully make sure that charges are resolved before they can ever be filed.

Contact Zachary Newland today if you are looking for help in a federal criminal case anywhere in the United States.

Zachary Newland is a father of two beautiful children, the lucky husband to a beautiful and successful wife, enthusiastic (but mediocre) skier, and aspiring BBQ connoisseur. Zachary Newland lives in idyllic Evergreen, Colorado, and practices in federal courts nationwide.

Representative Matters

Zachary Newland has appeared as counsel of record in over 120 federal cases all across the country since 2016.

Represented physician charged with making False Statement Related to Health Care Matters in violation of 18 U.S.C. Section 1035(a)(2), (b) related to alleged telehealth fraud. Successfully resolved matter with client receiving probationary sentence and no jail time.

Represented client in direct criminal appeal to Seventh Circuit. Successfully obtained reversal of lower court decision to deny hearing on motion to suppress evidence under Fourth Amendment based on lack of a Franks hearing.

Represented client as jury trial counsel in two-week long murder trial. Successfully obtained complete acquittal based on self-defense and defense of others.

Represented client as lead counsel at two-week long jury trial in U.S. District Court for District of Colorado. Client charged with wire fraud 18 U.S.C. Section 1343, money laundering in violation of 18 U.S.C. Section 1956 and 1957, and conspiracy in complex multi-million dollar alleged fraud case.

Represented client as jury trial counsel in U.S. District Court for Western District of Texas. Client charged with federal tax fraud in violation 26 U.S.C. Section 7201 and other related offenses.

Represented Nurse Practitioner charged with unlawfully distributing controlled substances in violation of 21 U.S.C. Section 841. Medical provider charged with federal drug statute offenses in connection with complex telehealth case spanning multiple states.

Represented client on appeal to Seventh Circuit from denial of motion to reduce sentence. Obtained reversal on issue of first impression involving Section 404 of the First Step Act of 2018.

Represented client in suing the Federal Bureau of Prisons for violating civil rights of inmate under Religious Freedom and Restoration Act (RFRA). Secured favorable settlement and change in policy for client.

Represented client on appeal to the District of Columbia Circuit Court of Appeals. Appeal sought access to Federal Bureau of Prisons materials under FOIA.

Represented client in seeking compassionate release from federal prison based on extraordinary medical conditions. Secured immediately release from prison for client after lengthy prison term.

Represented client on appeal to Tenth Circuit Court of Appeals. Successfully obtained reversal and published opinion on issue of first impression within the Tenth Circuit jurisdiction.

Secured Presidential commutation (clemency) for multiple clients seeking executive clemency. Clients received reduced sentences and were ultimately released early from prison.

Represented physician in seeking to overturn sentence for unlawfully distributing controlled substances under 21 U.S.C. Section 841. Challenge involved legal issue of first-impression based on retroactivity of Ruan decision.

Represented client in challenging restitution order resulting in millions of dollars benefit to client.

Represented client in challenging attempted forfeiture of personal residence after guilty plea. Client able to retain proceeds from sale of his home based on novel argument involving Nevada state law, trusts, and criminal forfeiture.

attorneys.name: Lawrence E. Nordling
attorneys.practice_type: Insurance Defense and Coverage Lawyers in Denver, CO
attorneys.bio:
Lawrence Nordling is an experienced litigator who handles pre-suit matters and active litigation in Kansas and Missouri. Larry has handled first and third-party cases throughout his entire career including premises liability, property damage, product liability, commercial coverage disputes and high exposure injury and death cases. He also has experience representing clients in significant business and commercial litigation matters including multi-jurisdictional concurrent litigation, as well as construction defect litigation on significant personal, commercial and/or public entity/governmental construction projects and developments. Larry also works with the firm’s transportation litigation attorneys defending corporations and other civil defendants.

In addition to representing his clients in high-stakes litigation, Larry has extended his devotion to the legal community through his service to the profession and his community; including serving as a Board Member of the Kansas Association of Defense Counsel (KADC), and as an invited lecturer for the Greater Kansas City Chamber of Commerce and the Kansas Bar Association. Larry has also authored publications and presentation materials on a variety of topics for KADC, Missouri Organization of Defense Lawyers (MODL), and the Defense Research Institute (DRI). Larry is also active in his local community and enjoys spending time with his wife and two children.

attorneys.name: Bradley J. O'Brien
attorneys.practice_type: Real Estate & Business Lawyers in Denver, CO
attorneys.bio:
Proactive, Personalized Representation for Real Estate and Business Transactions and Disputes

O'Brien Legal assists individuals and businesses with real estate and business legal matters, including transactions, advice and disputes. Bradley J. O'Brien is the principal attorney. He has more than 10 years of legal experience and is licensed to practice law in Colorado. Mr. O'Brien formerly practiced at a large law firm, where he gained experience with large and complex matters. At O'Brien Legal, the objective is to provide that big-law expertise for clients and matters of all sizes while being more responsive and more affordable than big law firms.

A Trustworthy Legal Advisor to Navigate Complex Legal Issues

O'Brien Legal helps its clients navigate complex legal issues. Whether it is closing a deal or resolving a dispute, O'Brien Legal identifies the key facts and applicable law that matter the most to reaching the client's objective. Experience from hundreds of transactions and disputes helps O'Brien Legal give its clients a fair and accurate assessment of the real-world facts and applicable law. O'Brien Legal identifies ways to mitigate risks and financial exposure and to reduce or avoid litigation costs. O'Brien Legal uses plain language and minimizes technical jargon in its analysis and recommendations and in drafting documents. This approach allows clients to spend less time on legal matters and more time on their business.

Real Estate Law, Business Law, Transactions and Litigation:

Real estate purchase, sale, financing and leasing

Draft and negotiate contracts and deeds

Prepare loan and security documents

Business entity formation, general business law and corporate transactions

Due diligence and title review

Land development and zoning

Attorney opinion letters

Breach-of-contract and debt collection

Land-related disputes: easements, encroachments, adverse possession, trespass, nuisance and quiet title

Other real estate disputes: foreclosure, mechanic's liens, HOA liens and covenants, landlord/tenant (commercial), deed and title defects, and tenancy-in-common

Prior to becoming a lawyer in 2005, Brad was a corporate finance and real estate finance professional for nine years, including five years as an associate director with a Fortune 100 company, and four years in commercial real estate and multifamily residential lending.

In addition to a special focus on negotiating and closing real estate transactions, he strives to resolve clients' legal disputes short of trial through settlement discussions, mediation and/or arbitration at strategic points in the case timeline.

attorneys.name: Lindsay Obert
attorneys.practice_type: Litigation Lawyers in Colorado Springs, CO
attorneys.bio:
Lindsay Obert is an experienced litigator with Robinson & Henry’s Civil Litigation practice. She has been in private practice since 2010 and is committed to helping clients resolve their civil litigation and real estate matters.

In her previous role, Lindsay handled cases for a diverse clientele, from large government entities to individual residential landlords. She assists clients facing unique challenges related to their properties and has experience with matters concerning titles, lot lines, and easements for mountain and historic properties.

For Lindsay, no two civil litigation cases are the same. She is dedicated to helping her clients manage their significant assets through strategic planning, selling, purchasing, renovating, and leasing.

Representative matters:

Commercial eviction – Successfully evicted delinquent commercial tenant after several months of failing to pay rent

Residential non-disclosure – Resolved failure to disclose matter for new homeowners surprised with a large HOA assessment upon closing

Bad contractor – Prevailed at trial on behalf of an HOA board against a contractor’s shoddy workmanship performance

Protected leasehold rights – Successfully obtained summary judgment for tenant in non-disclosure lawsuit over commercial parking lot

attorneys.firm_name: The Law Offices of M. Kent Olsen, P.C.
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Denver, CO
attorneys.bio:
M. Kent Olsen is a founding partner of The Law Offices of M. Kent Olsen, P.C. who specializes in estate planning, estate and trust administration, estate and trust litigation, guardianships and conservatorships, advanced medical directives, individuals with disabilities, and elder law. Mr. Olsen was Referee of the Denver Probate Court for six years prior to founding Olsen & Traeger, LLP.

Mr. Olsen is a member of the Colorado, Denver and American Bar Associations. As a long-term member of the Trust and Estate Section of the Colorado Bar Association, Mr. Olsen previously served as Chair of the Section, Chair of the Rules and Forms Committee, Column Editor for The Colorado Lawyer - Estate and Trust Forum, and Co-Chair of the Protective Proceedings Act Subcommittee; at this time, Mr. Olsen is a past member of the Statutory Revisions Committee.

Mr. Olsen was an appointed member of the Governor's Commission on Life and the Law. In addition to being a former instructor for paralegals and a member of the advisory board of Denver Career College, Mr. Olsen is a frequent author and lecturer on probate, estate litigation, disabilities planning, health care treatment, protective proceedings, legal ethics, and issues on aging.

Mr. Olsen is a founding member of the Colorado Fund for People with Disabilities, Inc., a pooled Medicaid trust; a past President of Advocacy Denver, an advocacy organization for people with developmental and intellectual disabilities; and a Board member of Arc of Colorado. Mr. Olsen's name appears in Who's Who in America, Who's Who in the World, and Martindale-Hubbell's Bar Register of Preeminent Lawyers. Additionally, Mr. Olsen has been named as a Colorado Super Lawyer since 2006.

attorneys.name: Sean T. Olson
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Denver, CO
attorneys.bio:
Sean Olson is a trial lawyer and founding member of the Olson Personal Injury Lawyers serving clients in Colorado and Wyoming. His practice focuses on providing unrivaled representation in and outside courtrooms at the state and federal level.

Prior to founding the firm, Olson served the law enforcement and business communities as a partner at another prominent law firm and as an associate attorney at a national litigation firm. Olson's experience at those firms allows him to offer the same quality of service provided by large Seventeenth Street law firms, at a fraction of the cost. Olson tailors his representation to the needs and desires of each client, taking the time to determine his client's wishes prior to beginning work on a case.

Olson received his J.D. from the University of Denver Sturm College of Law where he graduated in the top 1 percent of his class, and where, since 2010, he serves as an adjunct professor teaching trial advocacy. He graduated from Drake University in 1995 with a Bachelor of Arts in Journalism and Mass Communication. Super Lawyers named Olson a Rising Star for the last four years in a row.

Olson is a resident of Denver where he lives with his wife, two young children, and their dog, Maisy. Prior to becoming an attorney, Sean was an Emmy award winning photojournalist. His passion for that job took him around the globe telling other's stories. He now uses those skills to tell his clients' stories in courtrooms across Colorado and Wyoming.

attorneys.name: Halleh T. Omidi
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce Lawyers in Denver, CO
attorneys.bio:
Halleh T. Omidi counsels clients on the various aspects of dissolution of marriage cases, including complex asset division, allocation of parental responsibilities, child support, maintenance, paternity, post-decree modifications, appeals, and the like.

Halleh is experienced in litigation as often it is necessary for a case to be litigated. In 2013, Halleh completed the Houston Family Law Trial Institute, an elite family law trial seminar. However, when litigation is not required, she negotiates with opposing counsel/opposing parties, for an optimal outcome for her client's in highly contentious domestic matters.

Halleh was born and raised in Westminster, Colorado. Her experience and dedication to family law began even before she attended law school. She completed her undergraduate course work at the University of Colorado Boulder, graduating summa cum laude. During college, Halleh interned for the Boulder County Juvenile Court.

While in law school, she worked as a student attorney in the University of Colorado Juvenile Law Clinic representing children as a Guardian ad Litem in Dependency and Neglect cases. In addition, she also represented parents as Respondent Parent Counsel in Dependency and Neglect cases.

Halleh's experience in advocating for the best interests of the children is helpful in parental responsibility disputes because it gave her the tools to advise her clients of the outcomes that will benefit their children the most. Additionally, she spent time working on family law cases as a law clerk at Hogan Omidi, PC during law school. After law school, she worked at the Martin Law Firm representing clients in divorce, child custody, paternity, and post decree matters. In recognition of her high standard of ethics and successful outcomes for her clients, Halleh holds an AVVO "Superb" rating and has been awarded the AVVO "Client's Choice Award" for the past several years. Halleh was also given the distinction of Rising Star in the 2016 and 2017 publications of Super Lawyers Magazine

She serves the community as a committee member and mentor for "Law School Yes We Can," as a regular volunteer for Metro Volunteer Lawyers, and as a guest instructor for a variety of courses and panels at the University of Colorado Law School.

When she is not helping families navigate the legal system, Halleh enjoys practicing yoga, watersports, hiking, reading and traveling.

attorneys.name: Beverly W. Oserow Rhodes
attorneys.practice_type: Immigration & Naturalization Law Lawyers in Denver, CO
attorneys.bio:
Ms. Oserow Rhodes received her law degree from the University of Cincinnati in 1978 and a Master's of Business Administration in Taxation from Golden Gate University in 1984. She received her Bachelor's degree from Bowling Green State University. Since 1984 Ms. Oserow Rhodes' practice has been limited to U.S. immigration and naturalization law with an emphasis in employment-based immigration (including investor visas, religious workers, intracompany transferees, and labor certifications); as well as family immigration, deportation and removal defense, and political asylum. Ms. Oserow Rhodes focused on tax, estate planning and corporate law prior to limiting her practice to U.S. immigration and naturalization law.

Ms. Oserow Rhodes has represented clients before the U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Service (formerly INS), Immigration Courts, the Board of Immigration Appeals, the U.S. District Court (Denver, Colorado), the Tenth Circuit Court of Appeals, and the U.S. Department of Labor. She has testified as an expert witness in state court proceedings on immigration issues.

Ms. Oserow Rhodes is a member of the American Immigration Lawyers Association (AILA) and has been a speaker at the AILA annual conference. She has lectured at the AILA National Annual Conference and has lectured on immigration topics at various other seminars in Colorado. Ms. Oserow Rhodes is a past Chairperson of the Colorado Chapter of the American Immigration Lawyers Association. She serves as the Colorado AILA liaison to the US Customs and Border Protection agency and is a past member of the AILA Colorado Chapter Asylum Liaison committee. Ms. Oserow Rhodes is a member of the Colorado and Denver Bar Associations and a past member of the Denver Tax Association.

attorneys.name: David Lee Owen Jr.
attorneys.firm_name: Law Offices of David L. Owen, Jr., P.C.
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Lawyers in Highlands Ranch, CO
attorneys.bio:
I began my legal career in Kansas City, Missouri, providing legal representation to individuals charged with violating criminal laws from misdemeanors to felonies - in state and federal courts. From 1989 - 2007, I was an Assistant Federal Public Defender, rising to the position of First Assistant. During my 18 years at the Federal Public Defender's office, I defended individuals charged with all types of crimes, including high profile cases involving white collar crime, drugs, computer crimes, weapons offenses, conspiracy and death penalty defense.

While attending Adams State College in Alamosa, CO, I was a member of the Associated Student Government and was President of the student body my senior year. One of the programs which I instituted while President was a student legal services program which ensured all Adams State students had access to legal representation regardless of personal fiances.

During law school at Ohio Northern University, I participated in the Celebreeze Moot Court competition and also did an internship with the Lima, Ohio prosecutor's office.

I received additional training in conducting criminal defense trials attending the National Criminal Defense College in Macon, Georgia.

I honorably served my country in the United States Navy for 6 years.

On a personal level, I am s very passionate about golf.

The criminal defense Law Office of David L. Owen, Jr., P.C., focuses on the representation of individuals charged with violating Federal or Colorado criminal laws. Clients benefit from my twenty-two (22) years as a criminal trial attorney. I have handled hundreds of complex criminal jury trials involving all types of felony cases, such as:

Assaults

Arson

Offenses

Fraud

Theft

Burglary

Robbery

Kidnapping

Juvenile Cases

Computer crimes

Murder/Homicide

Public corruption

Identity Theft

Drug Offenses

Illegal Reentry

Bank Robbery

Sex Offenses

Economic Crimes

Firearms Offenses

Counterfeiting

Some of these previous trials have been high profile, with offenses involving : Kidnapping Resulting in Death (a death penalty case), Murder for Hire and, Public Corruption.

Being charged with a criminal offense is a very frightening and life changing event. A good criminal defense attorney will know and fight for your rights. Many times prosecutors are looking to make a name for themselves and will seek a conviction at all costs and without concern for your constitutional rights. Two of those constitutional rights are: the right to trial by a jury of your peers. The other is: every person is innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt. Make sure you have a qualified and experienced criminal trial attorney working for you. My 22 years of criminal trial experience against all types of prosecutors (Federal and State) has given me the tools to fight for your rights.

How you respond to a criminal charge is very important to your rights, now and in the future. There are considerations far beyond the immediate release on bail after being charged with a crime. Should you ever be charged in Federal criminal court, a previous state court conviction will have a severe impact upon the sentencing options a Federal criminal court judge will have. My experience in Federal criminal courts gives you that edge to make sure your rights are not lost in the hue and cry of prior state convictions.

If you have been arrested or even contacted by a law enforcement officer, call the Law Office of David L. Owen, Jr., P.C., and I will discuss your matter in confidence making sure your rights and interests are protected.

In my practice I serve the criminal defense needs of Colorado's Front Range communities: Denver, Aurora, Golden, Boulder, Lakewood, Littleton, Highlands Ranch, Castle Rock, Colorado Springs, Monument, Wheat Ridge, Westminster, Arvada, Commerce City, Brighton, Evergreen, Northglenn, Thornton and Broomfield or anywhere in Colorado someone needs a criminal defense attorney skilled at both the Federal & State levels.

attorneys.name: Brigette M. Paige
attorneys.practice_type: Real Estate Lawyers in Boulder, CO
attorneys.bio:
Brigette M. Paige has a transactional practice that provides support to clients in the areas of real estate, business, and taxation. Her extensive real estate experience includes real property acquisitions and sales, developments, and financings. She also has expertise in the formation of common interest communities under the Colorado Common Interest Ownership Act and has represented both landlords and tenants in the negotiation of retail, commercial, and industrial leases. Her business expertise includes providing general representation to emerging and growing businesses and non-profit organizations on issues including entity formation and governance, private financing, taxation, mergers and acquisitions, and employment and consulting arrangements. Finally, Brigette also has an LLM in taxation, which has enabled her to provide clients with sophisticated income tax planning and estate planning services. Brigette attended the University of Colorado School of Law where she was selected to be a member of the Order of the Coif and served as an editor of the University of Colorado Law Review. Prior to co-founding the firm, she practiced with Sherman and Howard and Hutchinson Black and Cook. Brigette loves to play tennis in her free time but most of her free time is consumed by her husband and five children.

attorneys.practice_type: Bankruptcy Lawyers in Denver, CO
attorneys.bio:
Gabrielle G. Palmer is a member of the firm. She focuses her practice on advising debtors, creditors, creditors committees and trustees in chapter 7 and chapter 11 bankruptcy cases. Gabrielle also represents clients in complex commercial litigation in state and federal courts, out of court workouts, collection actions, and other insolvency-related matters.

REPRESENTATIVE MATTERS

Represented unsecured creditors committee in a chapter 11 bankruptcy case filed by the developer of a stalled condominium development in a Colorado mountain town.

Represented retail debtor in chapter 11 bankruptcy case and § 363 sale and obtained dismissal of case after sale proceeds were distributed.

Represented numerous chapter 7 trustees in § 363 sales, exemption issues and other bankruptcy specific matters resulting in successful outcomes and favorable settlements.

Represented numerous chapter 7 trustees and defendants in avoidance actions (§ 547 preferences, § 548 fraudulent transfers, breach of fiduciary duty, and other claims) resulting in favorable settlements and successful trial outcomes.

Represented mechanic’s lien claimant in state court foreclosure action and trust fund litigation in bankruptcy court and obtained favorable settlement.

Represented commercial landlords in connection with lease negotiations and tenant evictions.

attorneys.name: Alan L. Pasternack
attorneys.practice_type: Real Estate Development and Finance Lawyers in Denver, CO
attorneys.bio:
Alan Pasternack is a tax and transactional attorney specializing in business and real estate transactions involving tax advantaged investing and community development. Alan represents developers, non-profit community development corporations, and community development entities in structuring, negotiating and documenting transactions in which a significant portion of the financing is derived from federal tax incentives, particularly new markets tax credits, historic rehabilitation tax credits, low-income housing tax credits, and tax-exempt bonds, and government loans and grants. Alan's experience includes transactions using multiple financing sources, including transactions twinning new markets tax credits with historic rehabilitation tax credits, and transactions involving new markets tax credits and tax exempt bonds.

Alan is active in the ABA Forum on Affordable Housing and Community Development Law, is a regular speaker at Forum conferences, and chairs the Forum's New Markets Tax Credits committee. Alan is also a regular speaker at industry conferences.

attorneys.name: Marc C. Patoile
attorneys.practice_type: Complex Litigation Lawyers in Castle Rock, CO
attorneys.bio:
Marc Patoile’s practice focuses on complex litigation, where he brings a law and business based education, which includes an M.B.A., and a diverse range of courtroom experience to these matters. Mr. Patoile has developed a regional reputation as a trial lawyer handing family law and criminal matters. He also practices in equine law matters and civil litigation.

He has first-chaired over 100 trials to juries and the courts in domestic, criminal and civil matters. He has also served as a mediator and court-appointed special master, in addition to having a background in collaborative law, which affords him a unique perspective on settling complex matters.

Mr. Patoile is the past President of the Douglas-Elbert County Bar Association, where he also served as Vice-President and Treasurer. He has served on to the Colorado Board of Governors and serves as an alternate Municipal Court Judge. Mr. Patoile was the prosecuting attorney for several years in Monument, Colorado and has been a Special Prosecutor in Castle Rock and Greenwood Village, Colorado. He has been previously appointed by federal and local courts to handle a wide variety of trial matters.

The firm was chosen as the Best of the Best 2007 Law Practice and as the 2008-Douglas County's Finest Attorneys. Mr. Patoile has been chosen as the Best of the Best 2009 Attorney, by the readers of the Douglas County News-Press and the Castle Rock News Press.

Mr. Patoile has achieved the highest possible ranking in the Martindale-Hubbell attorney rating system: AV-Preeminent Lawyer.

attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Highlands Ranch, CO
attorneys.bio:
Matthew Patton is a seasoned trial attorney who oversees one of Robinson & Henry’s Family Law Teams.

Matthew has been in private practice for more than a decade, serving as the primary attorney responsible for key decisions in complex family law litigation and criminal defense trials. Before that, he gained invaluable experience as District Attorney for the 18th Judicial District, where he prosecuted numerous misdemeanor and felony cases and participated in hundreds of trials and motions hearings. These credentials, coupled with the perspective he gained working as a Division Clerk for Douglas County Court and Deputy Sheriff of the Larimer County Sheriff’s Office, have given him insight into nearly every aspect of the legal system.

Every case presents a unique set of circumstances, and Matthew is dedicated to helping his clients achieve optimal outcomes in their complicated and sensitive legal matters. He accomplishes this through exceptional presentation and communication skills in pursuit of the best possible outcomes, whether through skilled negotiation, mediation, or aggressive representation in court.

Domestic violence defense - Achieved acquittal at trial and dismissal of all charges on behalf of client wrongfully accused of domestic violence amid divorce proceedings

Contentious custody dispute - Secured majority custody award for client if opposing party proceeded with their request to relocate

Common law marriage refutation - Successfully disputed claims that client was common law married to a former partner

attorneys.name: Kenneth B. Pennywell
attorneys.firm_name: Frank Azar Car & Truck Accident Lawyers - Aurora, Colorado
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Aurora, CO
attorneys.bio:
"I've seen many things in my career, protecting people's rights is one of the reasons I became an attorney."

Kenneth B. Pennywell was born in Shreveport, Louisiana. He witnessed firsthand the remnants of the post Jim Crow era regarding the treatment of blacks in America. Inspired by historical icons such as Thurgood Marshall, Mr. Pennywell decided to become an attorney. Mr. Pennywell received his B.A. from Southern University in Baton Rouge, Louisiana in 1981 and his J.D. in 1984 from Southern University School of Law. Kenneth was admitted to the Louisiana Bar in 1985 and Colorado Bar in 1992.

Mr. Pennywell's experience includes being a law clerk for the Louisiana State Senate from 1984-1985. He also served as an Assistant District Attorney for the 1st Judicial District in Caddo Parish, Louisiana from 1985-1993 and prosecuted all major felonies including murders, rapes, and armed robberies. Remembering a family vacation to Colorado Springs and how beautiful it was, Mr. Pennywell decided it was time for a change of scenery and Colorado was the perfect place.

After relocating to Colorado, he worked from 1993 to 2000 with the Colorado Supreme Court Office of Attorney Regulation. As a trial attorney, he handled ethics violations on the part of Colorado licensed attorneys. Presently, in addition to representing injured parties, Mr. Pennywell is also a frequent presenter for National Business Institute at Continuing Legal Education (CLE) programs for attorney's at both the local and national levels.

Kenneth loves to travel and read. He is an admirer of water sports and enjoys water snorkeling in particular. Hawaii is among his favorite places that he's been able to visit and partake in water sport activities. Being from Louisiana, he especially enjoys cooking and eating Cajun food.

Mr. Pennywell has been an attorney with Franklin D. Azar & Associates, P.C. since June 2000. His areas of expertise include personal injury, civil litigation, and attorney ethics. Kenneth has extensive trial experience with over 150 jury, bench or administrative trials. He is a member of the Colorado Bar Association, Louisiana Bar Association and a former member of the National District Attorney Counsel.

attorneys.name: Chris Phillips
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Denver, CO
attorneys.bio:
Chris Phillips credits his mom and dad for his dedication and passion to service and to helping people. “My mother was a teacher, and my father was a Baptist minister. They were all about empowering and uplifting the community.” Chris says he got his value system from them, and that inspired a lifetime of helping others. Chris started as a teacher for Teach for America.

After graduating law school went to work as a public defender. In 2015, Chris moved to Colorado and worked for a few years representing insurance companies. This line of work eventually brought him to his true calling: personal Injury law.

Now, he has seen how insurance companies work and knows he is in a unique position to be able to know how to fight for someone that has been injured by no fault of their own.

Chris says if you are fighting for someone and you are passionate about what they are going through, you will get great results.

He is proud to work at McDivitt Law Firm where he says the firm believes in compassion and results and understands that the two ideas go hand in hand.

Chris loves the mountains and the Colorado weather. Coming from the flatlands of Mississippi, he says the view of the Rocky Mountains will never grow old.

Chris did his undergraduate work at The University of Michigan and got his law degree from Chicago Kent College of Law.

attorneys.firm_name: The Law Firm of Springer & Steinberg
attorneys.practice_type: Mergers and Acquisitions Lawyers in Denver, CO
attorneys.bio:
Charles J. Piechota, Esq., brings a wealth of expertise to his role as Special Counsel at Springer & Steinberg Law Firm, based in Denver, Colorado. With a multifaceted legal practice, Chuck is a distinguished professional specializing in mergers and acquisitions, real estate transactions, estate planning, trademarks and copyrights, and liquor licensing.

In the realm of mergers and acquisitions, Chuck is a trusted advisor, representing businesses across diverse industries. His portfolio also includes reorganizations, private offerings, corporate governance, and contract negotiation. Chuck’s strategic approach ensures that businesses receive comprehensive legal counsel, fostering growth and success.

A seasoned practitioner in estate planning, Chuck focuses on tax, gift, and business succession planning. His expertise extends to estate and trust administration. Clients benefit from Chuck’s meticulous approach to safeguarding their assets and ensuring a smooth transition of wealth.

In the complex landscape of intellectual property law, Chuck advises businesses, artists, and creators on trademark and copyright matters. He provides guidance on intellectual property protection and licensing, as well as overseeing registrations applications. Chuck’s commitment to innovation ensures that his clients’ creative endeavors are legally protected.

As a seasoned liquor licensing attorney, Chuck facilitates liquor license transactions of all kinds. He is a valuable resource for businesses navigating state and federal liquor regulation compliance. Chuck’s insight into this specialized area of law ensures his clients operate within legal parameters while thriving in the highly regulated liquor industry.

Before embarking on his legal career, Chuck served as a research assistant in Colorado State University’s Mycobacterium Research Lab, demonstrating his commitment to precision and excellence in his work.

As Special Counsel at Springer & Steinberg Law Firm, Chuck contributes to the firm’s reputation as a leading legal force in Denver. His diverse skill set, and client-centered approach make him an asset to individuals and businesses seeking comprehensive legal solutions.

For unparalleled legal guidance in mergers and acquisitions, estate planning, taxation, intellectual property, and liquor licensing, trust Charles J. Piechota and the accomplished team at Springer & Steinberg Law Firm. Your legal success starts with Chuck’s expertise and dedication.

attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Colorado Springs, CO
attorneys.bio:
Adam Pienciak is a senior associate on Robinson & Henry’s Criminal Defense team. He holds over ten years of experience exclusively as a criminal defense attorney.

Before joining R&H, Adam handled a wide variety of cases as a tenacious public defender, including DUI, high-profile sexual assaults, and first-degree murder. His perseverance in the courtroom has resulted in numerous favorable outcomes for clients in criminal defense, including family reunification. Adam prides himself in treating his clients with respect and kindness while passionately defending their rights and working toward obtaining the best possible resolution.

Representative matters:

Sexual assault charges dismissed – Defended client charged with multiple counts of sexual assault of a minor, thus securing a dismissal of all counts.

Successfully defended client at trial– Procured a not guilty verdict after a jury trial for a client accused of domestic assault, thus leading to the reunification of the client and their children.

Dangerous dog acquittal – Defended client charged with ownership of a dangerous dog during a jury trial, thus securing an acquittal and reunification of the client and their dog.

DUI charges dismissed – Successfully litigated the suppression of all evidence and a dismissal of a DUI case.

attorneys.name: Justin M. Plaskov
attorneys.practice_type: Employment Law (Employees) Lawyers in Denver, CO
attorneys.bio:
My practice focuses on meeting the needs of individuals who need assistance in negotiating contracts or want to level the playing field when faced with a difficult employment situation. I regularly consult with and represent employees from all industries and areas of employment-from entry-level workers to managers and highly-skilled professionals to executives and corporate officers.

Although reaching an amicable resolution is often in all parties' best interest, hiring an experienced litigator can force your employer to take your situation more seriously. Throughout my career, I have had significant success in obtaining large recoveries for my clients. Representative cases include:

Helping former employees of a large annuity company obtain a $20.5 million settlement in a pattern and practice case involving race and sex discrimination and retaliation. EEOC et al. v. Jackson National Life Insurance Company et al., Civil Action No. 16-cv-02472-PAB-SKC.

Obtaining a $485,000 settlement on behalf of a qui tam plaintiff who was terminated after complaining that his employer was fraudulently selling grenade launchers to the federal government.

Winning a jury verdict of nearly $15 million on behalf of seven low wage earners, who worked sorting mail for a private federal contractor. Camara, et. al. v. Matheson Trucking, Inc., et.al., 12-CV-03040 (D.Colo. 2015).

Representing the Town of Minturn in litigation and obtaining a $48 million settlement on behalf of the town against a developer. Town of Minturn v. Battle One Developer, LLLP, et al., 2022-CV-030050 (Eagle Dist. Ct. 2024)

In addition to litigation, I consult with clients to help them negotiate severance agreements and non-competition agreements and have extensive experience in providing consulting services for executives who need assistance to understand and negotiate contractual obligations and compensation packages.

Outside of the employment law context, I represent individuals in drafting wills, trusts, and other estate planning documents. I file and defend lawsuits involving estate planning issues; property disputes, including quiet title actions; breach of contract; construction defect; and several other legal claims.

I also represent businesses who need assistance with litigation, business disputes, administrative proceedings, corporate documents, and employment law specific documents (including employee handbooks, employee contracts, and employment law policies).

attorneys.name: Stephen J. Plog
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Greenwood, CO
attorneys.bio:
"In any divorce or custody case, nothing matters more than securing the best financial and emotional future for my clients and their children."

Stephen Plog is the co-founder of Plog & Stein, P.C family law firm in Denver, Colorado. Mr. Plog has practiced family law for nearly two decades and enjoys helping his clients navigate the legal process, as well as fighting for the best possible outcome for themselves and their families. Steve has a great amount of knowledge and experience related to divorce and child custody cases to share with his clients and he also enjoys both complex legal writing and litigating in the courtroom. AS he continues in his family law practice, Steve looks forward to helping clients with all family law needs.

Family law attorney Stephen Plog was born in Chicago, Illinois. After moving to different cities, his family settled in Las Cruces, New Mexico where he attended New Mexico State University. He graduated with a Bachelor’s Degree in Psychology and a supplemental pre-law minor. Steve completed one year of course work toward a graduate degree in Public Administration, but rather than finishing it, he decided to move East and begin his legal studies. Attorney Stephen Plog graduated from Quinnipiac University School of Law in 1997.

After obtaining his law degree, Mr. Plog moved back West to Colorado with his twin brother, who also graduated from law school. In 1998 they decided to start their own law firm. The same year, Steve met his partner, Laura Stein, and in 1999 they formed Plog & Stein, P.C.

Outside his law practice, Steve enjoys spending time with his wife and daughters. He also enjoys working around the house, golfing, being involved in his daughter’s swimming, and traveling with his family. Steve is an avid reader of trivia and useless facts and is considered to be a walking encyclopedia. He puts his semi-photographic memory to good use with his clients’ cases.

attorneys.name: Robert L. Pomper
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Denver, CO
attorneys.bio:
Robert L. Pomper started his legal career in Chicago and came from one of the largest family law firms where he was director of litigation. Not only did Mr. Pomper have his own full caseload where he successfully litigated or negotiated many complex divorce/custody cases, but he also managed cases for the entire office to ensure that the firm's clients and the attorneys were a successful team. He would meet regularly with the firm's attorneys to help employ effective strategies to suit the particular facts of the case and needs of the client. Over the 21 years he has been practicing, he has represented many satisfied clients and always believe that it is important to really listen to what is most important to your client. It is then key to set out an effective strategy with the understanding that this may change, as necessary, in light of the many variables involved in the case. Having a good, open dialogue with your client is one of the most effective, yet underutilized, tools in effective representation, says.....

Mr. Pomper was born and raised right outside of Chicago and graduated with honors from the University of Chicago where he majored in PERL, an acronym for Politics, Economics, Rhetoric and Law. He attended Tulane Law School and graduated near the top of his class. After practicing law in Chicago for 18 years, Mr. Pomper decided it was time to move to Colorado where he could be near the mountains and enjoy time outdoors. He is licensed in both Colorado and Illinois. He enjoys handling all aspects of family law, including contested cases involving children as well as complex financial cases. Robert handles cases all over the Denver metropolitan area as well as El Paso and Pueblo.

attorneys.name: Michael S. Porter
attorneys.firm_name: The Law Firm of Michael S. Porter, LLC
attorneys.practice_type: Whistleblower - Qui Tam Lawyers in Wheat Ridge, CO
attorneys.bio:
Michael Porter has significant experience in complex civil litigation, representing all facets of litigation, including the drafting of pleadings, motion practice, discovery, trial preparation, trials and appeals. Michael has prepared and tried in excess of 60 bench and jury trials and has participated in over 20 appeals to the Colorado Court of Appeals, the Colorado Supreme Court, the Tenth Circuit Court of Appeals, the Second Circuit Court of Appeals and the Fifth Circuit Court of Appeals. Michael also has prepared and settled short of trial hundreds of other civil claims or cases. Michael has the unique distinction of having tried two non-intervened False Claims Act cases to federal juries.

The federal False Claims Act (FCA) empowers whistleblowers to report fraud against the government and allows the whistleblower to collect 15-30% of the recovery. Michael has been litigating FCA or qui tam actions for 24 years. Michael’s successes include a $7.5M jury verdict concerning federal oil royalty fraud that resulted in a $26M settlement; an $18M settlement that resolved claims of Medicare/hospice fraud; a $6M settlement remedying gas royalty underpayments and a $4.5M settlement to resolve claims of customs fraud. Michael is a 1981 graduate from DU Law (top 15% of class) and has been actively litigating civil cases for the past 42 years. Michael has been recognized as one of America’s Top 100 Attorneys in Colorado.

Michael Porter has significant experience in complex civil litigation, representing all facets of litigation, including the drafting of pleadings, motion practice, discovery, trial preparation, trials and appeals. Michael has prepared and tried in excess of 60 bench and jury trials and has participated in over 20 appeals to the Colorado Court of Appeals, the Colorado Supreme Court, the Tenth Circuit Court of Appeals, the Second Circuit Court of Appeals and the Fifth Circuit Court of Appeals. Michael also has prepared and settled short of trial hundreds of other civil claims or cases. Michael has the unique distinction of having tried two non-intervened False Claims Act cases to federal juries.

The federal False Claims Act (FCA) empowers whistleblowers to report fraud against the government and allows the whistleblower to collect 15-30% of the recovery. Michael has been litigating FCA or qui tam actions for 24 years. Michael’s successes include a $7.5M jury verdict concerning federal oil royalty fraud that resulted in a $26M settlement; an $18M settlement that resolved claims of Medicare/hospice fraud; a $6M settlement remedying gas royalty underpayments and a $4.5M settlement to resolve claims of customs fraud. Michael is a 1981 graduate from DU Law (top 15% of class) and has been actively litigating civil cases for the past 42 years. Michael has been recognized as one of America’s Top 100 Attorneys in Colorado.

attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Denver, CO
attorneys.bio:
Joe Prieksat has been practicing civil plaintiff’s trial since 2011. Joe works hard to seek justice for the injured and devotes his time to handling a wide range of personal injury cases at McDivitt Law Firm. Joe grew up in South Dakota, Wyoming, and Colorado and returned here to the mountains to practice law and start a family.

“No two clients’ injuries are the same and no two sets of facts are the same,” he said. “But everybody deserves the same care, compassion and a chance to tell their story in pursuit of justice.” Joe prides himself on listening carefully to clients to better understand their story.

“What sets McDivitt Law Firm apart is that we treat our clients like family,” he said. “We truly level the playing field. The mission is to help ordinary people obtain access to justice in cases against big insurance companies, and we make sure every client is treated with dignity and respect.”

attorneys.practice_type: Car Accident Lawyers in Denver, CO
attorneys.bio:
Samantha L. Pryor is an attorney at The Halliburton Law Firm, LLC, who focuses her practice on car accidents, civil rights, personal injury, premises liability, wrongful termination – employee, employment law – employer, and litigation and appeals. In October of 2007, Mrs. Pryor was licensed to practice law. She has represented clients of various sizes in civil and commercial litigation matters in state and federal courts over the course of her career.

Mrs. Pryor has represented clients in a wide variety of legal settings, including trials before juries and judges, as well as in arbitrations, mediations, small claims court, and administrative law proceedings. She currently works in the areas of employment and personal injury litigation. Her cases involve issues like discrimination, harassment, retaliation, slip-and-falls, and traumatic brain injuries (TBIs).

Mrs. Pryor has substantial experience in the field of motions practice and has garnered high praise for her skillful legal research, analysis, and writing from judges, peers, and clients alike. She has a long track record of success in settling cases out of court through negotiation, often avoiding the need for mediators or other third parties.

attorneys.name: Gary B. Pulitzer
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce Lawyers in Louisville, CO
attorneys.bio:
Gary B. Pulitzer obtained his Bachelor of Arts from the University of Colorado in 1983. After obtaining valuable experience in the business world as an entrepreneur, Gary pursued his law degree from Touro College in Huntington, New York. Gary served as Notes and Comments Editor of the Law Review, and received his J.D. in 1992.

Gary has over 28 years' experience litigating family law cases. His practice is devoted to cases involving divorce, valuation of assets, divison of property, prenuptial and postnuptial agreements, and parental responsibility (custody).

Gary is a member of the Family Law Section of the Colorado Bar Association and the Adams, Broomfield, and Jefferson County Bar Associations.

Gary is also a certiofied mediator.

Gary believes most divorce cases can be resolved in mediation. Gary works with experienced and well respected experts to value real estate, investments, restricted stock units, stock options, trusts, and retirement accounts.

Gary believes child related issues can be resolved through negotiation and compromise so long as both parties focus on the children's best interests and have realistic expectations of the outcome of their case.

Through personal contact with the client, Gary works to assure that his clients achieve these goals as quickly as possible, whether by negotiation or litigation.

He started his legal career as a criminal prosecutor but eventually moved into private practice focusing on family law and divorce.

attorneys.name: Joseph Ramos MD, JD
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Northglenn, CO
attorneys.bio:
Joseph Ramos, M.D., draws upon the values of his small-town upbringing to assist victims of accidents caused by the negligence of other parties to get back on their feet and back to a normal way of life. As the owner of Ramos Law, located in Northglenn, Colorado, he provides representation to clients who have been harmed in cases involving motor vehicle accidents, pedestrian knockdowns, premises liability, dog bites, defective products and much more. Ramos helps people throughout the Denver metropolitan, Colorado Springs, and the Phoenix, Arizona areas.

After attending college, Dr. Ramos obtained his Doctor of Medicine from the University of Nevada, Reno School of Medicine in 1997. As a practicing physician, he found himself increasingly called upon by attorneys for both plaintiffs and defendants to provide expert medical testimony at medical malpractice and other personal injury trials. This experience led him to feel that he could be of even greater assistance to people if he obtained a law degree. Accordingly, Dr. Ramos enrolled at the University of Denver, Sturm College of Law and was awarded his Juris Doctor in 2009. He is admitted to practice before all Colorado and Arizona state courts.

This combination of medical expertise and legal training enables Dr. Ramos to clearly detail the severity of his clients' injuries. His ability to directly interpret medical records ensures the effective communication of their pain and disability to juries. This depth of detail strengthens cases. His efforts also convince juries to award sufficient funds to plaintiffs when cases go to trial. He further supports clients by identifying the exact amounts of coverage specified in insurance policies and working hard to obtain the compensation that victims need to help them get back to a normal way of life.

attorneys.name: Patricia Rankin
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Erie, CO
attorneys.bio:
Patricia Rankin practices primarily in the areas of estate planning, elder law, estate administration, probate, guardianships, and conservatorships. Prior to focusing on elder law and probate, Ms. Rankin practiced in the areas of Equal Employment Opportunity Claims, family law, and insurance subrogation. Ms. Rankin spent several years working for the probate court of the 17th Judicial District Court and has seen a wide variety of simple and complex matters for elder law and probate.

Ms. Rankin’s interest in estate planning stems from courtroom observations of guardianships, conservatorships, and estate administration disputes. In many instances, the families experience long-lasting effects from their grief. She is focused to assist families in creating estate plans to prevent the family anguish which occurs when there is no plan in place to care for aging family members or for managing an estate when they become deceased. She has experienced firsthand from her own family the challenges which arise for a family in making care decisions when the elderly is diagnosed with debilitating diseases such as Parkinson’s and Dementia.

Ms. Rankin is an active member of the Colorado Bar Association, Elder Law Section, and Trust and Estates Section. Ms. Rankin is currently serving on the Elder Law Section Executive Council and the 17th Judicial District Senior Law Committee. Ms. Rankin has taught numerous classes on estate planning basics, conservatorships, and common law marriage.

attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Greeley, CO
attorneys.bio:
I have been practicing law in Northern Colorado since 2007. I have spent countless hours in the court room negotiating cases, litigating complex motions issues and going to trial. I have tried cases from all levels of traffic offenses to first-degree murder to complex property crimes. My clients have been found not guilty of charges at all levels in the criminal defense system. Once I graduated from law school I moved to Greeley, Colorado and began working for the Colorado State Public Defenders System.

For as long as I can remember I have sought to learn the skills and develop the compassion necessary to help people in need.

attorneys.bio:
Amanda Reeves is an attorney and part of the Ciancio Ciancio Brown, P.C. family law team. Amanda has worked in the legal field for over 10 years, working in various areas of the law including bankruptcy and disability law. Since April 2017, Amanda has worked exclusively on family law matters.

Amanda believes there is no one-size-fits-all solution for people who find themselves facing divorce, the allocation of parental responsibilities, the modification of existing family law orders, or any other family law matter. Each client deserves to be heard and Amanda strives to understand each client's unique set of circumstances so that she can help them identify solutions that work for them.

Amanda works with a calm, professional demeanor to help her clients navigate the legal process with a solution-focused approach so that clients can get through their family law matter with as much ease as possible and begin the next phase of their lives.

When Amanda is not working on behalf of clients, she enjoys spending time with friends and family, and exploring the Colorado outdoors.

attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Denver, CO
attorneys.bio:
Carly Regal is an Associate Attorney at GEM Family Law, practicing in all areas of family law, including divorce, child custody, child support, and modification matters.

Carly earned her Juris Doctor from the University of Denver Sturm College of Law, graduating in the top 10% of her class and earning membership into the prestigious Order of the Coif. She also holds a master’s degree in social work from Case Western Reserve University, which educational background is invaluable to Carly’s understanding of child development and welfare in family law cases.

Prior to attending law school, Carly worked for the Department of Human Services and served as a school counselor, addressing children’s mental health and family needs on an intimate level. These roles reinforced her belief that family law should balance both legal strategy and emotional well-being—an approach that continues to shape her advocacy today.

Drawing on her background in social work and child development, Carly brings a compassionate and informed approach to helping families navigate life’s most challenging transitions. She is dedicated to reducing the emotional and financial stress that often accompanies family law disputes, guiding clients toward practical, sustainable solutions. Carly’s blend of empathy, legal acumen, and real-world experience makes her a trusted advocate for clients seeking clarity and peace of mind during difficult family transitions.

attorneys.name: Lindsay Reilly
attorneys.practice_type: Real Estate Lawyers in Fort Collins, CO
attorneys.bio:
Lindsay was born in southern California. When her family moved to Colorado in her early teen years, she fell in love with the front range and has called it home ever since, graduating from Arapahoe High School in 1999.

Lindsay earned her BA from Boston College in 2003 with an English major and a chemistry minor. After undergrad, she returned to Colorado, completing a Juris Doctor at the University of Colorado in 2006. Lindsay spent a year in a mid-sized Boulder firm specializing in corporate and real estate law before beginning a career as a prosecutor.

In 2007, Lindsay moved to Larimer County to join the District Attorney’s office for the Eighth Judicial District. There, Lindsay handled and tried a wide variety of cases from simple misdemeanors to first degree murder and other complicated felony matters. Lindsay worked extensively on drug prosecutions and was the impetus behind the DA’s office adding a full time drug trafficking prosecutor, as well as the first attorney assigned to that role. In that capacity, she collaborated with law enforcement and prosecutors in multiple jurisdictions on numerous investigations and subsequent prosecutions.

Lindsay was then promoted to Chief Deputy District Attorney and oversaw both the Intake division of the DA’s office as well as Central Services, where she collaborated with colleagues and law enforcement to file cases and assisted in ensuring proper delivery of discovery.

For most of her 13 years at the DA’s office, Lindsay was involved in training for local law enforcement on areas including courtroom testimony, domestic violence investigations, driving under the influence investigations, drug investigations, legal updates, and search and seizure. Throughout her time as a prosecutor, Lindsay was well-known for her commitment to cases, passion for helping people, attention to detail, and command of the courtroom.

In 2021, together with longtime prosecutor and colleague, David Vandenberg, Lindsay opened the doors to Reilly, Vandenberg & Biggers. Through the firm, the partners continue their commitment to relationships, the community, and justice.

Lindsay is a Consilium Practitioner; she is a member of Consilium, an organization dedicated to an integrated and wholistic approach to domestic relations cases.

Lindsay lives in Fort Collins with her husband, two children, and absurd doodle mix. In her free time she enjoys running, skiing, travel, and family game nights.

attorneys.name: Gregg Rich
attorneys.practice_type: Construction Defect Lawyers in Denver, CO
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Gregg S. Rich is a partner at Coombe Curry Rich & Jarvis, based in Denver, Colorado. He offers litigation services that encompass the areas of commercial law, construction defects, contract disputes, insurance coverage, and personal injury. He regularly tries cases in Colorado courts as well as through arbitrations. He also handles appeals in Colorado's appellate courts.

After earning a Bachelor of Arts degree in political science at Cal Poly Pomona and working as a haberdasher, Mr. Rich received his Juris Doctor degree from the University of Denver. A student member of the Phi Alpha Delta law fraternity, he served as part of the law school's trial and appellate moot court teams and as a student lawyer and research assistant for the Student Law Office, helping those accused of crimes and conducting outreach programs for women's shelters, seniors, and the homeless.

With a license to practice law in the state courts of Colorado, New York, Wyoming and Texas, Mr. Rich also is a member of the bars for the U.S. District Courts for the District of Colorado and the Southern District of New York, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the 10th Circuit and the Supreme Court of the United States. Besides lecturing the insurance industry and attorney groups on various topics, he also mentors young lawyers in trial techniques through the Colorado Defense Lawyers Association (CDLA) Trial Academy.

A certified litigation management professional, Mr. Rich has garnered several recognitions. He is AV Preeminent peer-review rated,* the highest rating, through Martindale-Hubbell, has been consistently recognized as a Super Lawyer, and has received the Defense Research Institute Exceptional Performance Citation. He participates in organizations such as the Colorado Bar Association, the Arapahoe County Bar Association, Claims Litigation Management, and the Judge William E. Doyle American Inn of Court.

A former executive board member of the CDLA (including as its President in 2017-2018), Mr. Rich volunteered his time as pro bono counsel to the board of the Communications Technology Professionals for many years. Ethical and knowledgeable, he provides client-focused solutions and efficiently guides clients while implementing the appropriate strategy tailored to their needs. His track record of active trial practice has earned him the respect of his peers and opposing lawyers.

attorneys.name: Lyndsey Richard
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Denver, CO
attorneys.bio:
Lyndsey focuses her legal practice on estate planning matters, working in close partnership with individuals and families. She helps clients determine their estate planning goals and develop wills, trusts and other essential legal documents, and to navigate their roles and legal responsibilities during the probate process or through trust administration. For some, planning for the future and caring for loved ones also means maneuvering around real estate or small business challenges, family conflicts or other complexities. Having nearly 2 decades of legal experience, Lyndsey taps into her early experience as a litigator of a broad range of probate, contract, personal, business, and real estate disputes in her counsel as an estate planning specialist.

In addition to working directly with our clients, Lyndsey is our firm's managing attorney, overseeing our team and legal practice, which she founded in 2011 after working at a prominent downtown Denver law firm for several years.

My Approach

Whether your circumstances are simple and straightforward or riddled with complexity, estate matters are always personal and extraordinarily meaningful. I know how crucial it is to connect with and understand my clients' unique needs. My role — and my responsibility — is to provide my clients with thoughtful, detailed, and timely assistance, using my years of experience as a guide. My strength is in helping my clients understand their options, and in mapping out a common-sense path that meets their goals.

In addition to being an attorney, I'm also a mother and a wife, a daughter, a sister; I know, personally, how difficult it can be to balance our many responsibilities and plan for uncomfortable contingencies. I also understand how crucial and comforting it is to have a tailored set of estate planning documents on which your family can rely.
