attorneys.name: Laura B Stein
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Greenwood, CO
attorneys.bio:
Laura Stein is one of the founding partners of Plog & Stein, P.C. and currently serves as the managing partner of the firm. Her legal career started in 1997 clerking in the Denver Probate Court for the former probate judge, the Honorable C. Jean Stewart. In 1998, Laura left this position to start her own law firm, Plog & Stein, P.C. focusing primarily on probate matters but also representing family law cases such as divorce, child custody and child support matters. Over the years, with the growth of Plog & Stein, P.C., Ms. Stein has eased into the role of managing the financial and business side of the firm, as well as tending to client relations matters. Though Laura currently doesn’t maintain a caseload, she is always available to provide advice to clients and offer support to our attorneys and staff.

Ms. Stein attended college at Tufts University in Boston, where she graduated with a degree in Clinical Psychology and Child Development. With a keen eye towards details and facts, Ms. Stein elected to attend law school in Nova Southeastern University in Florida. Before graduating early from law school in 1995, she engaged in an internship with the Internal Revenue Service. Ms. Stein is licensed to practice law in both Colorado and Florida.

Laura Stein is currently the primary point of contact should clients have questions regarding billing and other financial matters. In her spare time, Ms. Stein enjoys being with her family, traveling and volunteering for various athletic, educational or school related endeavors.

attorneys.name: Johnathan Stien
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Greeley, CO
attorneys.bio:
Johnathan grew up in north central Illinois, about an hour and a half northwest of Chicago. After graduating with his Bachelor of Arts in Law and Society from Purdue University in 2015, Johnathan began his trek west and stopped in South Dakota where he attended the University of South Dakota School of Law until graduating in early 2019.

While in law school, Johnathan had the opportunity to begin learning the ins and outs of the criminal justice system by interning with the Minnehaha County Office of the Public Advocate and the South Dakota Attorney General’s Office. Johnathan’s experiences at both offices strongly affirmed his desire to advocate on behalf of people who are going through the criminal justice system.

After law school, Johnathan moved to Colorado where he took the Colorado Bar Exam. From there, he spent a few months working for Robert Half Legal in Denver, CO, until joining McAdams Law Office in late 2019.

When out of the office, Johnathan enjoys exploring Colorado’s vast wilderness, photographing nature, watching one of his favorite sports teams, or visiting one of the local breweries or restaurants.

attorneys.name: Jonathan Stine
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Denver, CO
attorneys.bio:
Jonathan Stine is a Colorado native born in Colorado Springs. At a young age, Jonathan's family relocated to Douglas County. He grew up in Parker, Colorado and graduated from Ponderosa High School.

Jonathan attended the University of Colorado at Boulder where he received bachelor of the arts degrees in Sociology and Philosophy.

Jonathan received his Juris Doctorate from the University of Denver, Strum College of Law. During law school Jonathan clerked for the litigation department at Lottner, Ruben, Fishman, Brown & Saul, P.C.; for Judge Russell Carparelli at the Colorado Court of Appeals; and as corporate in-house counsel for Rock Bottom Corporation, formerly the owner of Rock Bottom Brewery, Chop House, and Old Chicago Restaurants.

After being admitted to the Colorado State Bar, and right at the beginning of the 2007 economic down-turn, Jonathan began practicing at a thriving bankruptcy law firm, Robert D. Bradley & Associates, in Southern Colorado. During his time there Jonathan managed the practice, filled cases and successfully obtained discharges for over 450 bankruptcy clients.

Jonathan takes a straight forward, practical, results driven approach to his client's cases with a focus on the specific needs of each client and unique facts of each case. He has successfully resolved hundreds personal injury cases and obtained millions of dollars for his clients. He has experience in motor vehicle accident, motorcycle accident, semi-truck accident, premise liability, traumatic brain injury, dog-bite, and wrongful death cases.

attorneys.name: Patricia Jo Stone
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Parker, CO
attorneys.bio:
Jo Stone is a Colorado native, whose grandparents were homesteaders in eastern Colorado. Jo has both her bachelors and masters degrees in English literature as well as her law degree from the University of Colorado in Boulder, CO. Jo's practice focuses on estate and business planning, although she also has an extensive background in litigation of all kinds, including commercial, business, and personal matters. Her diverse background and experience allows her to approach all legal matters in a very circumspect and comprehensive manner that is somewhat unique in relation to the narrowly-focused niche firms prevalent today. Jo’s diversity also allows her to develop long lasting relationships with a wide variety of clients who may need different legal assistance through the years.

In addition to practicing law, Jo is on the faculty of the Graduate School of Business at the University of Phoenix and has taught at a variety of other colleges and universities throughout her career in the areas of business and arts and sciences. Jo is an active member of the Rotary Club of Parker and has served as the Director of International projects, Director of Club Service, as well as holding various posts in Rotary District 5450. She is an active advocate of Rotary’s program to eradicate Polio worldwide.

Outside of the office, Jo and her husband, Jim, enjoy spending lots of time with their large family, as well as writing, music and travel.

attorneys.name: Martin Adam Stuart
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Denver, CO
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Stuart's practice focuses almost exclusively on criminal defense for individuals and entities in both Colorado State and Federal courts. Mr. Stuart is President-Elect of the Colorado Criminal Defense Bar, is appointed to the Governor's Sentencing Commission's Task Force on Incarceration, and is the chair of the Colorado Criminal Defense Bar's Policy Committee.

Mr. Stuart's experience in criminal defense includes the representation of thousands of clients for offenses ranging from possession of drugs to murder. Mr. Stuart has tried over 70 jury trials including acquittals on charges from first degree murder to sexual assault on a child to drug distribution to kidnapping and robbery. Prior to the founding of his firm in August of 2003, Mr. Stuart work for nearly five years as a Deputy State Public Defender. Mr. Stuart has been named a rising star in the upcoming 2009 Super Lawyer rankings. Now with a brisk state and federal criminal defense practice, Mr. Stuart represents clients in most Colorado Counties from Denver to Las Animas to Eagle and in federal courts from the United States District of Colorado to the Supreme Court of the United States.

Mr. Stuart is a member of the National Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers, the Colorado Criminal Defense Bar, the Denver Bar Association, the Colorado Bar Association, and the United States District of Colorado Criminal Justice Act Panel. Mr. Stuart has been admitted to the Colorado State Bar, the United States District of Colorado, the United States Court of Appeals for the Tenth Circuit, and the Supreme Court of the United States. He received his juris doctorate from the University of Denver School of Law where he won the prestigious Hoffman Cup trial competition and received his undergraduate degree from Whittier College in California. Mr. Stuart was born in the United Kingdom to American citizens and raised in Fresno, California.

Mr. Stuart is a member of the National Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers, the Colorado Criminal Defense Bar, the Denver Bar Association, the Colorado Bar Association, and the United States District of Colorado Criminal Justice Act Panel. Mr. Stuart has been admitted to the Colorado State Bar, the United States District of Colorado, the United States Court of Appeals for the Tenth Circuit, and the Supreme Court of the United States. He received his juris doctorate from the University of Denver School of Law where he won the prestigious Hoffman Cup trial competition and received his undergraduate degree from Whittier College in California. Mr. Stuart was born in the United Kingdom to American citizens and raised in Fresno, California.

attorneys.name: Adeline M. Sulentich
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Denver, CO
attorneys.bio:
Adeline is an attorney, licensed in both Colorado and Illinois, who practices exclusively in family law. Adeline counsels her clients on numerous aspects of divorce and child-related proceedings, including parenting time and decision-making responsibilities, child support, spousal support, property division, grandparent visitation, and adoption proceedings, among other things.

While Adeline appreciates the need for litigation in some matters, she realizes that families often benefit greatly from settlement and promotes alternative dispute resolution processes, such as mediation and arbitration. Adeline helps her clients focus on the big picture while customizing her approach to every client’s individual needs, as there is no “one size fits all” for families. Regardless of the approach, Adeline is a fierce advocate for her clients inside and outside of the court room.

Aside from her litigation work, Adeline does work as a parent coordinator and decision-maker (PCDM), represents the best interests of children (CLR), and conducts child and family investigations (CFI).

Adeline’s legal acumen was recognized by the University of Illinois-Chicago, John Marshall School of Law, where she graduated cum laude with a certificate in Trial Advocacy.

During law school, Adeline gained invaluable family law experience as a judicial extern with the Honorable Regina Scannicchio in the Cook County Domestic Relations Division. Adeline’s experience working directly with a domestic relations judge provided her unique insight into how to prepare for and present a family law case. She later became a law clerk at one of Chicago’s premiere family law firms, serving clients in complex divorce and family law matters.

Adeline’s passion for family law and child welfare began even prior to law school, when she worked with Court Appointed Special Advocates (CASA) at the Harmony House, supervising court-ordered visits between children and non-custodial adults in their lives. Working at Harmony House provided Adeline with a unique skill-set that she has incorporated into her family law practice. Adeline’s work is also deeply influenced by her own experience as a child of high-conflict divorce; her compassion and insight in this regard is highly valuable to her clients.

Adeline is a Colorado native who graduated from Colorado State University before attending law school in Chicago. Outside of practicing family law, Adeline spends her free time with her family, outside playing pickleball or volleyball, reading, walking her dog, hiking, doing water sports, and much more.

attorneys.name: Eric A Sunness
attorneys.firm_name: Eric A. Sunness, Attorney at Law, LLC
attorneys.practice_type: DUI Lawyers in Fort Collins, CO
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Sunness has handled thousands of cases in Northern Colorado. Mr. Sunness joined Frey, Korb, Haggerty & Michaels, P.C. as an associate in 1995 and became a shareholder in 1998. Mr. Sunness has represented and counseled a wide range of clients for 25 years, and has extensive experience in handling criminal defense cases, and DUI law. Mr. Sunness is a member of the Colorado Bar Association, Larimer County Bar Association, and Colorado Trial Lawyers Association. He presently serves on the Larimer County Bar Association Professionalism Committee.

Mr. Sunness graduated in 1992 with a Juris Doctor degree from the Thomas M. Cooley Law School in Lansing, Michigan. While attending law school, Mr. Sunness served as a legal intern at Sixty Plus, Inc, Elder law Clinic of the Thomas M. Cooley Law School, and served as a law clerk for Abood & Doyle, PC. Mr. Sunness was also a member of the Thomas M. Cooley Law School Trial Team, served as a Professor's Assistant in the Trial Workshop program, and was on the Dean's List.

In 1982, he received his Bachelor of Science degree from the State University of New York, College at Brockport. Prior to attending law school, Mr. Sunness worked for the New Jersey Nets Basketball Team as assistant to the public relations director, and sold fine printing paper for Horwitz Paper Company, Elmira, New York, and Alling & Cory Paper Company, Syracuse, New York.

Mr. Sunness is married and has three children. He is also active in his community. He has served as president of Fort Collins Youth Lacrosse and vice-president of Northern Colorado Youth Hockey. He was named Coach of the Year by Colorado State University, and for the Western Region of the American Collegiate Hockey Association. In his spare time he enjoys playing the electric bass guitar and listening to music.

attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Evergreen, CO
attorneys.bio:
Andrew Synchef is an attorney with experience spanning litigation, negotiation, regulatory compliance, and legal research across both private practice and public-sector settings. His work focuses on complex family law matters and personal injury cases including legal analysis, drafting and negotiation and advising on risk, compliance, and dispute resolution matters.

Andrew has supported litigation and regulatory matters through comprehensive legal research, motion drafting, and case strategy development. He has extensive trial experience and has experience preparing appeals, discovery materials, memoranda, and client-facing analyses, as well as reviewing contracts and advising on statutory and regulatory requirements.

In addition to his litigation and research experience, Andrew has extensive medical industry work experience which contribute to his compassionate and professional representation of personal injury clients. Andrew brings a detail-oriented, analytical approach to his practice, with a strong emphasis on precision, professionalism, and practical problem-solving.

Andrew earned his Juris Doctor from Whittier Law School, where he developed a strong foundation in legal writing, advocacy, and statutory interpretation. He is admitted to practice law in Colorado and Illinois. Andrew is the proud father of two wonderful children and two amazing dogs. In his free time, Andrew enjoys playing hockey, mountain biking and spending quality time with family and friends.

attorneys.name: Alisha Nicole Taibo Coombe
attorneys.practice_type: Child Support Lawyers in Centennial, CO
attorneys.bio:
Alisha Taibo Coombe earned her Juris Doctorate at the University of Colorado Law School in 2009 and was admitted to practice in Colorado the same year. She also graduated Summa Cum Laude with a Bachelor of Arts degree in Communication from Regis University in Denver, Colorado. Prior to pursuing a career in law, Alisha worked at Janus Capital Group for seven years, ending her finance career as a research associate on the investment team. Alisha served in the U.S. Army for four years.

While in law school, Alisha interned at the Boulder District Attorney's office, prosecuting DUI and Minor in Possession cases. Alisha participated on the CU trial team and the moot court competition, and coached other mock trial teams, leading one team to the number one spot in a competition between rival law schools CU and DU.

Alisha practiced as a student attorney in the CU Legal Aid Clinic; a non-profit legal program which provides legal representation to poor Coloradans. Since passing the Bar, Alisha has represented clients in all types of domestic disputes, general civil litigation, and complex construction litigation cases. Alisha is dedicated to helping victims of domestic violence and previously served on the Board of Directors at Gateway Battered Women's Services. She is a regular volunteer on KUSA Channel 9 Law Line and the Arapahoe County Bar Association pro se free legal aid clinic. Alisha serves as the Continuing Legal Education Committee Chair with the Arapahoe Bar Association and volunteers with the Judicial Nomination Commission of the Colorado Women’s Bar Association.

attorneys.name: Leonard D. Tanis Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Broomfield, CO
attorneys.bio:
After graduating from college, I studied at New Brunswick Theological Seminary for two years in a Master of Arts program in Theology. Tired of academia, I worked for a major retail shoe company as a management trainee in New Jersey for a year, then travelled the country for six weeks In 1974, settling finally in Boulder, where I resumed working in retail sales at Thornton Shoes on Pearl Street in Boulder prior to Pearl Street becoming a Mall. I changed careers in 1976 and began working in restaurants. Beginning as a busboy, I worked my way to Manager and then Regional Supervisor of five restaurants.

In 1990, intent on finding a career where I could really make a difference in people's lives, I entered the University of Denver College of Law. During law school, I was awarded membership in the Order of St. Ives Honor Society, the American Jurisprudence Award in 1992 for Administrative Law, and the Bureau of National Affairs, Inc., BNA Law Student Award at graduation. I also served as a Technical Editor of the University of Denver Law Review. During his final year in law school, I interned for Judge Donald Cordova in the United States Bankruptcy Court for the District of Colorado in Denver, where I gained valuable knowledge of the behind the scenes working of the courts. I obtained my Juris Doctorate in 1993, graduating eighth in my class.

I began my professional law career as a Law Clerk for Frascona and Joiner, P.C., in June 1991 and then moved to the law firm of Cooper & Cooper, P.C., in March 1992, again as a law clerk until being admitted to the practice of law as an attorney in October 1993. At Cooper & Cooper, P.C., we did about equal amounts of commercial litigation and family law related work. In late 1995, Bob Cooper asked me to be his partner and we agreed that specializing in one area of law would provide the best service for clients. Thus, in January 1996, the firm was renamed Cooper & Tanis, P.C., and we began specializing in family law. Bob and I have continued working together since then, committed to assisting people as they work through family law issues of every kind: divorce, custody (Allocation of Parental Rights), child support, maintenance, guardianships and probate.

In my leisure time, I enjoy cooking, walking my dog, reading and spending time with my family. An interesting fact about me is that both of my daughters were adopted from Chile.

Timothy G. Tarr is an associate attorney with Ciancio Ciancio Brown, P.C. and a member of the Personal Injury and Criminal Defense Teams. Tim was a Staff Editor for the Criminal Law Review, Head Student Representative for Themis Bar Review, and Treasurer for the Student Trial Lawyers Association.

A Colorado Native, Tim enjoys spending time in the Rocky Mountains, he is an avid hometown sports fan, and he finds great pride in helping the people of Colorado navigate the legal system during difficult times in their lives.

attorneys.name: Alexandra Cochran Taylor
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Denver, CO
attorneys.bio:
Allie counsels individuals and families, helping them understand and navigate the law, develop comprehensive plans to care for their loved ones, transfer assets, and clarify and manage their responsibilities during probate. Allie has worked with our team for nearly a decade, beginning as a legal intern during law school before joining our firm as an associate attorney after graduation. Allie has worked with clients across the front range from diverse backgrounds, affluence, and individual estate planning experience; she offers a fresh perspective and strategic, sound, and approachable sensibility.

My Approach

While necessary, planning for the future can sometimes be uncomfortable and confusing. Many people have misconceptions about the law or feel intimidated by it. Estate planning might also be the first instance in a client's life where they have hired an attorney. Some clients are also, understandably, reluctant to think about what their wishes would be in the event of a life-altering accident or death.

I'm honored to support and advocate for so many individuals and families, whether we're having meaningful discussions about their estate planning or when I am helping manage an unfortunate turn of events in a client's life. I'm grateful to help bring light and clarity to these situations, to make sure my clients know they are heard, and that I will work diligently to further their goals.

My Community

Born and raised in Colorado, I love the ease and beauty of living in the foothills of Arvada with my husband, Brooks, our young children, and our rescue animals, Annie Oakley, Wyatt Earp, and Doc Holliday. We often explore the parks and trails near our home, visit local breweries with family and friends, or go hiking and camping in the state and national parks in the Rocky Mountains. I love sports and am an avid fan of most local Colorado professional teams and the South Carolina Gamecocks. I also enjoy cultivating my backyard garden, staying active with various fitness and outdoor challenges, practicing my cello, and reading current events and historical and political non-fiction.

Supporting underserved populations is important to me, whether volunteering at local animal shelters or working across language barriers to advocate for working-class and immigrant communities. I am active with the Tribal Wills Project at the Sturm College of Law, which provides pro bono estate planning counsel to Navajo, Ute, and Crow Nation families and individuals. Just as with our law office clients, Tribal Wills works to clarify ever-fluctuating state and federal laws and help these folks develop comprehensive and empowered estate plans.

attorneys.name: Brenda L. Teig
attorneys.practice_type: Real Estate Lawyers in Niwot, CO
attorneys.bio:
Brenda L. Teig has practiced law in both the public and private sector for over 25 years. As an undergraduate student at the University of Northern Iowa, Brenda studied Public Administration with an emphasis in Public Services and was a member of the honor society Omicron Delta Kappa. In 1997, she received her J.D. from the University of Oregon Law school where she obtained a Trusts and Estate Certificate.

After clerking for Clark County District Court, Brenda worked in Las Vegas creating and developing Pro Se Clinics in conjunction with the newly established William S. Boyd School of Law school. While in private practice in San Francisco, she represented artists and athletes including the Estate of Tupac Shakur, as well as, served as a member of the California Bar Examination Wills & Trust committee developing consensus answers and grading bar applicant essay questions. She later worked as a Public Interest attorney in Salt Lake City where she also taught a course on Not-For-Profit Organizations at S.J. Quinney Law School.

Over the course of her legal career, Brenda has been a member of several local Bar Associations, served on a number of nonprofit Board of Directors including Children First of the Rockies in Longmont. In 2010 she was recognized by the Utah State Bar as Pro Bono Legal Aid Attorney of the Year.

Brenda lives in Niwot with her husband, two dogs and two kids. She currently serves as President of the Niwot High School Boosters and is a member of the Left-Hand Giving Circle.

attorneys.name: Lance P. Thibert
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Fort Collins, CO
attorneys.bio:
Lance P. Thibert knows that criminal cases do not occur in a vacuum and are often a snapshot of a person’s worst day. Often times the criminal legal process can feel judgmental, humiliating, and dehumanizing. Lance fiercely believes that the dignity of each person must be respected regardless of the accusation against them.

Lance’s career as a criminal defense trial attorney has involved representation of clients in nearly 4500 cases to date. Lance spent 6 years working as a Senior Deputy Public Defender in Larimer County and in that time gained extensive litigation and trial experience working cases encompassing Driving under the Influence, Theft, Domestic Violence, firearm-related charges, Drug Possession/Distribution, Arson, Burglary, Assault, and Homicide. Lance has taken innumerable cases to trial and achieved a favorable outcome.

Lance’s experience is not limited to the trial courtroom. Lance has been responsible for submitting briefs to the Court of Appeals that went on to produce published opinions along with writing hundreds of legal motions in County and District Court dealing with complex legal issues.

Lance has also acted as a mentor and instructor to aspiring and newly minted lawyers. He has trained several attorneys who have gone on to become excellent trial attorneys. Lance has acted as the subject matter expert in the area of DUI Litigation for the Fort Collins Regional Public Defender Office and has taught many training sessions on nearly every aspect of DUI litigation.

Lance also worked as one of the Public Defender representatives in the DUI Recovery Court in Larimer County. Lance has also filled the same role in a substitute capacity for similar treatment courts including Drug Court, Wellness (Mental Health) Court, and Juvenile Drug Court.

Lance earned his Juris Doctorate from University of Nebraska School of Law and has a Bachelor’s of Arts in Political Science and History from the University of Colorado, Denver. Lance is of counsel to Haltzman Law Firm and is a Fort Collins native. In his spare time Lance enjoys hiking, outdoor rock climbing, and playing ice hockey.

She received her B.A. in English Literature at Smith College in 2006 and M.A. in International Peace and Security at King’s College London in 2007.

When not in the office, you will likely find Ms. Thomasson backcountry skiing, mountain biking, or rock climbing with her boyfriend.

Kyle joined Abrams & Associates, LLC in July of 2019 and immediately played an important role achieving his client’s litigation goals. Kyle continues to grow as a lawyer, gaining substantial experience in construction, business, real estate, and family law and developing his talents as a legal researcher and advocate for his clients. His strengths include deep analysis of complicated legal issues and evaluating the intangible consequences of legal strategies with his clients. Kyle has quickly proven himself as an invaluable contributor to the continued and growing success of Abrams & Associates, LLC.

Kyle hails from Des Moines, Iowa. He relocated in Denver for the outdoor lifestyle Colorado affords, including hiking, fishing, and rock climbing. Kyle received his Juris Doctor from University of Oregon Law School where he was the Editor of Technology for the esteemed Journal of Environmental Law and Litigation. Kyle’s emphasis during law school was in environmental and natural resource law, and he participated in the school’s Natural Resource Law clinic. He was also a frequent contributor to the school’s Environmental Law Conference.

Kyle began in environmental law, and continues to show a passion for environmental justice. This unique perspective is an invaluable contribution to clients involved with large-scale real estate and construction projects, which often implicate environmental rules and regulations.

attorneys.name: Nathaniel Thompson
attorneys.practice_type: Bankruptcy Lawyers in Denver, CO
attorneys.bio:
Nathaniel Thompson brings more than a decade of experience to the firm’s bankruptcy practice. Having handled the full spectrum of bankruptcy filings, Nate is poised to help his clients obtain sustained financial relief.

Before joining R&H, Nate successfully ran his own law office, where he assisted clients with consumer and nonconsumer bankruptcies, business winddowns, debt settlement, and dischargeability adversary actions. Given his successful track record, potential clients can be confident that Nate will take a careful and comprehensive approach to their cases.

Nate has a wealth of knowledge and insight to offer clients. His experience and familiarity with federal bankruptcy procedures enable him to put his clients’ needs first.

Representative matters:

Chapter 7 Bankruptcy – Successfully discharged six figures of consumer debt by ensuring clients’ eligibility, complete and accurate filings, maximizing exemptions, and avoiding actions that could have led to a denial of discharge.

Chapter 13 Bankruptcy – Successfully obtained bankruptcy payment plan by demonstrating its feasibility, compliance with all legal requirements, and the client’s ability to follow the plan.

Business Winddown – Assisted client in the orderly dissolution of the business by advising client through operational shutdown, asset liquidation, and debt settlement best practices.

Dischargeability Adversary Actions – Defended client from creditor attempting to dismiss the client’s bankruptcy discharge by demonstrating the creditor’s failure to meet the burden of proof necessary for a judge to deny discharge.

attorneys.bio:
Jon Topolewski is a distinguished partner at Robinson & Henry where he spearheads the firm’s Personal Injury and Insurance Claim Denial practices. His strategic and tenacious approach as a litigator, coupled with a genuine compassion for his clients, has yielded millions of dollars in relief from personal injury and bad faith claims.

Jon has taken on deceitful water purification companies whose products damaged Coloradans’ property and put their health at risk. He has fought and won against multi-million-dollar insurance companies acting in bad faith. With extensive experience at every stage of litigation, from negotiation to trial, Jon consistently delivers favorable resolutions for individuals and companies.

Jon joined Robinson & Henry as a civil litigation attorney, bringing a vast skillset across numerous practice areas. His diverse expertise continually elevates the caliber of representation provided.

Representative matters

Secured $1.5M settlement - Negotiated a $1.5 million settlement for a car accident victim with brain and neck injuries. Discovered an extra $1 million umbrella policy through thorough investigation and pursued a case against the insurer for not disclosing full coverage.

Reversed claim denial - Negotiated a $130,000 settlement from three insurance carriers for a client injured in a scooter-car accident, overturning initial claim denials by leveraging Colorado insurance laws and presenting compelling evidence.

attorneys.name: Jennifer Torres
attorneys.firm_name: Frank Azar Car & Truck Accident Lawyers - Aurora, Colorado
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Aurora, CO
attorneys.bio:
"The Latina in me is an ember that blazes forever." - Sonia Sotomayor, Supreme Court Justice

Jennifer Torres was born in Los Angeles, California but raised in Aurora, Colorado. When she joined Frank Azar & Associates in August 2015, it was apparent she was a gifted attorney. Ms. Torres decided in her sophomore year of high school that she would be an attorney. She saw the enormous effect that the law can have on a society and how it perpetuated through different political administrations. It caused her to be a strong believer that the law shaped society and her work as an attorney could contribute to that social change and improvement.

attorneys.name: Judge Jennifer Torrington (Ret.)
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Denver, CO
attorneys.bio:
The Honorable Judge Jennifer Torrington (Ret.) is a retired Colorado district court judge with more than two decades of judicial experience. Judge Torrington (Ret.) served with distinction as a judicial officer in Denver from 2004 through 2025, presiding over a wide range of matters in the domestic, civil, criminal, and juvenile divisions. During her time on the bench, Judge Torrington (Ret.) developed a particular passion for family law and compassion for the litigants involved in family law matters.

Throughout her judicial career, much of Judge Torrington (Ret.)’s work focused on families and children involved in the legal system. Her experience overseeing complex and emotionally sensitive cases has given her deep insight into the challenges individuals face during family law disputes and other difficult legal matters.

Judge Torrington (Ret.) is widely respected for her thoughtful and balanced approach to resolving disputes. Drawing on her years on the bench, she works to ensure that every party has the opportunity to be heard while encouraging solutions that are fair, practical, and focused on long-term outcomes.

In addition to her work on the bench, Judge Torrington (Ret.) has been an active leader within the Colorado legal community. She has presented at numerous legal education programs, including the American Academy of Matrimonial Lawyers, the Family Law Institute, and the Colorado Judicial Conference. She has also served on the Colorado Child Support Commission and the Judicial Well-Being Committee, and she co-chaired the Licensed Legal Paraprofessionals Subcommittee of the Colorado Supreme Court Advisory Committee.

Judge Torrington (Ret.) was honored with the Distinguished Jurist Award from the American Academy of Matrimonial Lawyers, Colorado Chapter, in recognition of her contributions to the family law community. She has also received recognition for her work advancing access to justice and improving legal services in Colorado.

Judge Torrington (Ret.) is passionate about helping families resolve matters through alternative dispute resolution and offers mediation services, arbitration, and private judge appointments.

She also remains committed to mentoring attorneys and supporting the legal community, including through the Metro Volunteer Lawyers Program and mentorship of judges assigned to domestic divisions.

attorneys.name: Peter Towsky
attorneys.practice_type: Business Representation Lawyers in Highlands Ranch, CO
attorneys.bio:
Peter Towsky is an esteemed senior associate on the firm’s Civil Litigation, Real Estate & Business Law Teams.

Peter handles various legal matters, including contract disputes, HOA problems, and real estate issues. He also helps clients with intellectual property needs, including trademark registration and copyright enforcement.

Peter began his career as a prosecutor, handling thousands of criminal cases in the Violent Criminal Enterprises Bureau and the Gun Violence Suppression Division with the Brooklyn (New York) District Attorney’s Office. He aided in the indictment of 18 gang members on 41 charges related to various murders, shootings, and conspiracy to commit murder.

Prior to joining Robinson & Henry, Peter conducted nine criminal jury trials for the 10th Judicial District Attorney’s Office in Pueblo, where he obtained seven convictions and no acquittals.

Peter draws on this vast trial experience to inform his approach to a spectrum of litigation challenges.

Representative matters

Lawsuit dismissal - Successfully negotiated client’s dismissal from $1 million lawsuit involving wrongful allegations of sexual assault

Unjust enrichment - Obtained motion for summary judgment on client’s behalf, receiving treble damages for civil theft and breach of contract

HOA dispute - Negotiated favorable settlement for client sued by HOA several years after receiving bankruptcy discharge

Fraudulent transfer - Obtained more than $200,000 in damages total for client ghosted by homeowner on the hook for a purchase and sale agreement

HOA dispute - Negotiated settlement for client with reasonable disability accommodation requests of hostile HOA

Awards and Honors

Honors

#3 Most Jury Trials Conducted in Kings County (Brooklyn) Criminal Court, 2015

attorneys.name: Tony D. Tracy
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Denver, CO
attorneys.bio:
Tony Tracy was the second person in his extended family to graduate college. After graduating from Drake University with a degree in Broadcasting, he was ready for the next challenge. Because of his previous volunteer efforts, Tony knew he wanted to practice an area of law where he would be able to help the less fortunate.

“I don’t think the average person really understands the legal system or gets the equal access to the justice system that we’re all supposed to have,” Tony said. “And that was really important to me.” He explored several different practice areas when he was in law school in Nebraska. But personal injury, workers’ compensation and social security were his heart. “It was an opportunity where I could help regular people — people like me,” he said.

Tony approaches each client as an individual. “No two people are the same,” he said. He likes to listen to clients’ stories and get to know them. He picks up on details and notices things in the narratives that can help his clients’ cases.

Tony chooses to work at the McDivitt Law Firm because he likes the culture in the office. “People are outstanding,” he said. “You don’t feel stress from other people even when you have a busy workday. I also love that the clients always have access to us.”

attorneys.name: Tamara E. Trujillo
attorneys.practice_type: Elder Law Lawyers in Denver, CO
attorneys.bio:
Tamara Trujillo began practicing elder law and joined Chayet & Danzo, LLC in December 2009. She works as the Senior Managing Attorney in the areas of elder law, contested guardianships and conservatorships, complex estate litigation, probate administration, and estate planning. Ms. Trujillo is also an adjunct professor in Elder Law at the University of Colorado School of Law with Marco Chayet.

Ms. Trujillo has earned the distinction as a Certified Elder Law Attorney by the National Elder Law Foundation and is a former director of the National Academy of Elder Law Attorneys (2016-2020). Ms. Trujillo was named a 2022 & 2023 Super Lawyers Rising Star for her work in Elder Law, as well as being recognized by her peers in 5280 Magazine as a Top Elder law attorney. Ms. Trujillo is also a member of the Colorado Bar Association's Elder Law and Trust and Estate Sections. She has served on the Elder Law Section Executive Council since 2010 and is a member of the Denver Bar Association.

Ms. Trujillo received her Juris Doctor from Valparaiso University School of Law where she was active in the Trial Advocacy Program, the Client Counseling Program, the Volunteer Income Tax Program and assisted clients through Valparaiso's Low Income Taxpayer Clinic.

Ms. Trujillo earned her undergraduate degree from The Ohio State University. She grew up in the Denver area, graduating from Colorado Academy, and now resides in Parker, Colorado with her family. She enjoys hiking, horseback riding, reading, and traveling.

attorneys.name: Hans Christian Tuft
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Colorado Springs, CO
attorneys.bio:
Hans Christian Tuft was born in Sandy, Utah in 1977. He attended the University of Utah and San Jose State University, where he graduated Cum Laude with a bachelor of arts. While at San Jose State University, Mr. Tuft was awarded the President’s Scholar Award, the Dean’s Scholar Award, and the Highest History Honors Thesis Grade award and was a member of the University’s rugby team. Mr. Tuft attended law school at the University of Colorado School of Law in Boulder, Colorado, where he earned the Jules Milstein Law Fund Scholarship and served as Resource Editor on the Board of Editors for the University of Colorado Law Review. While at the University of Colorado, Mr. Tuft was a member of the schools legal aid and natural resources clinics. Mr. Tuft graduated from law school in 2005. attorneys.name: Rachel Tumin
attorneys.practice_type: Employment Law (Employees) Lawyers in Denver, CO
attorneys.bio:
I am an associate attorney at Plaskov Prescott & Moore, LLP, where my practice focuses on representing employees and advising employers on their duties to employees. As examples, since joining PPM, I have represented individuals and businesses in lawsuits and arbitration hearings on trade secret, non-competition, and whistleblower actions; negotiated settlements for employees in disputes with their employers; and brought charges of discrimination, harassment, and retaliation with the Colorado Civil Rights Division and Equal Employment Opportunity Commission. I also draft employee handbooks and agreements, and counsel employers on all of these topics and more, such as paid leave and COVID-related matters. Besides my employment practice, I represent clients in a variety of civil litigation proceedings, including business matters and real estate. Often, I consult and assist clients with reaching resolutions before litigation begins, through negotiation and mediation.

I have built my career on protecting civil rights. During law school, I worked with the ACLU of Colorado and Killmer, Lane and Newman, LLP, on cases spanning Constitutional and statutory rights, including: free speech, search and seizure, due process and access to justice, civil asset forfeiture, discrimination, and wage issues. After graduating from the University of Denver Sturm College of Law with honors, a certificate in Constitutional Rights and Remedies, and Public Good Distinction, I served as a law clerk to the Hon. Robert L. McGahey, Jr. in Colorado's 2nd Judicial District. While clerking on an exclusively civil docket, I participated in two dozen trials and hearings and worked on all types of disputes, from medical malpractice to civil rights to appeals from administrative agencies.

attorneys.name: Bob Turner
attorneys.firm_name: Frank Azar Car & Truck Accident Lawyers - Colorado Springs, Colorado
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Colorado Springs, CO
attorneys.bio:
"Education is what you get by reading the fine print, experience is what you get when you don't. A good lawyer has one or the other. A great lawyer has both."

Bob Turner was born in a small farming town in eastern Ohio. He learned the value of hard work at a young age, being taught to add and subtract riding the milk truck with his father. He obtained an A.B. degree from Dartmouth College in 1970 and a J.D. from the University of Denver in 1973. Mr. Turner has been an advocate for the cause of injured workers' rights and has been one of the name partners in several practices before joining Franklin D. Azar & Associates.

Bob's first job was with Lansford F. Butler (Lance), who was the father of Claimant's workers' compensation practice. Lance mentored Bob and played a great role in helping him become the attorney he is today. Among his noted accomplishments, Mr. Turner played a role in the development of the Colorado Bar Association (CBA) Workers Compensation Section and the Workers Compensation Education Association in the mid-80s.

Bob Turner has been admitted to practice in Colorado and the U.S. District Court for Colorado and the Court of Appeals since 1973. He is also a member of the Colorado Trial Lawyers Association (CTLA).

In 2002, he was honored as the recipient of the Lansford F. Butler Award given by the CBA for outstanding and continuing service to the workers compensation bar.

Bob has served on various committees for the Director's Office of the Colorado Bar Association. He also testified as an expert before the state legislature of Colorado and in the U.S. District Court on workers' compensation matters. Mr. Turner has tried over 2000 cases in his 45 years of practicing workers' compensation.

When he has free time, Bob enjoys spending time with his wife and five kids. He also spends time trying to improve his golf game. Bob is passionate about the rights of injured workers and believes the practice of law is best accomplished with dignity and professionalism.

attorneys.name: Keith D. Vance
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Colorado Springs, CO
attorneys.bio:
With nearly 30 years of experience in personal injury litigation, Keith Vance is one of Colorado’s most seasoned and respected trial attorneys. He is one of only five attorneys in Colorado who are Board Certified in Civil Trial Law by the National Board of Trial Advocacy, a distinction he has held since 2013. This national certification reflects his extensive courtroom experience, mastery of trial law, and unwavering ethical standards.

Mr. Vance devotes his practice exclusively to representing individuals who have been seriously injured due to the negligence or misconduct of others. His areas of expertise include:

Automobile, semi-truck, and motorcycle collisions

Nursing home negligence and elder abuse

Insurance bad faith

Premises liability and dangerous property conditions

Keth has successfully litigated complex personal injury cases involving traumatic brain injuries, spinal cord injuries, paralysis (quadriplegia and paraplegia), amputation, orthopedic trauma involving shoulders, knees, neck and back, and severe psychological injuries—securing millions upon millions of dollars in compensation for his clients.

Over the course of his distinguished career, Mr. Vance has taken over 70 cases to jury verdict, demonstrating a depth of trial experience that few attorneys can match. He is routinely recognized by peers and national organizations for his exceptional skill, integrity, and results. His accolades include:

Colorado Super Lawyers – Recognized for 9 years

Top 100 Lawyer – The National Trial Lawyers Professional Organization

AV Preeminent Rated – The highest possible peer and client rating by Martindale-Hubbell for legal ability (A) and ethics (V = “Very High”)

National Association of Distinguished Counsel, Top 1% recognition

Perfect “10.0” AVVO rating from peers and clients

Lifetime Achievement Award by America’s Top 100 Attorneys, 2017

A native of the San Luis Valley, Mr. Vance grew up on a cattle ranch near Manassa, Colorado. He earned his undergraduate degree from Adams State College in 1994 and worked full-time—often as an over-the-road semi-truck driver—to put himself through school. He graduated with honors from the University of Nebraska College of Law in 1997, where he clerked for the Honorable Donald Endacott in Lincoln.

Mr. Vance began his legal career defending negligent drivers and insurance companies at the Colorado Springs firm of Wittman & McCord. There, he learned how the insurance industry evaluates claims and looks at personal injury cases. In 2000, he made a decisive shift: he left defense work to dedicate his career to representing injured individuals—a commitment he has never wavered from.His insight into the “other side” of the case has served him well over the years to understand why the insurance adjusters and attorneys look at cases the way they do.

In 2005, Keith was selected to attend the renowned Trial Lawyers College founded by Gerry Spence, an intensive, invitation-only program for trial lawyers who represent people—not corporations.

Mr. Vance is licensed to practice in Colorado and is an active member of the:

Colorado Trial Lawyers Association

Colorado Bar Association

American Association for Justice (formerly Association of Trial Lawyers of America)

Through a combination of deep legal expertise, hard-earned trial experience, and a steadfast commitment to ethical advocacy, Keith D. Vance has built a reputation as a trusted, authoritative voice in personal injury law—and a relentless champion for the injured.

attorneys.name: David Vandenberg
attorneys.practice_type: Business & Commercial Lawyers in Fort Collins, CO
attorneys.bio:
David was born in Anchorage, Alaska but moved around quite a bit as he was part of a military family. He ultimately ended up in Monument, Colorado where he graduated from Lewis Palmer High School in 1998. He moved to Boulder, Colorado where he attended the University of Colorado and graduated in May 2002. Upon graduating he moved to Washington, D.C. where he completed an internship with a congressional committee. David returned to Colorado where he attended the University of Colorado School of Law from 2003-2006.

While in law school, he was selected to join the University of Colorado Law Review and in his final year was chosen to sit on the Law Review's editorial board. As part of his law review experience he wrote a legal article which was selected for publication by the Law Review in 2006.

David has been a licensed attorney in Colorado since October 2006. In August 2006, David began his legal career in Larimer County as a law clerk for two District Court judges in the 8th Judicial District. As a law clerk he assisted the judges in all practice areas by attending trials, serving as bailiff for jury trials, and drafting legal opinions and orders across all practice areas that were before the Court.

After his clerkship, he was hired as a Deputy District Attorney in August 2007. David conducted his first jury trial less than two weeks after being hired and continuously litigated motions and conducted jury trials for the next 13 years. He has successfully tried dozens of cases on behalf of the People of the State of Colorado ranging all the way from traffic offenses and DUI's up to sexual crimes and homicides. David has also handled criminal appeals and has litigated multiple cases before both the Colorado Court of Appeals and Colorado Supreme Court. In 2013, David was appointed to the Colorado Supreme Court's Criminal Rules Committee and served until December 2020. In his time as a prosecutor, he served as a Chief Deputy District Attorney and later as an Assistant District Attorney

Through his experience, he has observed the impact that involvement in the legal system can have on an individual's life and well-being and specifically understands the importance of having competent, effective, and compassionate legal counsel throughout the entirety of a case. His wealth of experience as a prosecutor gives him a specialized perspective on criminal justice matters in Larimer County and Northern Colorado.

David is a Consilium Practitioner; he is a member of Consilium, an organization dedicated to an integrated and wholistic approach to domestic relations cases

In his free time, he tries to take advantage of the outdoor opportunities Colorado provides including skiing, whitewater rafting, and fly fishing. He has lived in Fort Collins since 2008 and is married with two children and a goldendoodle.

attorneys.name: Bryan S. VanMeveren
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury-- Plaintiff Lawyers in Fort Collins, CO
attorneys.bio:
Bryan S. VanMeveren: From Insurance Defense to Champion for Injury Victims

Bryan VanMeveren isn't your typical attorney. His journey, marked by both legal expertise and extraordinary athletic achievement, uniquely positions him to fight for those injured by negligence. With 31 years of experience, he began his career defending insurance companies, gaining an insider's understanding of their strategies. Now, he uses that knowledge to champion the rights of personal injury victims across Colorado, Wyoming, and Arizona.

His academic foundation—a Bachelor’s degree from the University of Wyoming and a Juris Doctorate from the University of South Dakota—is complemented by a deep commitment to legal ethics and community service. Bryan served on the Colorado Supreme Court's Standing Committee on the Rules of Professional Conduct, helping shape the standards of legal practice. He also contributed to the selection of Larimer County District Court judges through his role on the Eighth Judicial Nominating Commission.

For over 25 years, Bryan has been a pillar of the Larimer County legal community, providing pro bono services, advising on a variety of legal issues, coaching local high school basketball teams, speaking to local civic organizations and high school students and fostering ethical dialogue through the Bench-Bar Committee. He’s also written and published numerous books, articles and blogs to guide injured victims attempting to navigate their personal injury claims. His dedication also extends to numerous local charities, including the Boys & Girls Clubs of Larimer County, where he served as a board member and legal counsel for many years.

Bryan's passion for endurance sports—over 50 marathons and ultra-endurance events, 28 Ironman Triathlons, and a #1 world ranking in his age group in 2019—reflecting his relentless drive and commitment to excellence. This same determination fuels his legal practice, ensuring his clients receive unwavering advocacy and service. His experience and dedication make him a formidable advocate for those seeking justice.

Now, he uses that knowledge to champion the rights of personal injury victims across Colorado, Wyoming, and Arizona.

His academic foundation—a Bachelor’s degree from the University of Wyoming and a Juris Doctorate from the University of South Dakota—is complemented by a deep commitment to legal ethics and community service. Bryan served on the Colorado Supreme Court's Standing Committee on the Rules of Professional Conduct, helping shape the standards of legal practice. He also contributed to the selection of Larimer County District Court judges through his role on the Eighth Judicial Nominating Commission.

For over 25 years, Bryan has been a pillar of the Larimer County legal community, providing pro bono services, advising on a variety of legal issues, coaching local high school basketball teams, speaking to local civic organizations and high school students and fostering ethical dialogue through the Bench-Bar Committee. He’s also written and published numerous books, articles and blogs to guide injured victims attempting to navigate their personal injury claims. His dedication also extends to numerous local charities, including the Boys & Girls Clubs of Larimer County, where he served as a board member and legal counsel for many years.

Bryan's passion for endurance sports—over 50 marathons and ultra-endurance events, 28 Ironman Triathlons, and a #1 world ranking in his age group in 2019—reflecting his relentless drive and commitment to excellence. This same determination fuels his legal practice, ensuring his clients receive unwavering advocacy and service. His experience and dedication make him a formidable advocate for those seeking justice.

attorneys.name: Leah P. VanLandschoot
attorneys.practice_type: Employment Lawyers in Denver, CO
attorneys.bio:
Leah P. VanLandschoot is the founding member of The Litigation Boutique LLC.

Ms. VanLandschoot is licensed to practice law in Colorado and has 20 years of experience handling employment and civil litigation matters in state and federal court, as well as before federal and state administrative agencies. Ms. VanLandschoot represents her clients in connection with charges of discrimination and harassment in violation of the Colorado Anti-Discrimination Act, Title VII, the ADA, ADEA, claims based on the Colorado Wage Claim Act, claims of wrongful discharge in violation of public policy, the Uniform Trade Secrets Act, the Defend Trade Secrets Act, non-compete and non-solicitation litigation, employment contract litigation, and civil and contractual legal and business disputes. Ms. VanLandschoot has successfully litigated matters (for employees and employers) of sexual harassment, sex discrimination, national origin discrimination, race discrimination, disability discrimination, and retaliation in the United States District Court for the District of Colorado. She also spends time counseling clients on non-compete agreements, FMLA issues, FLSA compliance, and employment policies, severance agreements, and hiring practices. In addition, Ms. VanLandschoot handles all matters of business and contract litigation. Ms. VanLandschoot has jury trial experience and has worked with a variety of experts and juror and trial consultants to obtain the best results for her clients.

Prior to forming The Litigation Boutique LLC in 2011, Ms. VanLandschoot worked as an employment and civil litigator at Brownstein Hyatt Farber Schreck, LLP and as a commercial litigator at Rothgerber Johnson & Lyons LLP.

Ms. VanLandschoot earned her undergraduate degree in Art and Business from the College of St. Catherine in St. Paul, Minnesota, and earned her J.D., with highest honors (Order of St. Ives), from the University of Denver Sturm College of Law.

Ms. VanLandschoot was named a Top Lawyer by 5280 Magazine and has been on the Rising Star and Super Lawyers list consecutively, every year from 2010 through 2025 (Rising Star 2010-2014; Super Lawyer 2015-2025).

attorneys.firm_name: Frank Azar Car & Truck Accident Lawyers - Pueblo, Colorado
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Pueblo, CO
attorneys.bio:
"Ethics is knowing the difference between what you have a right to do and what is right to do." - Potter Stewart

Erica Vecchio has been with Franklin D. Azar & Associates, P.C. since July 2007. Her practice is focused primarily on personal injury litigation. She is a native of Colorado having been born and raised in the southern regions of the state. She obtained her bachelor's degree from Colorado State University-Pueblo, graduating with honors, Summa Cum Laude in 2000.

In 2005, Ms. Vecchio attended the University of Wyoming College of Law where she graduated Order of the Barristers, with honors. While in law school, she received high merits by being the winner of Client Counseling, Moot Court and Student Trial Advocacy competitions. She also represented the University of Wyoming in five regional competitions. Ms. Vecchio was named UW's Civil Clinic's Outstanding Student Attorney for 2004-2005. In 2005, she completed the year by becoming licensed to practice law in Colorado.

Prior to joining Frank Azar & Associates, Ms. Vecchio worked as a trial lawyer within the Office of the Colorado State Public Defender. She became experienced in litigating misdemeanor, juvenile and felony cases. She became a member of the Colorado Trial Lawyers Association and is a past President of the Pueblo County Bar Association (PCBA). Since joining the firm, she was named Pueblo County's Outstanding Young Lawyer in 2009 and received the PCBA's Outstanding Pro Bono award in 2013.

Erica is a proud resident of Southern Colorado and loves spending moments with her family. She is married to Brian Ziolkowski, a Sergeant with the Pueblo County Sheriff's Office. They have one daughter, Inez Grace, they enjoy raising and bringing to all the multitude of family activities' Colorado has to offer.

attorneys.name: Jennifer Vedra
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Denver, CO
attorneys.bio:
Jennifer Vedra is a Member at KNM's Denver office. As an experienced litigator, she defends individuals as well as companies large and small. Ms. Vedra also has experience litigating internationally on behalf of clients. Ms. Vedra has represented her clients in a variety of matters including personal injury, products liability, toxic torts, and complex commercial and international disputes. She also has extensive experience in the restaurant and hospitality industries, and she was in-house counsel at a global hotel company prior to joining the firm.

Ms. Vedra has successfully defended clients in state and federal courts across the country and in the United Kingdom. She has obtained full defense verdicts at jury and bench trials in Colorado state courts and had claims dismissed on summary judgment, providing clients significant relief. Ms. Vedra routinely steps into cases after discovery to prepare them for trial or for other pivotal moments in a case to meet the client's needs.

Ms. Vedra obtained her law degree from the University of Denver Sturm College of Law in 2011. During law school, she was an articles editor on the Transportation Law Journal. Ms. Vedra attended university for her undergraduate degree at TCU in Ft. Worth, Texas, where she went to play soccer and was a member of Sigma Kappa Sorority. Between TCU and law school, she worked in avionics at Lockheed Martin Aeronautics Company on the then-developmental F-35 program.

Outside of work, Ms. Vedra enjoys checking out local breweries, playing soccer, running, cycling, and skiing with her husband and two children.

attorneys.name: Shana D. Velez
attorneys.practice_type: Family & Immigration Lawyers in Commerce City, CO
attorneys.bio:
Shana Velez is a dedicated attorney with over 18 years of experience in family and juvenile law, as well as criminal defense. Her journey into law began with a desire to assist individuals who faced challenges navigating the legal system. Raised in Denver, Shana's decision to pursue law school stemmed from her aspiration to support those without access to the opportunities she had encountered.

Understanding Diverse Legal Needs: With a diverse background as the daughter of a first-generation Peruvian immigrant, Shana possesses a profound understanding of the unique legal needs of culturally diverse communities. Her expertise extends to working with mono-lingual Spanish speakers, Native Americans, and others from various backgrounds. She adeptly guides her clients through the complexities of the American legal system, providing invaluable support during emotionally turbulent periods of their lives.

Courtroom Advocacy: Shana demonstrates her legal expertise in the courtroom, where she has refined her skills as a powerful litigator. She has represented clients in various cases, including dissolution of marriage, child custody and support, post-decree modification, domestic violence, and dependency matters. Additionally, Shana has served as a guardian ad litem for children accused of crimes and worked as a public defender, handling cases ranging from simple misdemeanors to serious felonies.

Commitment to Community Empowerment: Recognized for her leadership and involvement in the immigrant community, Shana was selected to participate in the Arizona Bar Leadership Institute. She has also shared her legal expertise with the public through appearances on the radio show "Contacto Total," where she provided live answers to listeners' family and criminal defense legal inquiries.

Educational Foundation & Hobbies: Shana holds a Juris Doctor from the James E. Rogers College of Law at the University of Arizona. She is an active member of the Colorado Bar Association and the American Immigration Lawyer's Association, where she continues to make significant contributions to the legal profession. When Shana is not at work, she enjoys spending time with her two daughters and volunteering.

attorneys.name: Stephen Vertucci
attorneys.firm_name: The Law Office of Stephen Vertucci, LLC
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce & Separation Lawyers in Fort Collins, CO
attorneys.bio:
Born and raised in south suburban Chicago, Illinois, Stephen Vertucci served aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln while on active duty in the U.S. Navy from 1990-1994 during the first Gulf War. Upon being honorably discharged, Stephen enrolled at University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign, earning a Bachelor of Arts in history in 1998.

Stephen’s interests in public speaking and litigation led to his decision to attend Chicago-Kent College of Law, largely due its outstanding reputation for having one of the top trial advocacy programs in the nation. Through this course of study and his internship with the Cook County Illinois Public Defender’s Office, Stephen discovered his passion: advocating for client’s rights in the Courtroom. Stephen earned a Juris Doctor degree from Chicago-Kent in 2001.

While attending Chicago-Kent and after being admitted to the Illinois Bar, Stephen worked for Schiff & Hulbert, a top-rated employment litigation firm. Seeking courtroom experience, he transitioned to family law, working at the law firm of Sullivan, Taylor & Gumina. His experience at STG Divorce Law taught him trial preparedness, client compassion, and to maintain the highest standards of ethical conduct.

In 2004, Stephen sought an opportunity to advance his trial skills. After being admitted to the Arizona Bar, he found this opportunity working as a felony prosecutor for the state of Arizona at the Maricopa County Attorney’s Office. This career move provided invaluable experience litigating jury trials against some of the best criminal defense attorneys in the State of Arizona.

After gaining experience as a felony prosecutor, Stephen partnered with a colleague and friend from law school to establish the law firm of Stewart & Vertucci, a successful family law practice in Phoenix.

In 2007, Stephen moved to Colorado to start a new personal and professional chapter in his life. He was admitted to the Colorado Bar, relocated to Fort Collins, married, and started a family. He elevated himself from Associate to Partner in one of the largest family law firms in Denver prior to making the decision to open his own firm in 2016. The Law Office of Stephen Vertucci, LLC was established to serve the communities of northern Colorado and focuses exclusively on the practice of family law.

Stephen is admitted to practice law in the states of Illinois, Arizona, Colorado and before the United States Supreme Court. Among his professional recognitions, he is proud to be a member of the Colorado Eighth Judicial District Domestic Relations Best Practices Committee.

Richard B. Vincent, Partner, enjoys helping others. His practice emphasizes the legal problems of the elderly and disabled, including legal issues related to establishing and maintaining eligibility for Medicaid and other public benefit programs, trust and estate planning, probate administration, conservatorships and guardianships, disability planning through use of durable powers of attorney and special needs trusts.

Mr. Vincent was born and raised in Battle Creek, Michigan and graduated from the University of Michigan with honors in 1977. In 1983, he received his law degree from the University of Denver College of Law and a Masters Degree in Business Administration from the University of Denver Graduate School of Business. Mr. Vincent was also awarded a Certificate in Gerontology by the University of Denver Graduate School of Social Work in 1996.

Mr. Vincent is certified as an Elder Law Attorney by the National Elder Law Foundation. He is a former staff volunteer for Denver Legal Aid and the Denver County Adult Protection Division and is a member of the National Academy of Elder Law Attorneys ("NAELA"), the Life Care Planning Law Firms Association, and the Colorado and Denver Bar Associations. Mr. Vincent is a past chair of the Colorado Bar Association’s Elder Law Committee, past editor of the Elder Law Section of the Colorado Bar Association Probate and Trust Law Section newsletter and a contributor to The Colorado Handbook of Elder Law. He has been designated by Super Lawyers for the past fourteen years. Richard’s interests include mountain climbing, hiking and international travel.

His practice emphasizes the legal problems of the elderly and disabled, including legal issues related to establishing and maintaining eligibility for Medicaid and other public benefit programs, trust and estate planning, probate administration, conservatorships and guardianships, disability planning through use of durable powers of attorney and special needs trusts.

Mr. Vincent was born and raised in Battle Creek, Michigan and graduated from the University of Michigan with honors in 1977. In 1983, he received his law degree from the University of Denver College of Law and a Masters Degree in Business Administration from the University of Denver Graduate School of Business. Mr. Vincent was also awarded a Certificate in Gerontology by the University of Denver Graduate School of Social Work in 1996.

Mr. Vincent is certified as an Elder Law Attorney by the National Elder Law Foundation. He is a former staff volunteer for Denver Legal Aid and the Denver County Adult Protection Division and is a member of the National Academy of Elder Law Attorneys ("NAELA"), the Life Care Planning Law Firms Association, and the Colorado and Denver Bar Associations. Mr. Vincent is a past chair of the Colorado Bar Association’s Elder Law Committee, past editor of the Elder Law Section of the Colorado Bar Association Probate and Trust Law Section newsletter and a contributor to The Colorado Handbook of Elder Law. He has been designated by Super Lawyers for the past fourteen years. Richard’s interests include mountain climbing, hiking and international travel.

attorneys.name: Steven M. Visioli
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Denver, CO
attorneys.bio:
Steven M. Visioli is Senior Litigation Counsel at GEM Family Law, specializing in divorce, complex asset division, child custody, support enforcement, and other family law issues. Steven is an exceptionally talented trial attorney who is sought out for his skill in the courtroom. He has been recognized as a Top 50 Young Professional by ColoradoBiz Magazine and as the “People’s Choice” Best Family Law Lawyer by Barrister’s Best, among other distinctions.

Prior to joining GEM Family Law as Senior Litigation Counsel, Steven managed his own legal practice, Visioli Legal, which was preceded by his partnership at another Denver-based family law firm. Steven’s clients benefit from his extensive experience, creative outlook, and broad network of legal resources.

Steven attended The University of Denver Sturm College of Law, where he focused on experiential courses designed to prepare him for skillful and efficient law practice. He was a competing member of the school's highly-ranked National Trial Team, was Co-President of the Student Trial Lawyers Association, and was an Editor on the Criminal Law Review.

During law school, Steven was a clerk for The Honorable Judge Michael Spear in Colorado's 18th Judicial District, on an entirely domestic relations docket, where he gained unique insight into the court's perspective on domestic matters, to include what strategies are – and are not – effective in persuading a judicial officer. Following his clerkship on the domestic relations docket, Steven began interning with a family law firm, commencing his law practice with a focus on complex divorce and child custody issues from the outset.

Prior to law school, Steven earned a bachelor’s degree in political science from the University of Colorado at Boulder, where he worked at Colorado Legal Services, assisting attorneys in the representation of Coloradoans who could not afford counsel. There, he developed a deep commitment to service; the following year, he worked at the Boulder County District Attorney’s Office, assisting district attorneys and court magistrates on misdemeanor issues. The most important aspect of these positions, for Steven, was the opportunity to spend countless hours with experienced trial lawyers and judges - observing, learning, and becoming comfortable and confident in the courtroom. Steven’s legal writing is additionally outstanding, having been honed since college by senior attorneys and judicial officers.

Steven was raised in small-town Colorado and worked his way through school. His talent and skill is matched only by his compassion and deep drive to serve his clients.

attorneys.name: Anthony J. Viorst
attorneys.practice_type: Medical Malpractice Lawyers in Greenwood Village, CO
attorneys.bio:
Anthony Viorst graduated Phi Beta Kappa from George Washington University and went on to receive his juris doctorate from Georgetown University in 1987, where he also served as editor for the Georgetown Law Journal. He has written numerous scholarly legal articles, on a variety of subjects, including medical malpractice, legal malpractice, and appellate law. Mr. Viorst has been named a Colorado Superlawyer every year for the past 15 years.

Mr. Viorst spent 10 years in the Colorado Public Defenders Office, where he tried over 100 cases, from DUI to murder. Since 2000, Mr. Viorst has also been practicing in the fields of personal injury, medical malpractice, legal malpractice, police brutality, and civil/criminal appeals.

Mr. Viorst's medical malpractice case, Preston v. Dupont, 35 P.3d 433 (Colo. 2001), was named the case of the year by the Colorado Trial Lawyers Association. More recently, Mr. Viorst wrote a comprehensive summary of Colorado legal-malpractice law for the Colorado Bar Association's Colorado Lawyer publication.

Mr. Viorst is licensed to practice in the Colorado state and federal courts, as well as the U.S. Supreme Court. He has the highest rating from his peers as independently reported to Martindale Hubbell.

Ms. Vultaggio found her passion for Elder Law while working in retirement communities for nearly a decade during college and law school. She understands the importance of planning and helps create directions for families to have better control over their future. attorneys.bio:
Mary is a Senior Associate Attorney at GEM Family Law, practicing in all areas of family law. Mary is passionate about advocating for her clients and helping them minimize the stress that often comes with navigating a family law matter.

Mary received her Juris Doctor from the University of Colorado Law School, graduating at the top of her class and earning membership in the Order of the Coif, a distinction earned only by the top 10 percent of law school graduates.

During law school, Mary sought out opportunities to build experience in family law. She worked as a Student Attorney in the University of Colorado Juvenile and Family Law Clinic, representing clients in divorce, dependency and neglect, and juvenile delinquency cases. Mary also completed internships with Metro Volunteer Lawyers, a Denver family law firm, and the 20th Judicial District. After graduation, Mary worked as an Associate Attorney for a Denver family law firm before joining GEM.

An avid writer, Mary earned her Bachelor of the Arts degree in English, with a minor in Business Administration, at Creighton University, and graduated summa cum laude. While pursuing her undergraduate degree, Mary was awarded the Creighton University Undergraduate Scholarly Writing Award and the O'Toole Award for Creative Non-fiction Writing. Mary employs her persuasive writing skills to advocate for her clients.

Mary has experience representing clients in highly contested cases involving divorce, child custody, and protection orders. Mary is passionate about helping her clients work through the myriad issues that arise in family law matters, and she is dedicated to providing a compassionate and personalized experience for each of her clients.

attorneys.name: Jason Wareham
attorneys.firm_name: Allen Vellone Wolf Helfrich & Factor P.C.
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Denver, CO
attorneys.bio:
Jason Wareham is a trial and appellate lawyer who has tried dozens of state, federal, and military courts and administrative hearing cases. Many of his cases were litigated under the highest stakes, including some of this country's most highly classified capital cases. No matter the complexity of the issue, Jason commits himself to a client-centered solution where trial success is the default focus. Whatever the forum or the stage of litigation, Jason has the breadth of understanding and skill to advise and navigate any civil, administrative, national security, military court-martial, or criminal matter when the stakes are the highest.

Jason joined AVWHF after establishing a successful practice in Colorado in 2021 following a successful career as a U.S. Marine Corps Judge Advocate where he held the distinction of being one of the longest continuously serving trial and appellate litigators - litigating some of the highest profile and most complex criminal and national security cases available. Jason has been recognized in that field as a "genius-level attorney and litigator" by one of the most experienced practitioners in that field for more than thirty-five years - even a presiding trial judge himself. During his Marine Corps career, Jason litigated at every level and forum available in the military system. From trial to appellate, administrative to collateral federal attacks, Jason earned the special Marine Corps designation of Master of Criminal Law. Beyond only military criminal work, Jason has also practiced globally throughout Europe and the Middle East conducting investigations and even advising on frontline law of war and engagement issues in active combat.

In addition to litigation, Jason has obtained a specialized Masters of Law (LL.M.) degree in the exploding world of digital evidence, electronic discovery, cybercrime, and cybersecurity litigation. He is routinely sought out by military and civilian litigators throughout the country to consult on matters pertaining to the digital world of litigation as well as national security issues. He maintains an active Top Secret/Sensitive Compartmented Information and completed his military affiliation in the Marine Corps Reserves as a Lieutenant Colonel.

Jason's practice at AVWHF focuses on civilian state and federal criminal defense, military administrative and court-marital defense, firearms law, national security and security clearance defense, civil rights and government litigation, FOIA and Privacy Act litigation, as well as domestic relations and civil litigation matters. Despite his broad legal practice in complex trial and appellate matters, Jason recognizes that every case, big and small, is of vital importance to the individual clients. Regardless of the size of the matter, Jason is committed to bring his wealth of knowledge to successfully resolve the issues for every one of his clients no matter what the case requires.

Jason's matters have been previously covered in The Washington Post, The New York Times and The Washington Examiner.

1Prior Representations:

Defended Major Jason Brezler, USMC, a Marine reservist and New York Firefighter, for over two years of litigation before an administrative rehearing seeking his removal from the service. Jason successfully won a unanimous vote in favor of Major Brezler's retention in the service following the presentation of new digital forensic evidence previously ignored and new evidence of unlawful retaliation by officers at the highest levels of the Marine Corps.

Managed the litigation branch of the capital defense team defending Ammar al Baluchi before the death penalty prosecution of those accused of planning the 9/11 attacks successfully analyzing troves of digital evidence and discovery produced over decades by the U.S. Government's highest and most obscure agencies.

Led the capital defense team defending Abd al-Rahim al-Nashiri accused of allegedly planning the 2000 USS Cole attack following a crisis resulting in the excusal of his learned counsel and civilian attorneys successfully initiating litigation simultaneously at the trial and appellate levels resulting in recusal of the judge and dismissal of two years of tainted rulings.
